title: With his next catch, Justin Jefferson will pass Randy Moss on Vikings' all-time list
summary: With eight catches for 92 yards, two touchdowns, and a two-point conversion in a nutty Week 1 win over the Packers, Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson has 587 career receptions.
full_text: With eight catches for 92 yards, two touchdowns, and a two-point conversion in a nutty Week 1 win over the Packers, Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson has 587 career receptions. His next one will be a significant one. Via NBC Sports research, Jefferson is tied with Randy Moss on the franchise's all-time catch list. Jefferson's 588th will put him all alone in second place. He still has a long way to go to set the Vikings' record. Cris Carter holds it, with 1,004 receptions. Jefferson needs another 418 to break Carter's mark. Jefferson is young enough and good enough to get there. The question is whether, unlike Moss, Jefferson remains in Minnesota long enough to do it. The more important objective for Jefferson and the Vikings on Sunday will be to extend a streak of six straight wins in Chicago. The Vikings are also 8-2 against the Bears since 2021. And while these Bears seem to be very different than Bears teams of the recent past (as evidenced by the 59 points scored in Week 1 at Carolina), it's going to be a rainy day in the Windy City, which could take some steam out of both offenses.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears open latest home slate at Soldier Field; how many more will there be?
summary: Illinois remains viable — and Chicago could still keep the team.
full_text: '' The Bears are where we thought they were. How much longer will they be there? On Sunday, the Bears begin their latest home slate at Soldier Field, the stadium into which they moved permanently in 1971. (In 2002, they spent a year at the University of Illinois as the building was being renovated.) They're actively trying to move out. And the uncertainty as to where, and when, they'll have a new home continues. Indiana is ready to go. But the Bears are still trying to parlay a potential Hammond home into an Illinois alternative. As recently reported by Brenden Moore of Capitol News Illinois , via Sports Business Journal , the Bears executive leading the stadium effort met with Illinois Deputy Governor Andy Manar in August. Bears executive V.P. of stadium development and COO Karen Murphy was joined by minority owner Pat Ryan for the meeting with Manar. Meanwhile, Axios has reported that Chicago mayoral candidate Willie Wilson has been pushing for a new domed stadium in Chicago . The Bears have been pushing property they own in Arlington Heights as the preferred Illinois location. These developments do nothing to change the perception that Indiana's pipe dream is leverage for a new stadium in Illinois. If anything, they reinforce the idea that the Bears are simply posturing when they claim to be focused on Hammond. The involvement of Ryan is also significant. With team president and CEO Kevin Warren's strategies not yielding a solution, Ryan and his son, Pat Ryan Jr., could be trying to influence the stalled stadium pursuit.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Eagles to move Cam Jurgens to guard, Drew Kendall to start at center
summary: Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said this week that the team would keep any plans for replacing left guard Landon Dickerson in-house, including whether moving center Cam Jurgens to the spot was a consideration.
full_text: Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said this week that the team would keep any plans for replacing left guard Landon Dickerson in-house, including whether moving center Cam Jurgens to the spot was a consideration. It appears that the Eagles have settled on doing just that. Cameron Wolfe of NFL Media reported on Sunday morning that the Eagles will be moving Jurgens to guard with Drew Kendall taking over at center against the Titans. Kendall played center at Boston College and was a 2025 fifth-round pick in Philadelphia. He started in Week 18 last year when the Eagles rested their starters ahead of the postseason. Jurgens broke into the Eagles' lineup as a guard, but moved to center in 2024 after Jason Kelce's retirement.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sam Darnold is "recovering faster than anyone had anticipated"
summary: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold left the Week 1 game against the Patriots after five snaps, with a hip injury becoming a glute tendon injury for which the team reportedly sought multiple second opinions.
full_text: '' Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold left the Week 1 game against the Patriots after five snaps, with a hip injury becoming a glute tendon injury for which the team reportedly sought multiple second opinions. Amid initial concerns that Darnold could miss 4-6 weeks, he could be back three weeks after the injury happened. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports that Darnold is "recovering faster than anyone had anticipated," and that he could return to practice "in some form or fashion" this week. That doesn't mean he'll be ready to go against the Commanders in Week 3. He could be back in Week 4 vs. the Chargers. A significant game is looming in Week 5. That's when the 49ers, who beat the Seahawks in Seattle last season, return to town for what will be a potentially massive NFC West showdown. Today against the Cardinals, it's Drew Lock. The Seahawks have beaten Arizona nine straight times, tying the longest active streak by any franchise against another team. Via NBC Sports research, the Chiefs have also beaten the Commanders nine straight times. More importantly, the Seahawks have now won 11 in a row. That equals the longest streak in franchise history. Which means, obviously, that a win today would give Seattle its first-ever 12-game win streak.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Michael Penix Jr. could debut for Falcons on Thursday night
summary: The Falcons have been waiting.
full_text: The Falcons have been waiting. And waiting. And waiting. The waiting may be over. ESPN reports that quarterback Michael Penix Jr. "is nearing a return" and "could" make his 2026 debut on Thursday night, when the Falcons travel to Lambeau Field for a Week 3 contest. During NFL Network's GameDay morning, Steve Wyche reported that Falcons president of football Matt Ryan said Penix is "getting close," but he declined to put a timetable on his return. The team has had some muted frustrations about Penix's unwillingness to play. But he's not yet comfortable exposing his surgically repaired left knee to contact. Without Penix, and with Tua Tagovailoa out due to an oblique injury, Cooper Rush started in Week 1, and he'll start in Week 2. Through two seasons, Penix has 14 regular-season appearances and 12 starts, with four wins. After starting last season 3-2, Penix has lost four straight starts. For now, the Falcons and Rush will face the Panthers, who won the division on the final Sunday of the 2025 season when Kirk Cousins led Atlanta to a win over the Saints.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos are expected to be without RJ Harvey on Sunday
summary: The Broncos are on track to be without one of their running backs for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
full_text: '' The Broncos are on track to be without one of their running backs for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that RJ Harvey is not expected to play in Week 2. Harvey missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury and was listed as questionable after a pair of limited practices to close out the week. Harvey had three carries for 18 yards and four catches for 23 yards in Denver's Week 1 loss to the Chiefs. J.K. Dobbins is the top back for the Broncos with rookie Jonah Coleman and Tyler Badie set to move up the depth chart in Harvey's absence.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Joey Porter Jr. considering second opinion on back injury
summary: Porter will miss his second straight game on Sunday.
full_text: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will miss his second straight game on Sunday and his outlook for Week 3 remains uncertain as well. The plan was for Porter to ramp up his workload this week, but he had to leave practice early on Thursday after his back flared up and he was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots. Porter is also working on his conditioning after spending all of training camp on the physically unable to perform list. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Steelers are targeting Week 3's game against the Bengals for his 2026 debut, but that Porter is considering a second opinion on his back. All of this is playing out against the backdrop of Porter's desire for a new contract that the Steelers aren't expected to discuss given their longstanding policy of not negotiating during the season. That impasse has led to speculation about a trade, although nothing appears imminent with Week 2 about to get underway. Should Porter remain out as the trade deadline draws closer, things could change on that front.
author: Josh Alper

title: Trey Hendrickson, Chris Olave, Chase Young are expected to play in Ravens-Saints
summary: The Ravens will be without wide receiver Zay Flowers for Sunday's game against the Saints, but they are set to have linebacker Trey Hendrickson in the lineup.
full_text: '' The Ravens will be without wide receiver Zay Flowers for Sunday's game against the Saints, but they are set to have linebacker Trey Hendrickson in the lineup. Hendrickson was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report of the week after returning to practice on Friday. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Hendrickson is expected to play while wearing a cast to protect his injured finger. Flowers is out with a hamstring injury and the Saints' top wideout Chris Olave has also been dealing with a hamstring issue this week. Olave traveled with the team to Baltimore and Rapoport reports that Olave is set to play on Sunday. Saints defensive end Chase Young, who has a calf injury, is also expected to play.
author: Josh Alper

title: Trinidad Chambliss shows NFL talent in leading Ole Miss to win over LSU
summary: Once a zero-star prospect, Chambliss is currently sixth in the betting odds to go first overall in the 2027 NFL draft.
full_text: '' Trinidad Chambliss was not supposed to be an NFL prospect. He's small, he was a zero-star recruit coming out of high school, and he started his college football career at Division II Ferris State. Even when he transferred to Ole Miss last year, he was expected to be a backup. But after Chambliss led Ole Miss to a 32-24 win over LSU on Saturday in one of this college football season's biggest games, there can be no doubt that Chambliss will be playing on Sundays next year. Chambliss completed 33 of 48 passes for 363 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception, and scored the game-winning touchdown on a 14-yard run in beating No. 7 LSU and Chambliss' former coach, Lane Kiffin. Since becoming the starter at Ole Miss in the third game of last season, Chambliss has been nothing short of sensational. Last year he was named the SEC Newcomer of the Year, and at the moment he's the Heisman Trophy favorite. He's also on the short list of favorites to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. Chambliss' odds to go first overall are currently at +1500, putting him sixth behind Texas quarterback Arch Manning, Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, Notre Dame quarterback C.J. Carr, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. There will still be some doubts about Chambliss: He's listed at 6-foot-1 and might not even be that tall. He plays an improvisational style while many NFL teams still prefer prototypical pocket passers. He's 24 years old and in his sixth year of college football, so some scouts will think he has less upside than younger prospects. But it's impossible to watch what Chambliss did on Saturday night and doubt he belongs in the NFL.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deion Sanders, Colorado get thumped by Northwestern, 41-7
summary: Like Bill Belichick, Deion Sanders had led his college team to a somewhat unexpected 2-0 start in 2026.
full_text: Like Bill Belichick, Deion Sanders had led his college team to a somewhat unexpected 2-0 start in 2026. Like Belichick, the run ended for Sanders in Week 3. Sanders and Colorado were thumped by Northwestern, 41-7 , on Saturday night in Evanston, Illinois. Before the game, Colorado's players were heard complaining about Northwestern's current venue — Northwestern Medicine Field at Martin Stadium. " This place fucking sucks ," one of them said. "Shit sounds like a fucking library." Then the game started, and Deion's team got Dewey Decimal System'd. After the game, Sanders called the outcome a " flat-out butt kicking ." He attributed the loss primarily to turnovers and penalties. Colorado is now 2-1. The nine-game Big 12 schedule starts next week, with a visit to Baylor.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL is aware of potential issues with field in Brazil for Ravens-Cowboys
summary: The clock is ticking for the Week 3 game.
full_text: '' Yes, there are concerns about the quality of the field at Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the Ravens and Cowboys are due to play next Sunday. And the NFL is aware of the situation. From rain to a significant number of soccer matches (with one more happening on Sunday), there are potential problems. The NFL is taking steps, we're told, to ensure that the field will be ready to host the game in only eight days. The clock is ticking. After Sunday's soccer game, the league will need to decide fairly quickly whether the field will be suitable for the Week 3 contest. If there's a chance it won't be, the only prudent thing to do would be to move it. With the Cowboys serving as the home team for the game, the obvious alternative would be to move the game to Dallas. A quick decision will need to be made. The overriding question is whether the NFL's international obsession will tip the scales toward rolling the dice on proceeding. Regardless of the enhanced physical risk that a substandard field may present to the players. Eight years ago, the NFL scrapped a Chiefs-Rams game set for Mexico City and moved it to L.A., due to issues with the field.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bengals elevate Josh Johnson to active roster with Joe Burrow questionable
summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow says he plans to play tomorrow against the Texans.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow says he plans to play tomorrow against the Texans. But just in case, the Bengals have added another quarterback to the active roster. The Bengals today elevated quarterback Josh Johnson from the practice squad to the active roster. The plan is for Burrow to start, Joe Flacco to back him up and Johnson to be available as the No. 3 quarterback. That the Bengals elevated Johnson suggests they're at least a little concerned that Burrow's back injury will sideline him on Sunday. Officially, Burrow is listed as questionable. The 40-year-old Johnson signed with the Bengals in March and didn't make their 53-man roster but was re-signed to the practice squad after he was released. Johnson is perhaps the most well-traveled player in the history of professional football, having signed about two dozen pro contracts in the NFL and other leagues. He has shown an ability to learn offenses quickly and play adequately when called upon, but the Bengals hope they won't need him. The Bengals also called up linebacker Joe Giles-Harris from the practice squad to the active roster.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bill Belichick and North Carolina blow big lead, lose 28-20 at Clemson
summary: Bill Belichick appeared to be on the verge of his biggest win as North Carolina's head coach today at Clemson, but his team fell apart late in a 28-20 loss.
full_text: '' Bill Belichick appeared to be on the verge of his biggest win as North Carolina's head coach today at Clemson, but his team fell apart late in a 28-20 loss. North Carolina jumped out to a 17-3 lead in the second quarter and was in control for most of the game, but Clemson came back by marching down the field on scoring drives of 88 yards, 92 yards, 68 yards and 44 yards against Belichick's defense. That defense was supposed to be coordinated by Belichick's son, Steve Belichick, but he resigned this week amid an investigation into unspecified misconduct. Belichick's other son, Brian Belichick, is now calling the defense. Belichick will be questioned especially for a fourth-and-1 play call with two minutes left in the fourth quarter, with North Carolina trailing 21-20. Instead of the running play most coaches would have called, North Carolina went with a play-action deep pass, which fell incomplete, turning the ball over on downs. From there, Clemson went downfield and scored its final touchdown, on a play when the Tigers could have just taken a knee and run out the clock. The loss drops North Carolina's record to 2-1 and represents a major disappointment for a North Carolina squad that appeared to be making strides in its second year with Belichick at the helm. Last year Belichick went 4-8 in his first year as a college football head coach, and he needs to show progress in Year 2. Instead, his team has suffered its first loss of the season, and the schedule doesn't get any easier: North Carolina's next game is against No. 3 Notre Dame.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL issues three fines for player safety fouls that count toward possible suspensions
summary: The first week of the 2026 season featured three fouls that will count toward possible suspensions.
full_text: The first week of the 2026 season featured three fouls that will count toward possible suspensions. Bills defensive back Sam Franklin was fined $9,425 for a blindside block, Packers defensive back Evan Williams was fined $7,087 for a hit on a defenseless player, and Dolphins cornerback Chris Johnson was fined $17,911 for a hip-drop tackle. Under a new rule adopted for this year, players who pick up three fouls for five specific player safety rules will be suspended. The three fouls above all qualify under the rule as well as fouls for horse-collar tackles and launching. The suspension would come into effect for three violations of the same rule. Players can appeal the fines and any player that ends the season with one violation of a rule will get 50 percent of the fine paid back to them.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL will no longer allow Patriots to use video board to confuse opposing kickers
summary: The Patriots' longstanding tactic of creating an optical illusion for the road team's kicker has been banned.
full_text: The Patriots have long used their video board to confuse opposing kickers, displaying video of the goal posts behind the actual goal posts, in a way that created an optical illusion for kickers. The Patriots only displayed the video when the opponent's kicker was lining up for a field goal, and not when their own kicker was on the field. That tactic had always been legal . Now it's not. The NFL has informed all teams that their video board display on field goal attempts has to be the same for the home team and the road team , according to ESPN. Teams can display either a live All-22 angle of the field goal or a static image during field goal attempts, but whatever they choose has to be the same for both teams throughout the game. A memo sent to all 32 teams on September 7 said teams that don't comply will face league discipline. The Patriots’ tactic was exposed by former NFL analytics staffer Ryan Paganetti, who posted on social media a series of images showing how the Patriots' video display at Gillette Stadium was used to confuse opposing kickers. Paganetti said he first noticed it when he worked for the Eagles, and that the Eagles considered doing it, too, but the location of the video boards at Lincoln Financial Field wouldn't have worked to create the same optical illusion that the Gillette Stadium video boards created. Now, it won't be allowed at any stadium.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lukas Van Ness fined for hit on Carson Wentz, no fine for hit on Kyler Murray
summary: Packers linebacker Lukas Van Ness was involved in the Week 1 play that ended with Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray suffering a concussion, but the only fine for a hit on a quarterback from that game stemmed from a different play.
full_text: Packers linebacker Lukas Van Ness was involved in the Week 1 play that ended with Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray suffering a concussion, but the only fine for a hit on a quarterback from that game stemmed from a different play. The NFL announced that Van Ness was fined $17,911 for a hit to the head of Carson Wentz, who replaced Murray in the first quarter. Van Ness was not flagged for the contact he made to Wentz's head while the quarterback was delivering a pass in the third quarter of the game. Van Ness made contact with Murray's head as the Vikings quarterback made his way down at the end of a run, but Packers defensive back Javon Bullard was penalized for delivering a bigger blow to Murray on the play. Van Ness also wound up in concussion protocol this week, but he cleared it on Saturday and is in line to play against the Jets this Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Deonte Banks, Micah McFadden questionable for Monday vs. Rams
summary: The Giants have two players with game statuses for Monday night's game against the Rams.
full_text: '' The Giants have two players with game statuses for Monday night's game against the Rams. Cornerback Deonte Banks (calf) and linebacker Micah McFadden (neck) as questionable for the contest. Banks was a limited participant on Thursday but did not practice on Friday or Saturday. He registered four tackles and two passes defensed in the season-opening win over the Cowboys. McFadden has been limited in practice all week. While offensive tackle Andre Thomas (ankle) has been limited all week, he does not have a game status and is set to play. Cornerback Greg Newsome (rib), defensive lineman Chauncey Golston (neck), and offensive lineman Sisi Mauigoa (shoulder) were all upgraded from limited to full on Saturday and are set to play.
author: Myles Simmons

title: 49ers TE Jake Tonges fined for leg whip on same play he tore his MCL
summary: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges's final play of the 2026 season was a painful one in more ways than one.
full_text: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges's final play of the 2026 season was a painful one in more ways than one. The NFL announced that Tonges was fined $9,266 for unnecessary roughness in last week's win over the Rams. The fine was for an unpenalized leg whip block on Rams defensive end Myles Garrett in the second quarter. Tonges remained down after the play and did not return. Head coach Kyle Shanahan announced this week that he suffered a torn MCL that required season-ending surgery. 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk was also fined $20,033 for lowering his helmet to initiate contact.
author: Josh Alper

title: Stefon Diggs fined for jumping on goalpost after Week 1 TD
summary: Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs punctuated his first touchdown as a member of the team with a celebration that hurt Washington on the field and hurt Diggs in the wallet.
full_text: Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs punctuated his first touchdown as a member of the team with a celebration that hurt Washington on the field and hurt Diggs in the wallet. Diggs jumped on the goalpost and wrapped his arms and legs around it, which drew a penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct during the game. The NFL announced on Saturday that Diggs has also been fined $14,926 for the infraction. The score put the Commanders within two points, but the penalty pushed them back 15 yards and forced a kick rather than a conversion try. The Commanders ultimately lost 24-22 when another two-point try failed with a minute to play in the game. Diggs had four catches for 55 yards in his Commanders debut and he'll try for his first win in the uniform in Dallas on Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ravens downgrade Zay Flowers to out for Sunday vs. Saints
summary: While Zay Flowers was able to get back on the practice field on Friday, he won’t be playing on Sunday against the Saints.
full_text: '' While Zay Flowers was able to get back on the practice field on Friday, he won’t be playing on Sunday against the Saints. Baltimore has officially downgraded Flowers from doubtful to out. Flowers caught five passes for 150 yards with a touchdown in Baltimore’s 41-23 victory over Indianapolis last weekend before exiting the contest. Additionally, the Ravens have placed cornerback T.J. Tampa on injured reserve with a knee injury. Linebacker Carl Jones has been signed to the 53-man roster from the club’s practice squad as a corresponding move. Offensive tackle Gerad Lichtenhan has been elected from the practice squad to the gameday roster.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Raiders elevate TE Chris Myarick with Brock Bowers listed as doubtful
summary: The Raiders didn't officially rule Brock Bowers out on Friday, but signs point to the tight end missing his second straight game on Sunday,.
full_text: '' The Raiders didn't officially rule Brock Bowers out on Friday, but signs point to the tight end missing his second straight game on Sunday,. Bowers practiced on Friday for the first time since having meniscus surgery, but was listed as doubtful to play against the Chargers. The Raiders added a tight end to the roster on Saturday to bolster their depth at the position. Chris Myarick was elevated from the practice squad. Myarick also played last Sunday and saw action on offense and special teams. Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas are the other Raiders tight ends. The Raiders also elevated wide receiver Cody White for Sunday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys elevate linebackers Justin Barron, Curtis Robinson from practice squad
summary: The Cowboys added a pair of linebackers to their roster for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
full_text: The Cowboys added a pair of linebackers to their roster for Sunday's game against the Commanders. Justin Barron and Curtis Robinson were both elevated from the practice squad on Saturday. The two players will revert back after the game. The moves come after the Cowboys ruled DeMarvion Overshown out for this week because of a hamstring injury. Rookie Jaishawn Barham is set to start in his place on Sunday, which means he'll also be wearing the green dot to receive play calls from coaches. Barron appeared on special teams in two games for the Cowboys last season. Robinson appeared in 14 games and made three starts for the 49ers last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Puka Nacua won't practice Saturday, questionable for Monday vs. Giants
summary: The Rams are already without one of their top defensive players for the next four weeks.
full_text: The Rams are already without one of their top defensive players for the next four weeks. Now, they may be without one of their key offensive players, too. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters in his Saturday press conference that receiver Puka Nacua will not practice on Saturday and will be listed as questionable for Monday night’s matchup against the Giants. While Nacua was listed with a hip issue on the injury report, McVay noted the wideout has an issue elsewhere. “He’s got a little bit of soreness in that groin, being smart with him as a skill player ,” McVay said Saturday, via Gary Klein of the L.A. Times . “Whether or not he plays is to be determined, and so we’ll see how he’s feeling.” While Nacua dealt with a psoas injury during the preseason, McVay said this is “a different thing.” Nacua was able to practice on Thursday and, according to McVay, “felt good but didn’t feel totally like himself, his ability to be able to kind of open up and really hit full speed.” Nacua caught five passes for 74 yards in the Rams’ season-opening loss to the 49ers in Australia. Also on the injury report, Jordan Whittington is doubtful for Monday night with a quad injury and safety Kam Kinchens is out with a hamstring injury.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Chris Olave, Chase Young traveled to Baltimore with the Saints
summary: The Saints listed wide receiver Chris Olave as questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Ravens, so their move to elevate another wideout from the practice squad on Saturday could signal Olave will not play in Baltimore.
full_text: '' The Saints listed wide receiver Chris Olave as questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Ravens, so their move to elevate another wideout from the practice squad on Saturday could signal Olave will not play in Baltimore. The clearest signal about his outlook would have been if Olave stayed in New Orleans, but that did not happen. Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports that Olave made the trip with the team on Saturday. Underhill reports that defensive end Chase Young also traveled with the team. Olave hurt his hamstring during the week and Young, who is also questionable, is dealing with a calf injury. The Saints elevated wide receiver Kevin Austin, who was also brought up to play in their Week 1 loss to the Lions. Long snapper Scott Daly was called up for Sunday's game as well.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dak Prescott looks to continue his home mastery of the NFC East
summary: The Cowboys are better at home than they are on the road.
full_text: The Cowboys are better at home than they are on the road. Especially when an NFC East team is visiting Dallas. Quarterback Dak Prescott has a record of 22-2 in division games played at home. Via NBC Sports research, it's the best winning percentage at home against division opponents (91.7 percent), with a minimum of 15 starts, since the merger. Prescott also has won 19 home games against NFC East teams in a row since 2017. He's one game away from tying Tom Brady's record of 20 straight home division wins since the merger, at 20. For Washington, quarterback Jayden Daniels has lost five straight starts. A loss would tie him for the second-longest losing streak for a Washington quarterback since the merger. Robert Griffin III and Joe Theismann lost six in a row. In 2023, Sam Howell lost eight in a row. It won't be easy for Daniels. Prescott has had a high level of success against Washington, overall. He's 13-2 against them, with 32 touchdown passes and five interceptions. At home against Washington, Prescott is 7-0 with 20 touchdown passes and zero interceptions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike McCarthy looks to become fourth Steelers coach to start 2-0
summary: Last Sunday, coach Mike McCarthy won in his Pittsburgh debut.
full_text: Last Sunday, coach Mike McCarthy won in his Pittsburgh debut. (The 20-13 game easily could have gone the other way.) With a win at New England on Sunday, McCarthy will be the fourth coach in Steelers history to start his tenure with the team at 2-0. Via NBC Sports research, the others were Mike Tomlin in 2007, Bill Cowher in 1992, and Johnny Blood in 1937, when the team was known as the Pirates. On the flip side, the Patriots hope to avoid starting 0-2 for the second time in 20 seasons. It last happened in 2023, to start Bill Belichick's final run in New England. A loss would make the Patriots the fifth Super Bowl participant since 2000 to start 0-2 the next year. It also happened to the 2025 Chiefs, the 2022 Bengals, the 2015 Seahawks, and the 2022 Rams. (Both the 2022 Bengals and 2015 Seahawks recovered to make the playoffs.) Is it a "must" win for New England? With trips to Jacksonville and Buffalo on deck, it very well could be.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers downgrade DT Javon Hargrave to out, remove DE Lukas Van Ness from injury report
summary: When the Packers face the Jets on Sunday, they won't have defensive tackle Javon Hargrave.
full_text: When the Packers face the Jets on Sunday, they won't have defensive tackle Javon Hargrave. The veteran lineman was downgraded from questionable to out on Saturday afternoon, as the Packers prepared to make the trip to New Jersey. Hargrave has both a knee injury and a concussion. He was limited in practice on Wednesday, and he did not practice on Thursday or Friday. The defensive starter participated in 30 snaps during the Week 1 loss at Minnesota. Hargrave joined the Packers in free agency, after playing for the Vikings in 2025. A third-round pick of the Steelers in 2016, he has also played for the Eagles and 49ers. The Packers also removed defensive end Lukas Van Ness from the injury report, after he cleared the concussion protocol. He had been limited in practice all week, and he was listed as questionable on Friday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Concerns arise regarding Brazil field where Ravens-Cowboys will be played
summary: In 2018, the NFL moved a game from Mexico to the U.S. Could it happen again?
full_text: '' Next Sunday, the Ravens and Cowboys will play in Rio de Janeiro, at Maracaña Stadium. And there are reportedly concerns about the grass there. Via Mauricio Rodriguez of AtoZSports.com, complaints about the quality of the field are coming from soccer players who have played there in recent days. “You don’t even need to talk about the field, it’s there for everyone to see ,” Flamengo goalkeeper Agustín Rossi said, per Rodriguez. “The way we play, it’s unbelievable that we’re playing on a field like this. Both penalty areas are bad as [expletive]. If you look at it, there are bumps everywhere. There’s still going to be an NFL game here during the international break. After that game, I hope the field is in better shape.” “We’ve been struggling a lot in these last few games, and the field keeps getting worse,” Flamengo midfielder Giorgian De Arrascaeta said. “It’s getting harder and harder to control the ball. We have to try to play quickly. If we want to be champions, we have to find a solution. With the team we have, we can’t be playing on a field like this.” Here are the highlights from the latest game played there. It definitely looks rough. One more soccer game is scheduled for Sunday, before preparations commence to host Ravens-Cowboys. In 2018, a Chiefs-Rams game that had been scheduled for Mexico City was moved to the L.A. Coliseum six days before the Monday night kickoff due to issues with the field. Ravens-Cowboys is only eight days away; the league will need to make a quick assessment of the field after Sunday's soccer game — and possibly make a decision that could lead to another game next weekend at Jerry World.
author: Mike Florio

title: Peter King expresses concern about changes to Hall of Fame voting panel
summary: Our good friend and former colleague, Peter King, spent 32 years on the Pro Football Hall of Fame's selection committee.
full_text: Our good friend and former colleague, Peter King, spent 32 years on the Pro Football Hall of Fame's selection committee. He has concerns about the recent decision to slash the panel from 50 to 28. The reductions came with no explanation as to shrinking the number of voters or as to the voters who were kept and those who were removed. There's no reason that fewer voters will make the process any better. King believes that one specific move will make it worse. "That Rick Gosselin, the most conscientious and well-researched member of the [Hall of Fame] selection committee I saw in my 32 years as a voter, has been removed from the voting group gives me doubts about the future of the Hall," King said on Twitter. " It’s outrageous ." The lack of transparency makes it even harder to understand the changes. There are no objective or obvious reasons for those who left and those who stayed. By having fewer voices, the criticism of the inevitable snubs will become even more glaring. And each individual voter will have much more power. Even with 50 voters, it has always seemed that the Hall of Fame is guided by a mysterious, arbitrary process. No one ever seems to know who's making the changes. With the most sweeping changes the Hall of Fame has seen in years, the problem becomes even more conspicuous. And while the NFL likes to claim that it has no control over the Hall of Fame , its fingerprints are all over leadership. The 26-member board of directors consists of eight owners or team representatives and the Commissioner. Even though it's called the "Pro Football Hall of Fame," everyone knows what it is. The candidates for enshrinement always come exclusively from the NFL; no CFL, Arena League, XFL, USFL, and/or UFL players or coaches ever have been or will be considered. It's an extension of the NFL. Which should give the NFL every reason to ensure it's properly managed, in all respects.

title: Steelers downgrade WR Michael Pittman Jr. to out, with a foot injury
summary: Pittman caught three passes for 58 yards in his Week 1 Pittsburgh debut.
full_text: The Steelers will head to New England for a Week 2 game without receiver Michael Pittman Jr. Pittman has been downgraded to out, with a foot injury. He had been listed as questionable. Pittman was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday. He didn't practice on Thursday or Friday. The downgrade is a common move for road teams. If the player isn't going to play, he doesn't travel. When he doesn't travel, he gets ruled out. Last week against the Falcons, Pittman caught three passes on three targets, for 58 yards in his Steelers debut. He had been traded by the Colts after Indy re-signed receiver Alec Pierce to a deal that pays $29 million per year. Based on the Steelers' online depth chart, Germie Bernard steps into Pittman's role. His absence will could mean for opportunities for the likes of DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson in Pittsburgh's offense.

title: Browns to reevaluate QB situation after Week 2, opening door for potential Shedeur Sanders start, per report
summary: A shaky Week 2 performance against Tampa Bay could push Todd Monken to bench Deshaun Watson
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns held the most publicized quarterback battle of the offseason, but the winner of said battle may not see Week 3.
The Browns will reevaluate their quarterback situation following their Week 2 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , according to ESPN . That sparks the possibility Shedeur Sanders replaces Deshaun Watson under center for Cleveland's home opener against the Carolina Panthers .
The Browns fell to the Jacksonville Jaguars in their season opener, 34-10. Watson completed 16 of 22 passes for 205 yards, one touchdown and one interception in his first game in 693 days. Monken's offense never got off the ground, recording 272 total yards and converting just one of eight third downs. Watson actually led the team in rushing with 38 yards on six carries. His performance reportedly left those in the building feeling "frustrated."
First-year Browns coach Todd Monken has defended Watson, and even said that he didn't anticipate the issue of his starting quarterback being a week-to-week issue. But a poor performance against the Buccaneers could mean a change under center.
One could argue that Sanders actually earned the starting job if you look at preseason stats, but Monken decided on the veteran, given the "full body of work."
"(I) took in the full body of work over the course of offseason to training camp to the games, the joint practice, and ultimately felt like to start the season on the road Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points -- I mean that's really what it's about," Monken said last month. "I felt that way going into last game but wasn't sure, and after we talked as a staff and after we relooked at everything, we're gonna go that direction."
While the son of NFL legend Deion Sanders made the Pro Bowl as a rookie, he was statistically one of the worst quarterbacks. Since his NFL debut in Week 11, Sanders recorded the second-worst completion percentage (57%) and threw the most interceptions (10). His 68.1 passer rating ranked second-worst in the league, as did his TD-INT ratio (7-10). With that being said, he definitely injected some energy into this fan base.
In Sanders' first NFL start, which came in Week 12, the Browns defeated the Las Vegas Raiders , 24-10. He completed 11 of 20 passes for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception, and became the first Browns quarterback since 1995 to win their first start. Previously, Browns quarterbacks went 0-17 in their first starts dating back to 1999. The last quarterback to win his first career start for the Browns was Eric Zeier, who was coached by Bill Belichick.
Sanders also became the first player in Browns history to throw for 350 yards, three touchdowns and rush for a touchdown in a single game during a Week 14 loss to the Tennessee Titans . The only other rookie quarterback to register that kind of stat line was Joe Burrow in 2020, according to CBS Sports Research.
If Watson can't jump-start the Browns' offense on Sunday, then it could be Sanders' time.

title: Last minute best bets for NFL Week 2: Patriots bounce back vs. Steelers, Eagles cover as road favorites
summary: Need some last-second help filling your bets for Week 2? We've got you covered
full_text:
Life is chaotic. You're being pulled in a bunch of different directions, so it's understandable that by the time you plant yourself on the couch on Sunday to gear up for another slate of NFL action, you don't exactly have your finger on the pulse. That's fine if you simply want to sit back and watch the events unfold, but not so great if you want to sprinkle some bets in along the way. That's were you can lean on us.
Below, we've rolled out five best bets for Week 2, as well as hand out a pick for every other matchup that'll take place on Sunday (and Monday) for you to either fade or follow. Let's not waste any more of your valuable time and get right into the picks!
NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
Cooper Rush is going to get another start for Atlanta, so we'll gladly fade him after a rough debut with the Falcons in Week 1. Out of every starting quarterback that took the field in Week 1, no one has a worse passer rating than Rush (54.9). There was essentially no vertical passing game as Rush averaged just 3.5 air yards per attempt (31st among QBs). Despite that, he still had an off-target rate of 13.6% (22nd). So, while the Panthers ' defense was pantsed by the Bears in Week 1 to the tune of 59 points allowed, they won't face nearly the firepower under center as they did when squaring up against Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams . Meanwhile, lost in the Bears' lighting it up, Bryce Young put together a strong effort, with his .29 EPA per dropback ranking sixth-highest among all quarterbacks in Week 1. The Panthers QB also owns a 4-1 SU and ATS record when he starts against Atlanta.
Projected score: Panthers 24, Falcons 20 The pick: Panthers -2.5

Drake Maye is also 6-0 SU and 5-1 ATS as a 3-plus point favorite at home in his career.
