full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens offensive tackle Carson Vinson (76) looks on after the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will be looking to follow up their massive Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts with another victory in their home opener against the New Orleans Saints. Injuries are already playing a major factor in this matchup. Nnamdi Madubuike and Teddye Buchanan are not yet ready for their 2026 debuts. Zay Flowers has been ruled out, and Ronnie Stanley is expected to join him. Starters Trey Hendrickson and John Simpson are also questionable but could play after participating in practice on Friday. So how do the Ravens navigate these absences and start 2-0? Derrick Henry vs. Saints’ run defense The Ravens’ offense in Week 1 against the Colts was centered around Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry, using the threat of one to play off the other. When Flowers went down, it took a while for the passing game to find its rhythm again, but Baltimore leaned on the run game to close the game out. Last week, the Saints gave up over 150 yards to Jahmyr Gibbs, who averaged over five yards per carry. Henry is capable of a similar performance, but without Flowers, he will likely face a lot of loaded boxes. If the offensive line is missing a starter or two, New Orleans could slow Baltimore’s run game and put more pressure on a Ravens wide receiver room that is also missing Ja’Kobi Lane. Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, and/or Elijah Sarratt will have to take advantage of 1-on-1 matchups and burn the Saints downfield. Carson Vinson vs. Chase Young Ronnie Stanley didn’t practice most of this week leading up to the game. He was listed as a limited participant on Friday, but reporters noted that while he was dressed, Stanley didn’t do much actual work compared to other veterans like John Simpson and Trey Hendrickson who were also listed as limited. The Ravens also elevated offensive tackle Gerad Lichtenhan off the practice squad, which makes Stanley’s ‘questionable’ status for Sunday look closer to ‘doubtful.’ That would position second-year lineman Carson Vinson to make his first career start at left tackle. He was drafted in the fifth round last year as a developmental tackle with long-term hopes of succeeding Stanley. Vinson started last year as a healthy scratch but eventually ended up taking the swing tackle job from veteran Joe Noteboom. Now he could face a massive test, protecting Lamar Jackson’s blind side against Chase Young. The former No. 1 pick had a quiet Week 1 statistically (with a strip sack that was strangely overturn), but he still gave Lions All-Pro Penei Sewell fits all game. Young is coming into the game with a calf injury, but is expected to play. Declan Doyle will do what he can to help Vinson out, including extra help, running the ball at Young, and using quick game and play action. But there will be situations where Vinson has to hold the edge in a third-down, gotta-have-it situation. That will be the first real chance to gauge his developmental progress and long-term potential to take over for Stanley at one of the game’s most important position. Ravens secondary vs. the Saints’ high-volume pass attack Against the Lions, Tyler Shough threw the ball nearly 60 times for 410 yards, three touchdowns, and two picks. On the other hand, the Saints didn’t have a single rusher who had 10 attempts or went over 50 yards. Part of that was the game script – New Orleans went down big early and had to play catch-up through the air most of the game. But it’s also clear that the Saints want to lean on their young quarterback (and his big arm). His group of offensive weapons is thin on exciting names outside of Chris Olave, who led the league with 182 receiving yards in Week 1. But the team has a lot of trust in former Bronco Devaughn Vele and fourth-round rookie Bryce Lance, two young, big-body receivers who combined for 10 catches and 111 yards in Detroit. Veteran tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant are not particularly explosive, but they are still capable pass-catchers who allow the Saints to use a variety of personnel groups. For the Ravens’ defense, this game will come down to Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins shutting down Chris Olave. That will force Shough to be perfect to his other targets while processing Jesse Minter’s mad-scientist defensive scheme. It is hard to see Shough being able to perfectly pick apart Minter’s secondary looks and disguises all game without a couple of mistakes that give the ball back to Lamar Jackson and company. The Saints will move the ball through sheer volume, but limiting Olave can cap their efficiency and make it nearly impossible to keep up with the Ravens.
author: Zach Canter

title: Ravens Roundtable: Score predictions, X-factors for Week 2 vs. Saints
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are set to take on the New Orleans Saints in their regular-season home opener on Sunday as heavy favorites, but injuries to multiple key starters could level the playing field. Here is how Baltimore Beatdown’s staff thinks the matchup will play out: Nikhil Mehta The Ravens’ injuries have thrown a major wrench […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Mark Andrews #89 of the Baltimore Ravens runs with the ball against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are set to take on the New Orleans Saints in their regular-season home opener on Sunday as heavy favorites, but injuries to multiple key starters could level the playing field. Here is how Baltimore Beatdown’s staff thinks the matchup will play out: Nikhil Mehta The Ravens’ injuries have thrown a major wrench into their Week 2 matchup with the Saints. Starting Carson Vinson at left tackle and either Andre Vorhees or Emery Jones at left guard will force Lamar Jackson to stay in rhythm and trust his quick passing game – which will be even harder with Zay Flowers also sidelined. Baltimore will need their other pass-catchers to step up, particularly Rashod Bateman after his goose egg in Week 1. Trey Hendrickson was quietly the straw that stirred Baltimore’s pass rush in Indianapolis, but a finger injury could impact his black belt-certified hand usage. Still, even having him on the field will draw the Saints’ attention and open up opportunities for the rest of the D-line. Baltimore still seems to have the coaching and talent advantage, but injuries could quickly take them out of the groove they found in Week 1 and create a much tighter contest than initially expected. X-factor: TE Mark Andrews. When Jackson needs a completion – to get back in rhythm, to convert a third down, to reach the end zone – he will probably go back to his faithful tight end. Andrews had a rough start in Week 1, but finish the game with 49 yards on 4 catches, suggesting he has a bounce-back season in him. This Sunday will be an excellent opportunity to get it going. Score prediction: Hand-wringing about injuries aside this is still an extremely talented Ravens team with a coaching staff that seems less vulnerable to the early-season trap games of the John Harbaugh era. Ravens 27, Saints 16. Stephen Bopst With it looking increasingly likely that LT Ronnie Stanley will be out this week, the Ravens are getting their first taste of injury adversity in the Jesse Minter/ Declan Doyle era. Personally, I think if there was a week for the Ravens offensive line to be down a few men – it would be this one. The Saints don’t have a strong interior defensive line and their one good pass rusher, Chase Young, is hobbled with a calf injury. This combined with Doyle’s ability to get Lamar Jackson out of the pocket via play-action, should minimize Stanley (and possibly John Simpson’s) absence. Additionally, with Zay Flowers out, some of the other Raven receivers will get their chance to make an impact. Because of the rapid ascension of Ja’Kobi Lane, we haven’t heard much about rookie Elijah Sarratt throughout camp and the beginning of the year. With both Flowers and Lane out, I’m very curious to see if Sarratt can make a meaningful impact. X-factor : DB blitzes. The Saints offensive line has struggled protecting against blitzing defensive backs which happens to be one of Jesse Minter’s play-calling strengths. I expect Minter to get creative this week on 3rd and long, dialing up a few blitzes that could lead to turnovers. Score prediction: This feels like a bad matchup for the Saints (regardless of injury). They aren’t effective at running the ball and relied heavily on QB Tyler Shough to play hero ball last week against a weak Lions secondary. The Ravens will force multiple Saint turnovers this week en-route to a 35-17 win. Zach Canter Despite the Ravens already dealing with injuries in Week 2 of the season, I don’t see it slowing down this new era of football in Baltimore at all. The offense will have some new struggles with Zay Flowers down and Ronnie Stanley looking like he won’t be playing. But I’m actually excited to see what offensive coordinator Declan Doyle can do with time to prepare and the wide receiver room in particular. Rashod Bateman will get a chance to lead the room with guys like Tez Walker, Elijah Sarratt filling in the rest of the top three. LaJohntay Wester can fill in some of the movement/motion roles that Flowers does and we saw veteran Chris Moore make a play last week when needed. I think Doyle will have a gameplan dialed up to get the ball out quick with Carson Vinson going up against Chase Young. Bateman could have a huge day as guy who’s release package allows him to win off the line quick. Expect Tez Walker to get multiple deep shot looks off of play action and Sarratt could fill in some of the big slot, steady hands role that Ja’Kobi Lane filled. X-factor: TE Matthew Hibner. This could be a huge breakout spot for the Ravens rookie. Hibner has some explosive receiving ability and with the Ravens missing Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane, this could be the game to get Hibner on the move catching the ball for some explosive plays for a tight end. Score prediction: Ravens 30, Saints 17 Dustin Cox Without two of their top three wide receivers in Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane, I expect a heavy dosage of Derrick Henry from the Ravens against a Saints’ defense that surrendered 165 rushing yards to the Lions in Week 1. Baltimore’s ground game looked as dangerous as ever with Henry and Lamar Jackson in Week 1 and I do not expect that to slow down this week, even if Ronnie Stanley is missing from the offensive line. Under center play action should once again be effective this week if Henry is rolling on the ground, which should help boost the passing attack in the absence of Flowers. Don’t be surprised if Jackson hits a big play to the speedy Devontez Walker off of play action in this game. X-factor: Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey. The Ravens’ top cornerback duo will need to be on the top of their game again this week against Chris Olave. New Orleans’ star receiver exploded for 182 yards on 10 catches last week against Detroit. If the Saints fall behind early, then it will be Olave that second-year quarterback Tyler Shough will look to for explosives in the passing attack to get back into the game. Score prediction: Ravens 33, Saints 13 Frank Platko The Ravens may struggle to put up 41 points for a consecutive week down Zay Flowers and possibly Ronnie Stanley as well. Their defense will need to ensure no lapses occur against the Saints, particularly in pass coverage. New Orleans airs the ball out frequently and Tyler Shough is not shy to take deep pass attempts. Like they did last week, limiting big plays through the air will be key. If the Ravens can put a lid on wide receiver Chris Olave and close middle of the field windows against the Saints’ tight ends, New Orleans will likely have a difficult time scoring. X-factor: WR Rashod Bateman. The Ravens will likely spread the ball out and get several pass-catchers involved without Flowers in the lineup. However, Bateman needs to have a strong performance after a zero-catch outing in Week 1, both for the Ravens’ success and for his own stock. He’ll almost surely receive more than one target and the Saints’ secondary is plenty beatable. Bateman asserting himself would take pressure off the Ravens’ younger, less proven wide receivers. Score prediction: Ravens 31, Saints 17 Kevin McNelis As Baltimore comes home for the first time this season, they’re in territory that’s uncomfortably familiar as injuries have them down several key pieces to start the year. With Zay Flowers doubtful and Ja’Kobi Lane down for a while, the passing attack is going to have to mix it up with some of their depth pieces to try to exploit a New Orleans defense that surrendered 369 yards to Detroit. Detroit’s star power was on display as Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown were able to hit the Saints for a combined four touchdowns, but who steps up this week for Baltimore? If I had my druthers, Derrick Henry gets the call early and often coming off of his hat-trick performance against Indy. Otherwise,…
author: Kevin McNelis

title: Ravens-Saints predictions: how will Baltimore adjust to injuries?
summary: The Baltimore Ravens largely dictated terms on both sides of the ball in their Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Jesse Minter’s defense bounced back after getting walked down the field to start the game, forcing three punts and two turnovers on their next five drives. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle exploded out of […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Baltimore Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins (21) and linebacker Trey Hendrickson (91) celebrates a turnover against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens largely dictated terms on both sides of the ball in their Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Jesse Minter’s defense bounced back after getting walked down the field to start the game, forcing three punts and two turnovers on their next five drives. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle exploded out of the gate with four touchdowns on his first five possessions and finished the game with over 500 total yards. But Minter (and defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver) could be without All-Pro edge rusher Trey Hendrickson on Sunday, while Doyle could be missing as many as three of his Week 1 starters. The Ravens are still entering their Week 2 matchup against the Saints as 8.5-point favorites ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ), but those injuries could make the margins much tighter. Getting Pressure on Tyler Shough In Hendrickson, the Ravens would not just lose their best individual pass rusher. The former Bengal may have made his name by producing in a four-man rush, but Minter and Weaver clearly have bigger plans for him in Baltimore. Take Week 1, for example. Hendrickson torched Colts left tackle Bernhard Raimann with speed-to-power moves in their lone previous matchup back in 2023. Despite the time interval since, both teams likely studied that encounter last week. Other coaches may have been content to simply turn Hendrickson loose against Raimann a second time, but the Ravens’ staff had a slightly different approach. Minter designed his pressure packages around Hendrickson’s ability to collapse the pocket from the blind side. The opposite edge rusher, often Tavius Robinson, was lying in wait for Daniel Jones to feel the pressure and move off his spot. With the fastball established, Hendrickson could mix in change-ups with his elite hand usage and Minter could throw curves by having him loop back to the inside. Hendrickson missed most of this week’s practices, giving Minter and Weaver a chance to tinker with the pass rush for Sunday’s matchup with the Saints. Their offensive line had a solid Week 1 performance outside of right tackle Taliese Fuaga, who had his hands full with Aidan Hutchinson. The Ravens do not have another edge rusher of that caliber, so they will likely need to scheme up pressure to get to Tyler Shough consistently. Mike Green only had nine pass rush snaps in Week 1, but he would be in line for a lot more if Hendrickson is absent. He has some power, but his game is more built around his combination of burst and bend that allow him to get around the edge. New Orleans will likely have left tackle Kelvin Banks take Green upfield when he tries to do so, which will create space next to the left guard. Minter can attack that directly with delayed blitzes from the second-level. He can also use Calais Campbell and Travis Jones to draw double-teams and flip them directly into into pick plays, potentially with Aeneas Peebles using his quickness to line up over the right guard and loop through the opposite B gap. Keeping Lamar Jackson Clean On offense, the Ravens will be without star wide receiver Zay Flowers, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley and left guard John Simpson are also questionable. Flowers was dominant before going down in the first half in Week 1, while Stanley and Simpson enabled Jackson to roll out to the left side for explosive plays. That was how Baltimore opened their first possession in Indianapolis. Those absences could stack on each other in the pass game. Flowers is often Jackson’s first read, especially under pressure. That could happen more often on Sunday with Carson Vinson making his first NFL start (potentially against Chase Young) and either Andrew Vorhees or Emery Jones stepping in at left guard. Doyle has two obvious solutions: using extra blockers and going into the shotgun. The former deprives the Ravens of numbers downfield with Flowers already sidelined, while the latter moves Jackson away from the under-center looks that worked so well in Week 1. Doyle will stick with his 12 and 13 personnel formations with Jackson under center to slam the run with Derrick Henry and set up max-protect play-action shots. On those plays, the Saints will likely focus on Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews, the Ravens’ clear second and third receiving targets behind Flowers. That should create opportunities for Devontez Walker to run free after missing Week 1 with an ankle injury. The Ravens will still want Jackson to drop back and pass from under center, but if the left side of the line cannot hold, they will have to consider a few changes. Rolling out to the left off play-action may be less of an option, and Jackson might need to stay in the shotgun in obvious passing situations so he has more time against the blitz. Moving to the shotgun can also remedy any potential weakness in the run game as a result of this week’s injuries. Even the threat of Jackson taking off with the ball changes the math at the line of scrimmage and forces an unblocked defender into a tough decision. Enough a whiff of hesitation can give the O-line enough of an advantage to create a hole.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Buffalo Bills records and milestones from Week 2 win over Detroit Lions
summary: It didn’t take long for the Bills to start making history in their new home.  The Buffalo Bills christened the new Highmark Stadium with a 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night, moving to 2-0 in the process. Josh Allen accounted for five touchdowns, James Cook ran for 139 yards, and Buffalo scored touchdowns on five of its […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: A general view of the Buffalo Bills taking the field as fireworks explode prior to the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images It didn’t take long for the Bills to start making history in their new home. The Buffalo Bills christened the new Highmark Stadium with a 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night, moving to 2-0 in the process. Josh Allen accounted for five touchdowns, James Cook ran for 139 yards, and Buffalo scored touchdowns on five of its first six possessions. But the scoreboard wasn’t the only place the Bills were putting up numbers Thursday night. From Allen reaching all the way back to 1929 for company to Cook moving up the franchise record book, there is plenty to Shout! about after Week 2. _____________________________________________________________________________ Josh Allen became the first player in NFL history with at least five passing touchdowns and three rushing touchdowns through the first two games of a season. And somehow, that’s not the strangest Allen stat to come out of Thursday night. Allen became just the second player in NFL history to account for at least nine total touchdowns, including four rushing touchdowns, over a span of five days. The other was Ernie Nevers, who did it in November 1929 when he ran for nine touchdowns and scored all 59 of the Chicago Cardinals’ points in two wins. Yes, 1929. Josh Allen is the second player in NFL history to account for 9+ total TDs & 4+ rushing TDs over a span of 5 days. Allen joins Ernie Nevers from November 24-28, 1929, when he ran for 9 TDs & scored all 59 of the Cardinals' points in 2 wins (19-0 & 40-6), per @OptaSTATS . pic.twitter.com/W2Mh4YkOXq — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 18, 2026 Allen’s second rushing touchdown Thursday also gave him 82 for his career, tying Hall of Fame running back Jim Taylor for 18th on the NFL’s all-time rushing-touchdown list. _____________________________________________________________________________ James Cook entered Thursday night needing 130 rushing yards to pass Joe Cribbs for fifth place on the Bills’ all-time rushing list. He got 139. Cook passed Cribbs’ 4,445 career rushing yards and now sits alone in fifth place in franchise history . Next up are Josh Allen and Fred Jackson — although one of those two is going to keep moving the target. _____________________________________________________________________________ Then there’s Dalton Kincaid. Apparently, he wasn’t satisfied after Week 1 After putting up a career-high 130 receiving yards in Week 1, Kincaid added seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown Thursday night. That gives him 225 receiving yards through two games. That’s the fifth-most receiving yards by a tight end through the first two games of a season in the Super Bowl era, trailing only Ben Coates (285 in 1994), Shannon Sharpe (247 in 1995), Rich Caster (240 in 1972), and Jared Cook (229 in 2018). Dalton Kincaid has tallied the fifth-most receiving yards through 2 games by a tight end in the Super Bowl era: 1. Ben Coates – 285 (1994) 2. Shannon Sharpe – 247 (1995) 3. Rich Caster – 240 (1972) 4. Jared Cook – 229 (2018) 5. Dalton Kincaid – 225 (2026) pic.twitter.com/TRKDORPH9m — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 18, 2026 Kincaid has also led Buffalo in receiving in each of the first two games of the season. _____________________________________________________________________________ Greg Rousseau recorded two sacks against Jared Goff, giving him four through the first two weeks of the season. That’s the most by a Bills player through two games since Mario Williams had 4.5 in 2013. Greg Rousseau has four sacks this season, marking the most sacks by a Bill in the team's first two games since Mario Williams had 4.5 sacks in 2013. pic.twitter.com/KxTGn5n665 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 18, 2026 Rousseau also joined Bruce Smith as the only players in franchise history to record at least two sacks in each of the first two games of a season. But, the streak didn’t start this season. Rousseau has recorded at least half a sack in five consecutive regular-season games . The last Bills player with a longer streak was Lorenzo Alexander, who did it in seven straight games in 2016. _____________________________________________________________________________ Joe Brady became the first head coach in Bills history to win each of his first two regular-season games with the team. But it isn’t just the wins we are Shout!ing about. Buffalo has scored 77 points through Brady’s first two games as head coach. That’s the fourth-most points scored by a team in a head coach’s first two games during the Super Bowl era, trailing only Bud Carson’s 1989 Cleveland Browns (89), Dan Campbell’s 2015 Miami Dolphins (82), and Mike Martz’s 2000 St. Louis Rams (78). Through 2 games under HC Joe Brady, the Bills have scored 77 points. That marks the fourth-most points in a head coaches first two games in the Super Bowl Era. pic.twitter.com/NnD51VwsBj — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 18, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ The Bills didn’t waste much time making some history in their new home. Allen’s 1-yard touchdown run on Buffalo’s opening possession gave him the first regular-season touchdown in the new Highmark Stadium. And then the offense kept going. Buffalo became the first team since the Arizona Cardinals in 2006 to score at least 14 points in the first quarter of the first game in its new home stadium. By halftime, the Bills had 27 points, making them the first team to score at least that many in the first half of the first game in a new home stadium since the Dallas Cowboys scored 34 in the first half of their Texas Stadium debut in 1971. The Bills are now the first team to score 27+ points in the first half in their new home stadium since the 1971 Cowboys scored 34 first half points at Texas Stadium (10/24/1971). https://t.co/s2VgdE91WH — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 18, 2026 So, yes, there were fireworks before the game. Turns out the Bills had plenty more once it started.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: First projection at a Dalton Kincaid extension with Buffalo Bills
summary: Is it too early to start envisioning what a second contract for Dalton Kincaid could look like? Sure. Maybe a little bit. While he is in the fourth year of his rookie deal with the Buffalo Bills, and the club has already picked up his fifth-year option for 2027, we know Brandon Beane’s history of […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Tight end Dalton Kincaid #86 reacts after scoring a touchdown during the first half of an NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Billsat Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York, USA, on Thursday, September 17, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Is it too early to start envisioning what a second contract for Dalton Kincaid could look like? Sure. Maybe a little bit. While he is in the fourth year of his rookie deal with the Buffalo Bills, and the club has already picked up his fifth-year option for 2027, we know Brandon Beane’s history of signing homegrown talents early. Without a Bills game on Sunday in Week 2, we have time to peer well into the future on Kincaid’s potentially impending extension. After a small-sample season in 2025 in which Kincaid led all tight ends in yards per route run — the ultimate receiving efficiency metric — and his blazing start to 2026, we need to start this projection at the top of the tight end market. Here are the top 3 contracts at tight end right now in the NFL: Years Total Value APY Guaranteed At Signing George Kittle 4 $76.4M $19.1M $33M Trey McBride 4 $76M $19M $32.5M Tucker Kraft 4 $75M $18.75 $26.5M While it’s always relevant to showcase the “top” of the market at a certain position when these type of scenarios arise, it’s simultaneously the perfect time to reference why guaranteed at signing matters more than anything else. Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts, who’s technically fourth in Average Per Year (APY) — which is the default metric used for sorting purposes — at $17.67M, actually has received the most money guaranteed at signing of the group at $36M. With that, let’s get into the ages of these players, which absolutely will play into negotiations with Kincaid. Pitts is almost exactly one year younger than Kincaid. Of course Kittle is much older. Kraft was picked in the same draft as Kincaid but also a year younger, and McBride is a month younger than the Bills star tight end. And let’s stack these tight ends against each other from a production standpoint. I’ll remove Kittle because while he has the highest APY at the position, because of his age, I don’t believe the deal he’s currently playing on will factor as significantly into contract talks with Kincaid: Games Career Yards Per Route Run Regular-season games missed due to injury Career catches Trey McBride 67 1.80 1 356 Tucker Kraft 43 1.67 9 116 Kyle Pitts 79 1.63 8 284 Dalton Kincaid 43 1.91 10 168 In a perfect world for the Bills, the team would’ve gotten ahead of the Kraft contract. But Green Bay didn’t hesitate to hand him the massive extension despite his torn ACL in 2025 while Kincaid’s prolonged injury history likely very much factored into why an extension has yet to be offered to Kincaid. There is some timing precedent for a Kincaid extension — Greg Rousseau. He and the Bills agreed on a second contract after his fourth season. If the Bills ultimately go that route, it’d be sensible, right? Rousseau was a quality player for Buffalo in his first four seasons. And they waited. Kincaid has been quality too, and probably even more productive than Rousseau at his respective position but noticeably less durable. Beane and Co. haven’t historically given out contracts in-season — not many teams do — and this is precisely where the projection gets hazy because we don’t know what’s ahead for Kincaid. Internally, the Bills may know he’s miles ahead on the health front compared to either of the past two seasons. They may finally feel great about that vital element for any player. If that’s the case, they’d subsequently be expecting a monstrous 1,000-plus yard campaign for Kincaid, which would come at the perfect time for the tight end given where he is timeline wise on that rookie deal. And I think a Kincaid extension would look something like this: Years Total Value APY Fully Guaranteed At Signing 4 $76.8 $19.2 Somewhere between $28M – $32M Almost identical to his 2023 draft classmate Tucker Kraft. Essentially a market-setting deal for Kincaid, who was a bit older when he started his NFL career — turned 24 in October of his rookie campaign, but is still distinctly in his professional prime. And right now, I’m projecting lower than truly market-setting on the critical guaranteed-at-signing figure because Beane has regularly gotten these extensions done under that mark. But that could’ve been due to the quality of player he’s signed in the past. It doesn’t feel like the Bills would get into a hold out/hold intype situation with Kincaid — he very much appears to be fully embedded in Buffalo’s team culture — but contract negotiations can certainly alter team-player relationships. Then again, James Cook technically held in last summer. Said hold in lasted like two days, and he signed a very team-friendly deal. Culture can impact the contract-front too. Even if Beane can work his magic to get a Kincaid extension under, say $18M in APY and $32M in guaranteed at signing, we have to be prepared for this to be an expensive deal. But, frankly, it’d be a long time coming for the Bills to have a (homegrown) receiving weapon for Josh Allen worthy of getting a lucrative extension.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Panthers fans’ confidence holding steady after historic loss
summary: You may have heard that the Carolina Panthers allowed the most points that they ever have in a game to the Chicago Bears in what became the highest scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. It was not a good look for defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero or his players. It did, however, help underscore that […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers looks to hand the ball off during the game against the Chicago Bears at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images You may have heard that the Carolina Panthers allowed the most points that they ever have in a game to the Chicago Bears in what became the highest scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. It was not a good look for defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero or his players. It did, however, help underscore that most people are worried about the development of quarterback Bryce Young with the defense ranking as a distant afterthought. This week’s Reacts survey showed a small dip in the overall confidence that fans have in the current direction of the franchise and a large part of that is attributable to the offense, before the game got well and truly out of hand, out scoring all but one game in Young’s career. Young showed a level of play that has rarely been seen outside of Atlanta. The only game where Young has scored more than he did against the Bears last week was 2024’s season finale where the Panthers beat the Falcons 44-38 in overtime. It’s the kind of performance he was drafted to have routinely. Instead, it has proved very much the exception. Showing that exception in a season opener—a game that Young has traditionally bombed in— provides fresh hope that he has turned the proverbial corner. Optimism on that front is my best theory for why more people aren’t concerned about the Panthers’ future with their current defense. A surprising 41% of fans think that last Sunday will prove to be an average to below average performance for Young and offensive coordinator Brad Idzik. Again, evidence that a lot of Panthers fans are ready and willing to jump on the Young hype train if he’s pulling out of that station this year. Similar optimism has moved the Panthers odds over at FanDuel from +1.5 point underdogs when odds opened to -2.5 point favorites here on the eve of the game. Will Atlanta Bryce show up against the Falcons tomorrow or will we see another disappointing game that will deflate most of the fanbase? We’ll find out tomorrow.
author: Walker Clement

title: Chicago Bears vs. Minnesota Vikings Game Picks and Predictions
summary: Hello Chicago Bears fans! We are back with our roundtable on Week 2 predictions of the Chicago Bears’ home opener against the Minnesota Vikings. This week, the Bears face one of the NFL’s most unpredictable defenses as Brian Flores matches wits with Ben Johnson. Johnson’s offenses have tended to get the better of Flores coordinated […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 08: Joe Thuney #62 of the Chicago Bears in action against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 08, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello Chicago Bears fans! We are back with our roundtable on Week 2 predictions of the Chicago Bears’ home opener against the Minnesota Vikings. This week, the Bears face one of the NFL’s most unpredictable defenses as Brian Flores matches wits with Ben Johnson. Johnson’s offenses have tended to get the better of Flores coordinated defense over the years; however, Flores’ defense gave the Bears fits last year in their two games, which they split. What happens when the unstoppable force meets the immovable object? We are going to find out on Sunday at 12:00pm CST. Below are our predictions for the game. Lester : Bet the over again this week as the Bears will win 34 to 27. The running game will be the story, as D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai will again be over 200 combined yards, and Caleb Williams will add 50 more on scrambles. The quick passing game will find Colston Loveland for a half dozen catches, and Caleb will hit one massive deep shot to Luther Burden III. Grady Jarrett picks up his first sack of the year, and the Bears get three more takeaways. Sam : The forecast calls for a rainy Sunday at Soldier Field. All the more reason for Ben Johnson to rely on his ground game to neutralize Minnesota’s blitz. Hopefully, Caleb has been practicing his wet ball drills, and they can stay clean from turnovers. I think it could be a slog at times and a bit lower scoring. Bears 27, Vikings 23 Gary : Bears 28, Vikings 17. Heavy dose of the ground game makes QB1’s life easier; Carson Wentz takes a couple sacks, loses a fumble, and throws a pick. The game gets iced with a Caleb Williams touchdown pass. Bears move to their rightful spot: 1st place in the NFC North. Gooch : Bears 42, Vikings 10. I know most analysts are predicting a major regression in the Bears’ scoring this week given the Vikings’ defense, but I don’t think Flores will find as much success this week with his pressure scheme against Caleb as he did against Jordan Love. Caleb will throw for 300 yards and 3 touchdowns. Colston Loveland finally gets on the board with two touchdown catches and 80 yards receiving. Swift adds a rushing touchdown and puts up another hundred-yard game. On defense, both Sweat and Booker notch a sack and several QB pressures as the Bears find Wentz a much easier target in the pocket than Bryce Young was in Carolina. Bears force Wentz to throw two interceptions, putting the Vikings behind the eight ball for most of the game. Superfans: If I didn’t know any better, I’d say Gooch was a distant relative on Busha Swerski’s side with a prediction like that. Actually, I may need to check the family tree to be sure he’s not a second cousin, because a first cousin wouldn’t have gone with such a close score prediction. A first cousin would have brought another 50-burger to the party with some beefs and giardiniera, and called it: Bears 56, Vikings 3. What do you think the score will be in Bears vs. Vikings? Who will win? What amazing things will happen? Tell us in the comments below!

title: NFL fans think the Chicago Bears will have the best offense in 2026
summary: I always enjoy seeing how NFL fans vote whenever SB Nation’s Reacts features a question related to the Chicago Bears. It’s one thing to post a poll on Windy City Gridiron’s Feed section, since that’s filled with mostly Bears fans (and a few trolls), but it’s another thing when there’s a question posed on the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears looks on during the game against the Carolina Panthersat Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images I always enjoy seeing how NFL fans vote whenever SB Nation’s Reacts features a question related to the Chicago Bears. It’s one thing to post a poll on Windy City Gridiron’s Feed section, since that’s filled with mostly Bears fans (and a few trolls), but it’s another thing when there’s a question posed on the Feed section of SB Nation’s main NFL page, because fans of all 32 teams chime in. After the Week 1 games, they asked which team would have the best offense in 2o26, and look who was number one by a wide margin—Ben Johnson’s Chicago Bears. That same question could change if you asked it after Week 2. The Buffalo Bills just smacked the Detroit Lions around on Thursday Night Football, and the Bears face a tough defense on Sunday, when the Minnesota Vikings come to town. The San Francisco 49ers, back from Australia, have the Miami Dolphins visiting, so the ‘Niners offense could pop off again. The Baltimore Ravens host the New Orleans Saints, so Declan Doyle’s offense might put up some massive numbers too. The Jacksonville Jaguars, in year two under Liam Coen, are expected to be among the league’s best offenses, but they head to Mile High Stadium to face the Denver Broncos. But back to our Bears, even with a division foe looming, our fans are confident the franchise is on the right track. Last week our confidence level was at 87%, so the historic road win gave us a boost to 94% The win over the Carolina Panthers also moved the odds for the Bears to make the NFC playoffs. According to our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook , Chicago now has the sixth-best odds to make the NFC postseason at -144. Caleb Williams’ MVP odds have also shot up, and he trails only Buffalo’s Josh Allen (+260) and Baltimore’s Lamar Jackson (+650). If you think Caleb can build on his strong Week 1 and make a serious push for MVP, FanDuel has those odds at +1000. Head coach Ben Johnson has talked about their goal of being the highest-scoring offense in NFL history, and if the Bears are going to get back to the playoffs, they may need to win a bunch of shootouts this year, because Chicago’s defense was lit up in Week 1. In our other Reacts poll question this week, over half our fans have at least a medium level of concern over Dennis Allen’s unit. I think dickbutkus97 had some interesting perspective when he said, “I’m going to wait a while to let it unfold. This team actually has coaches who can develop players- and has outperformed our expectations in 100% of the seasons we have had with them so far. So, not panicking, as familiar as that is to the Bears fandom.” The Bears face a backup quarterback on Sunday as Carson Wentz gets the nod for the Vikings. He’s a vet, but not nearly as mobile as Kyler Murray, so maybe the defense can harass him a bit. The following week, they host the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, and last year the Bears bullied Philly while holding them to 15 points, 317 total yards, and 4 of 12 on third downs. The New York Jets come to Chicago in Week 4, so the next three games offer a chance to see the Bears’ defense tighten things up.

title: Bears vs Vikings: Minnesota may not blitz Caleb Williams as much at Soldier Field
summary: On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll previews the Week 2 matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Minnesota Vikings with longtime friend of the show, Tyler Forness, who covers the Vikings for A to Z Sports, and also with our guy, Bears Over Beers cohost Bryan Orenchuk. They kick things off by going […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 08: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears throws a pass against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter in the game at Soldier Field on September 08, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images On her latest Making Monsters podcast, Taylor Doll previews the Week 2 matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Minnesota Vikings with longtime friend of the show, Tyler Forness, who covers the Vikings for A to Z Sports, and also with our guy, Bears Over Beers cohost Bryan Orenchuk. They kick things off by going over the Kyler Murray injury and what it means with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback. The Vikes have a slew of weapons, so they talk about those as well, the running back room without the injured Jordan Mason. They also dive into the Brian Flores blitz-heavy defense and whether he will approach Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams the same way he did Green Bay’s offense. As for the Bears, they discuss how the secondary can slow down Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson, and company, and if the Bears defense can get after Wentz. They also look at the Bears’ offense and how it matches up with Minny’s defense. But back to the Vikings and defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ blitzing trends in his four games against Caleb Williams. Taylor asked Tyler if he thinks Minnesota would blitz as much this week as he did last week at home against Jordan Love and the Packers, and here’s what he said. “That’s where things get really interesting,” Forness said on the podcast. “I did pull up some stats trying to figure out what does this look like. At Soldier Field facing Caleb Williams, Brian Flores is blitzing 44.4% and 40.9% of the time. At US Bank Stadium, 60% and 77.8% of the time. I think some of that has to do with the playing surface and maybe not having faith, but just not trying to put the back-end defenders in as many negative spots because so much of what they do is communication on the back end, and maneuvering and showing one look and then going to another. And with the playing surface, it’s just a lot harder to do some of those things with the change of direction. So, I think you’re going to see a little bit less of the overall blitzing.” Make sure you check out Taylor’s show in either of the embeds below for her Bears vs. Vikings preview! title: Let’s hope this Colston Loveland prediction comes true for the Bears this Sunday
summary: After watching second-year Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland emerge as one of the league’s best last season, it was pretty jarring to see him finish the team’s season opener with zero catches for zero yards. Logically, there could be a number of reasons for this: the Bears dominating on the ground so much that […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - NOVEMBER 16: Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland (84) makes Minnesota Vikings defensive back Josh Metellus (44) and Minnesota Vikings defensive back Harrison Smith (22) on their tackle attempts during the fourth quarter of a NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears on November 16, 2025, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After watching second-year Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland emerge as one of the league’s best last season, it was pretty jarring to see him finish the team’s season opener with zero catches for zero yards. Logically, there could be a number of reasons for this: the Bears dominating on the ground so much that getting him the ball wasn’t a priority, Caleb Williams just missing him sometimes in the progression, and Carolina working hard to take him away as a receiving option. And of course, let’s not forget Loveland also started off slow last season before coming on extremely strong to close the year. That said, it would be extremely welcome if Loveland got back on track against a Minnesota Vikings defense that will need its tight ends to serve as outlets against defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ aggressive defense. That’s what NFL.com’s Gennaro Filice is predicting could happen on Sunday when the Bears face off against the Vikings. “Despite Chicago racking up 59 points and 552 yards at Carolina , Loveland somehow finished the game without a single catch. It was a bizarre disappearing act, especially considering the tight end comfortably paced Bears pass catchers in snaps (60) and routes run (33). I think the pendulum emphatically swings back in Loveland’s favor this Sunday against the division-rival Vikings. With Brian Flores blitzing his face off, Minnesota’s defense puts serious stress on opposing offenses. However, the aggressive approach leaves the Vikes vulnerable to chunk gains, as evidenced last Sunday by Jordan Love ‘s 387 passing yards, including eight explosive plays (20-plus yards). Facing pressure from all angles , Caleb Williams will seek an easy outlet. Insert the 6-foot-6, 241-pound mismatch nightmare in the No. 84 jersey. One Say no more. Now, it’s worth noting that Flores and the Vikings defense probably wouldn’t make this easy. Loveland has only put up 52 yards on five catches in two games against Minnesota last year, though this was before he had truly come into his own. The young tight end is a different player than he was then. But that’s all the more reason for the Vikings to specifically try to take him out of the game and force other players, like Luther Burden III and Cole Kmet, to beat them. So the idea of him putting up massive yards still seems unlikely. But touchdowns in the red zone? That’s an area the Bears could be more intentional about getting Loveland the football, which could get him going in a bigger way on Sunday. Especially with a possible backup quarterback playing for the Vikings on Sunday in Carson Wentz, the Bears need to hit Minnesota where it hurts early and often. And we already know there are few players on any defense who can lock Loveland up when it’s time to hit paydirt. My bold prediction: Loveland gets his first touchdown this weekend. If he goes even bigger than that? It’s just icing on the cake.

title: Chicago Bears vs. Minnesota Vikings: Week 2 Players to Watch
summary: The NFL season is always evolving. Week 2 arrives with just a bit more insight into who the teams are and how they project to attack the next opponent. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 08: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings runs for a first down in the second quarter of a game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 08, 2023 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season is always evolving. Week 2 arrives with just a bit more insight into who the teams are and how they project to attack the next opponent. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team’s success. I’ll also try and mix in a few under the radar players from time to time. Let’s start with the Minnesota Vikings offensive player that I will be focused on. Offense: T.J. Hockenson, TE In 13 career games against the Bears (both as member of Vikings and Lions) T.J. Hockenson has had 58 catches for 618 yards with 3 touchdowns. That equates to roughly 4.5 catches per game and 47.5 yards per game with a score every 4 games. Even so, the fact that he hasn’t scored against the Bears in 6 games is not why he’s on this list. Hock is on this list because he’s going up against a team in Chicago that struggles to defend the pass and is starting a rookie at safety with a veteran QB in Carson Wentz. With Justin Jefferson figuring to gain most of the attention, I expect either veteran signal-caller to target Hockenson more than the 6.4 targets he is accustomed to receiving against the Bears. If Thieneman can stay close both mentally and physically, he will once again remind Vikings fans of the draft day disappointment when he could have been a Viking but the Vikes instead chose DT Caleb Banks out of Florida. Speaking of rookies, given the fact that Jordan Mason is on IR, I was tempted to highlight former Wake Forest Demon Deacon and 6th round pick, running back Demond Claiborne. But as I suggested prior to the draft, he is likely a player that benefits from some seasoning before pressed into action. Defense: Dallas Turner, Edge Speaking of seasoning, it seems that may have been exactly what the former first-rounder needed to finally reach his potential, and he’s now showing why Minnesota targeted him two seasons ago. That said, I have been nervous about that potential being reached against Chicago for a while now. And if week one is any indication, where Turner had 7(!) QB hits and a sack, Turner is ready. It sounds like he has the attention of head coach Ben Johnson. Which we know by now means the HC will have a plan for DT. As my guy MongoPeanut pointed out, his one-on-one matchup against Braxton Jones will be key this week, and I expect a lot of TE help to keep him contained. The problem is Brian Flores is a madman at calling defensive plays, creating pressure and chaos for opposing offenses. Oh, and Minnesota is loaded with absolute dogs on defense like Andrew Van Ginkel, Ivan Pace Jr., Blake Cashman, Erik Wilson, Byron Murphy Jr., and my personal Minny fav, Josh Metellus. But Turner taking that next step into consistent pass rush and playmaking threat could be enough to stifle any offense. Even ours. What about you? Which Viking player outside of Justin Jefferson will you be keying in on this week?

title: Chicago Bears Week 2 Flashbacks: Grossman, Amukamara, Piñeiro, and more!
summary: Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we rev the engines up for another season-long trip down memory lane! 1.) 2006, Bears vs. Lions: Rex Grossman has a career day as Chicago rolls. Coming off a 26–0 shutout of Brett Favre and the Packers in Green Bay, the Bears returned to Soldier Field in Week […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 15: Pat O'Donnell #19 holds as Eddy Pineiro #15 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a 40 yard field goal in the second quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 15, 2019 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we rev the engines up for another season-long trip down memory lane! 1.) 2006, Bears vs. Lions: Rex Grossman has a career day as Chicago rolls. Coming off a 26–0 shutout of Brett Favre and the Packers in Green Bay, the Bears returned to Soldier Field in Week 2 of the 2006 season looking to prove their dominant opener was no fluke. Rex Grossman made sure of that. After spending much of his first three NFL seasons battling injuries, and even hearing some boos during the preseason, Grossman put together what was easily the best performance of his young career. He completed 20 of 27 passes for 289 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions, good for a ridiculous 148.0 passer rating. Both his passing yardage and touchdown total were career highs at the time. Chicago wasted almost no time taking control. On Detroit’s opening possession, Tank Johnson sacked Jon Kitna and knocked the ball loose, allowing Brian Urlacher to recover at the Lions’ three-yard line. Grossman immediately cashed in, finding tight end John Gilmore for a touchdown. The defense forced another fumble on Detroit’s next possession, this time with Alex Brown stripping Kevin Jones and recovering it himself. Robbie Gould turned that takeaway into a field goal, and early in the second quarter Grossman found Bernard Berrian for a 41-yard touchdown to put Chicago ahead 17–0. Grossman tossed two touchdowns to Gilmore, while Berrian finished with 89 receiving yards and Desmond Clark added 85 yards and a score. On the other side of the ball, things weren’t any easier for Detroit. The Bears recovered three Lions fumbles, held them to 245 total yards and sacked Kitna six times. The 34–7 win moved Chicago to 2–0 while giving the Bears a staggering 60–7 scoring advantage through the first two games of the season. As it turned out, that start was a pretty good indication of what was coming. The Bears went 13–3, won the NFC North, defeated Seattle and New Orleans in the playoffs, and advanced to Super Bowl XLI. And for at least one afternoon at Soldier Field, the phrase “ Good Rex ” didn’t even begin to cover it. 2.) 2018, Bears vs. Seahawks: The defense finishes the job and gives Matt Nagy his first win. The Matt Nagy era couldn’t have started in much more painful fashion. One week earlier, the Bears had taken a 20–0 lead at Lambeau Field, only to watch Aaron Rodgers lead the Packers all the way back for a crushing 24–23 victory. So when the Bears returned home for a Monday Night Football matchup against Russell Wilson and the Seattle Seahawks, the message was pretty simple: Finish. Chicago opened the game with a 96-yard touchdown drive capped by Mitchell Trubisky’s shovel pass to Trey Burton, but the offense struggled to find much consistency afterward. Fortunately, the Bears defense didn’t need much help. Led by their newly acquired superstar Khalil Mack, Chicago harassed Wilson all night, ultimately sacking him six times. Even after Trubisky threw interceptions on consecutive second-quarter possessions, the defense answered both mistakes by immediately forcing Seattle three-and-outs. Trubisky finally gave the Bears some breathing room early in the fourth quarter when he connected with rookie Anthony Miller for a 10-yard touchdown, making it 17–3. Seattle answered with a touchdown to pull within seven. Then Prince Amukamara made the play of the night. With 6:37 remaining, Amukamara recognized the Seahawks’ formation, jumped a pass intended for Rashaad Penny and took the interception 49 yards to the house. It was Amukamara’s first interception since 2015 and the first pick-six of his NFL career. 20 days till the #NFLdraft Today’s countdown feature is Prince Amukamara, who was solid for the ‘18 #Bears . 66 TOT, 12 PD, 3 INT, 2 FF, 1 INT He was drafted ‘11 by the NYG in the 1st round. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/zPyCaqVJ5s — Just Another Year Chicago: Bears (@JAYChi_Bears) April 5, 2024 One possession later, Danny Trevathan blitzed Wilson, recorded his second sack of the night and forced a fumble that Leonard Floyd recovered. Trevathan finished with a team-high eight tackles, two sacks, two quarterback hits and the forced fumble, earning NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors. Seattle managed one last touchdown with 14 seconds remaining, but Anthony Miller recovered the ensuing onside kick to seal a 24–17 Bears win. More importantly, it gave Nagy his first regular-season victory as an NFL head coach. After spending the previous week hearing about the collapse at Lambeau, the Bears defense finished one. It wouldn’t be the last time that unit carried them in 2018. 3.) 2019, Bears @ Broncos: Fourth-and-15, one second left, and “Steady Eddy” After the excitement of a 12–4 division championship season in 2018, the Bears’ 2019 campaign began with a thud. Chicago managed just three points in a season-opening loss to Green Bay, and things weren’t looking much better offensively a week later in Denver. Eddy Piñeiro provided almost all of Chicago’s early scoring, connecting from 40 and 52 yards to give the Bears a 6–3 halftime lead. The offense had now gone six quarters without scoring a touchdown. That drought finally ended late in the third quarter when David Montgomery punched the ball across the goal line from one yard out, finishing an 80-yard drive in which the Bears ran the ball on all nine plays. Chicago suddenly had a 13–3 lead and appeared to have the game under control. It didn’t last. Denver chipped away with a field goal before Joe Flacco led the Broncos on one final drive. With 31 seconds remaining, he found Emmanuel Sanders for a seven-yard touchdown. After each team traded penalties, Broncos coach, and former Bears defensive coordinator, Vic Fangio elected to go for two. Flacco found Sanders again. Denver 14, Chicago 13. After an offseason dominated by Chicago’s very public search for a kicker following the infamous end to the 2018 season, it looked as though the Bears might not even get Piñeiro a chance. Then came fourth-and-15. September 15th, 2019: The Bears beat the Broncos in a wild finish in Denver #DaBears pic.twitter.com/xfWTNfZ5Nr — Back Then Football (@BackThenFB) September 16, 2026 With nine seconds remaining and Chicago at its own 40, Mitchell Trubisky stepped up in the pocket and found Allen Robinson II over the middle for 25 yards. Robinson went down at the Denver 35 and the Bears managed to call their final timeout. One second remained. Out came Piñeiro. From 53 yards away, he drilled it. Bears win, 16–14. Piñeiro finished the afternoon a perfect 3-for-3 on field goals, hitting from 40, 52 and 53 yards. His game-winner was the longest by a Bears kicker since Paul Edinger hit from 54 yards to beat Detroit in the 2000 season finale. Piñeiro was rewarded a few days later by being named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week. Considering everything that had happened at the kicker position over the previous nine months, you couldn’t have scripted it much better. For one glorious September afternoon in Denver, there was no kicking controversy, and no double doink. There was just Steady Eddy. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: Texans GM gives big praise to Dexter Lawrence
summary: If you just watched the box score of the Cincinnati Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, you wouldn’t think Dexter Lawrence II did very much. If you watched the game, however, you saw that the Bengals’ blockbuster trade for the defensive tackle already looks like a massive success. Lawrence was double-teamed on […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 13: Dexter Lawrence #97 of the Cincinnati Bengals walks off the field after 33-27 win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you just watched the box score of the Cincinnati Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, you wouldn’t think Dexter Lawrence II did very much. If you watched the game, however, you saw that the Bengals’ blockbuster trade for the defensive tackle already looks like a massive success. Lawrence was double-teamed on 80% of his snaps, per PFF, which helped open things up for his teammates. Those teammates sacked Baker Mayfield four times and contributed to four fumbles forced and recovered. The attention Lawrence requires impacts the game far beyond the stat sheet. Ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Houston Texans, Texans general manager Nick Caserio gave Lawrence his due praise and even compared him to an NFL legend at his position: Former Patriots All-Pro Vince Wilfork. “I think the Vince (Wilfork) comparison is probably pretty apt, just their athleticism. He’s a massive problem. When he’s going vertically, it’s hard to contain him,” Caserio said. “He’s been double-teamed more than any defensive tackle in the league. He presents a lot of problems. He has a very unique playing style. He and Vince have some similar attributes. “Those are two rare players with that kind of size to move the way they do.” Similar to Lawrence, Wilfork didn’t always stuff the stat sheet, but his impact on the game was felt each and every snap. Wilfork spent the 2015 and 2016 seasons with Houston, so Caserio got a close-up look at the dominance a player like that is capable of. The Bengals will be counting on Lawrence to have another dominant performance this week if they want to upset the Texans on the road and if they get it, the Bengal defense could give C.J. full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Josh Johnson (11) drops back to throw during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals are expecting Joe Burrow to start at quarterback vs. the Houston Texans on Sunday. But just in case, the team is protecting itself in the event another quarterback needs to suit up. On Saturday, the Bengals announced the elevation of quarterback Josh Johnson and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris from the practice squad to the active roster for Week 2. Giles-Harris and Johnson are both classified as standard elevations. As practice squad players being elevated to the active roster for the game, they will automatically revert to the practice squad on Monday. On Friday, head coach Zac Taylor said that the team could elevate Johnson even though they’re expecting Burrow to play as he deals with back tightness. If Burrow were to be a surprise inactive, Joe Flacco would get the start, while Johnson would be his backup. This elevation also means it’s possible that Johnson will be designated the emergency third QB for Sunday’s game. The designated emergency QB can only enter the game if the first two active quarterbacks are injured, ejected, or undergoing an injury evaluation. Let’s hope it doesn’t come to that.

title: 4 key matchups to watch for Bengals vs. Texans
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Houston this Sunday to take on CJ Stroud and a very talented defense on the other side of the ball. That defense is coming off a performance in which they allowed 36 points against the Buffalo Bills. Will the Bengals do the same, or will the Texans bounce back? […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II (97) runs on the field before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Houston this Sunday to take on CJ Stroud and a very talented defense on the other side of the ball. That defense is coming off a performance in which they allowed 36 points against the Buffalo Bills. Will the Bengals do the same, or will the Texans bounce back? Let’s take a look at some of the key matchups in this one. Ja’Marr Chase vs. Derek Stingley This is a matchup of two of the best players at their respective positions. These guys are familiar with one another dating back to their LSU days. Chase is coming off a game in which he had just 2 catches for 12 yards. Stingley was credited with allowing 4 catches on 6 targets that came his way. That 66.7% completion rate is much higher than his career mark of 53.4%. With both players looking for a better performance than in Week 1, we could be in for some fireworks. Amarius Mims vs. Will Anderson Jr. Anderson was able to record .5 of a sack against Buffalo during week one. He is a player who has 30 sacks through his first 3 seasons in the league. He is one of the most explosive pass rushers in all of football. Meanwhile, Amarius Mims didn’t allow a single pressure against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Mims was tasked with going up against a talented rookie in Rueben Bain. While that was a fantastic performance, Anderson presents an even bigger challenge due to that aforementioned explosiveness. This titanic battle could go a long way in deciding which team comes out on top this weekend. It is important to note that the Texans will move their defensive ends around. Even when Mims is not facing Anderson, he will be going up against talented pass rushers like Danielle Hunter and Jadeveon Clowney for the Texans. Amarius Mims vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers pic.twitter.com/ehyW38iwIP — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 14, 2026 Texans running backs vs. Bengals linebackers Not a one-to-one direct matchup, but the running game of the Texans against the run defense of the young Bengals linebacker is a key matchup in this one for me. Barrett Carter looked like an improved player from his rookie season. However, he did still record 3 missed tackles. Demetrius Knight Jr. also recorded 3 missed tackles against Tampa Bay. They did combine for 15 tackles, with Carter adding half a sack on a play that Knight scooped and scored on. Carter would then go on to force a fumble at the goal line on Baker Mayfield, which was recovered in the end zone by Bryan Cook. The young Bengals linebackers will need to make sure they do not allow David Montgomery and Woody Marks to run wild this week. Montgomery finished Week 1 with 3 total touchdowns. He rushed for 60 yards and added another 19 receiving yards to go with it. Woody Marks was also able to rush for 42 yards against the Bills. Dexter Lawrence vs. Texans interior 0-line Lawrence didn’t stuff the stat sheet in Week 1, but he was all over the revamped Bengals defense. He was second on the team with 3 pressures during the game, and should have drawn several holding penalties against the Buccaneers offensive line. One of those non-penalties was when he almost had a sack on Mayfield, before Mayfield ultimately had the ball knocked loose by Barrett Carter. The Texans interior offensive line consists of Keylan Rutledge, Evan Brown, and Ed Ingram. Those three players will all take turns having their hands full with trying to slow down Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence’s impact will continue to free up his teammates, but I imagine Lawrence is hoping that this is the week he gets to unleash the Sexy Dexy dance for a sack celebration after coming so close during the first week. Dexter Lawrence vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Lawrence’s impact will not always show on the box score, but this is absolutely a difference maker on defense. pic.twitter.com/5ccswD2BDK — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 15, 2026

title: Bengals vs. Texans: 5 questions with Battle Red Blog
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are getting set for a big test in Week 2 against the Houston Texans. There are concerns on the injury front for the Bengals, and the Texans are hungry to get their first win in front of a home crowd. To help us get a lay of the land, we tapped the […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow runs the ball in the first quarter during the home opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals are getting set for a big test in Week 2 against the Houston Texans. There are concerns on the injury front for the Bengals, and the Texans are hungry to get their first win in front of a home crowd. To help us get a lay of the land, we tapped the knowledge of Scott Barzilla over at Battle Red Blog. Here are five questions we asked him ahead of the clash. 1.) What did you see from C.J. Stroud, in terms of improvement this summer and last week? I know there has been a contract impasse between him and the Texans—does he still feel like the long-term answer? SB: It’s always a mixed bag with Stroud. Overall, it was a really good performance, and it makes you feel good about him as a quarterback. He had a 106.5 rating and is on pace to have a 30-TD season. However, that was sandwiched by two fumbles that played a key role in the game. I don’t really blame him for the second fumble, but ball security is a huge issue. The question for the Texans long-term is how much they want to invest in a near-franchise quarterback, considering that they have committed so many resources to their defense. $60-million quarterbacks mean you have to save elsewhere, and there is still an open question as to whether he is good enough to elevate a flawed roster the same way the other elite quarterbacks do. As I sit here, I don’t know what the long-term answer is. He is certainly as good as many of the quarterbacks that have gotten paid, but he is not as good as others (say Joe Burrow), so it makes it an impossibly complicated question. 2.) Talk about the loss of Henry To’oTo’o this week, and its potential impact on this game. SB: I’m really worried that this team is already losing key starters to injury when the defense was very healthy last year. It is not as acute as when facing more mobile quarterbacks, but it still presents coverage issues because the Texans already have difficulties covering tight ends, and that is one more option taken away from them. I would bet pretty heavily on the over for Mike Gesecki receiving yards, as the Texans really don’t have a good answer for him with injuries they have already suffered to their linebacking core (they lost E.J. Speed in training camp). 3.) Much like the Bengals, questions about the Texans’ offensive line have been prevalent. They have made moves to remedy that—did it show up last week? SB: Keelan Rutledge may have been the steal of the draft. He was the only lineman to have a 70+ PFF rating last week at left guard. They are marginally better at center with Evan Brown than they were last season. The rest of the line is the same. In particular, the right side of their line struggled against Buffalo as Trent Brown and Ed Ingram got beat on some key plays. Ingram was solid last season, so we can hope that was a one-off. Brown was solid down the stretch, but there is very little chance he makes it through 17 games healthy. They signed Braden Smith in the offseason, and he is out with a plantar fasciitis injury. Hopefully, he will be able to return by week five, but that is the state of the line. So, overall they are improved, but there are still some holes that opponents can exploit. 4.) Who are a couple of X-Factors (maybe under-the-radar guys who could surprise) on Houston’s offense and defense for you this week? SB: On offense, the big key on Sunday will be the receiving core with Nico Collins out. Keyshon Boutte was acquired right before the end of the preseason, so he is probably still learning the playbook, but he is capable of making a big play or two. The rest will likely rest on their tight ends and Xavier Hutchinson. I like Jaylin Noel in the open field if they give him a screen or two, but the overall production from the receivers will be an issue. A deep cut could be Marlin Klein, their second-round pick. He has a ton of athleticism for a tight end, but is still raw. If he is guarded one-on-one by a linebacker or safety, it could be a mismatch. 5.) The line has hovered between 2.5-3-points in favor of the Texans, per FanDuel this week. What are your thoughts on that and how do you see this playing out? SB: I’m not comfortable going either way on this line. I just don’t have a good feel for the game. Like you, I think the over is as good a bet as could be had in this game. Both offenses can put points on the board, so someone is going off in this game. If you held a gun to my head, I would pick the Bengals and take the points. I am not touching this money line with a forty-foot pole on either side. I just don’t have a good feel for it, to tell you the truth. Our thanks to Scott Barzilla for the chat. Check out the other side of the conversation at Battle Red Blog .

title: Sunday Browns rumor: Shedeur Sanders’ time? Deshaun Watson’s final game?
summary: For Cleveland Browns fans, QB Deshaun Watson’s resume was full and faulty long before HC Todd Monken came in and gave everyone a clean slate. Almost no one was happy when Monken named Watson the Browns Week 1 starter, but the head coach has time and time again reinforced that he believes that decision is […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) and quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) before the game agains the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For Cleveland Browns fans, QB Deshaun Watson’s resume was full and faulty long before HC Todd Monken came in and gave everyone a clean slate . Almost no one was happy when Monken named Watson the Browns Week 1 starter , but the head coach has time and time again reinforced that he believes that decision is the right one for Cleveland. Then in Week 1, the Browns offense was putrid with Watson as the quarterback, with some game-breaking issues , but Monken was steadfast that Watson was his starter . The veteran QB blamed the media , and the head coach backtracked on whether the team’s opinion mattered . As we shared in this morning’s news wrap-up , our Daily Dawg Chow, there was a quick change in narrative around the quarterback position from Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com . Talking about Shedeur Sanders’ expectations and the possibility of a quarterback change after Week 2. Then, Sunday morning brought this report of a rumor from ESPN and The NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport: The #Browns plan to reevaluate the QB position after two road games in two weeks, and there is a variety of outcomes. But it could mean Shedeur Sanders’ time is coming in Week 3: https://t.co/MzYR5dqj9D https://t.co/MzYR5dqj9D — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 20, 2026 Rapoport noted that with Week 1’s bad loss and Cleveland having back-to-back road games, “the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point.” Given this report, it is likely that a bad game from Watson would see Sanders as the starter for the home opener, and could spell the end of Watson’s NFL career. If the veteran plays well, especially with an upset victory, Watson could stave off Sanders for a few more weeks. As Rapoport noted, “The middle ground is the area where it’s less clear cut.” To some extent, two games seem like a very short evaluation time for such an important decision. Would that timeline have been true if Sanders was named the starter to start the season? If Watson is benched and Dillon Gabriel returns from injured reserve, would the veteran Week 1 starter even dress for games the rest of the year? Would Taylen Green stay on the roster and be the emergency quarterback? Lots of questions that need to be answered, starting with Watson’s performance Sunday in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Given this report by Rapoport and the column by Cabot, it seems like Browns fans might get what they have wanted for a long time: No more Watson at quarterback. What will Sanders look like if/when he gets his shot? That is a question that might take a little time to answer. What do you think of the Browns evaluating the QB starter after 2 weeks? title: Browns vs. Buccaneers weather forecast calls for hot temps, possible thunderstorm
summary: The Cleveland Browns have a bit of a unique schedule this season. They don’t play any West Coast games, but they also began the season with two straight games in Florida. That means dealing with the summer heat and humidity. Last week’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars got them a taste of things, but will […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - DECEMBER 9: The grounds crew removes the tarp off the field at Raymond James Stadium after the rain before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers host the New Orleans Saints on December 9, 2018 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have a bit of a unique schedule this season. They don’t play any West Coast games, but they also began the season with two straight games in Florida. That means dealing with the summer heat and humidity. Last week’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars got them a taste of things, but will it be the same this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers? Pretty much. Per the Weather Channel, temperatures are expected to be in the high 80s at around 88 degrees, with the feels like temperature at 95 degrees. Wind is not expected to play a factor, but precipitation might. The forecast is currently calling for scattered thunderstorms around 4:00 pm ET. Now, last week, that wouldn’t have been an issue. Cleveland was beaten so badly and so quickly, that the game was over quickly — I think it was around 3:45 pm ET, which is crazy, as all of the other games still had the majority of the fourth quarter left to play. Originally, the forecast was projected that thunderstorm to play a factor in the 3:00 pm ET hour too. It’s only projected at 42%, so that is far from a guarantee. But, if the game ends up being a tight one down the stretch, it’s possible that weather could play a factor in the final moments of the game. For what its worth, Accuweather is calling for the thunderstorm chances to be closer to 5:00 pm ET. We’ll continue to monitor the forecast and the threat for inclement weather as gametime approaches.
