title: Browns fans don’t expect an improvement this week, due to worst QB situation in NFL
summary: After their loss to open the season, Cleveland Browns fans lost confidence in the direction of the team. Specifically, they had a decrease of 34 percentage points from week-to-week, dropping from 55% confidence to 21% confidence. I think fans were willing to deal with the usual frustrations from QB Deshaun Watson for a couple of […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - AUGUST 03: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns instructs Deshaun Watson #4 during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on August 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images After their loss to open the season, Cleveland Browns fans lost confidence in the direction of the team. Specifically, they had a decrease of 34 percentage points from week-to-week, dropping from 55% confidence to 21% confidence. I think fans were willing to deal with the usual frustrations from QB Deshaun Watson for a couple of weeks, with the assumption that QB Shedeur Sanders’ shot at starting again would come sooner rather than later. However, it’s one thing to lose a close game with bad quarterback play. It’s another thing to get completely blown out by the second quarter, with horrible defense all-around playing a factor in that blowout too. How can a team look so lost and uninspired in Week 1? We asked one other question this week, which asked if fans expected the Browns to at least have a better performance in Week 2 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I phrased the question in that way because I thought, “If I ask my usual question of who will win the game, 99% of people are going to vote Tampa.” I thought my phrasing would lend to more optimism, but only 29% of fans think that Cleveland will play better this week. The rest are expecting a rinse and repeat of the same degree of shitty football, as Todd Monken would put it. There was also a national poll this week that asked which team had the worst quarterback situation. There were some good contenders on the list — the Browns, Falcons, Dolphins, Vikings, and Patriots — but the Browns ran away with it easily at 67%, followed by the Falcons at 19%. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 8.5 point underdogs against the Buccaneers this week, with the over/under being 41.5.

title: College football’s top Cowboys draft targets in Week 3
summary: It’s never too early to prep your draft board. Today we look at the best college football matchups, where a future prospect lurks that could be on the Cowboys radar.  LSU at Ole Miss The best game of the weekend takes place in Oxford, where two unbeaten SEC teams meet on Saturday night. LSU has […]
full_text: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 5: Jordan Seaton #77 of the LSU Tigers in action against the Clemson Tigers at Tiger Stadium on September 5, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) It’s never too early to prep your draft board. Today we look at the best college football matchups, where a future prospect lurks that could be on the Cowboys radar. LSU at Ole Miss The best game of the weekend takes place in Oxford, where two unbeaten SEC teams meet on Saturday night. LSU has allowed only 94 rushing yards across its opening two games, while Ole Miss has scored 79 points. The game also puts two possible first-round linemen under the spotlight. Key Dallas Targets: LSU: Jordan Seaton, Offensive Tackle Seaton transferred from Colorado to LSU after establishing himself as one of the best young tackles in college football. The 6-foot-5, 330-pound left tackle started 13 games as a true freshman in 2024 and did not allow a sack across nine appearances last season before an injury ended his year. His best quality is how easily he moves for such a large player. Seaton has the quick feet to stay in front of fast edge rushers, but he can also use his size and strength to move defenders in the running game. He does not have to lean or reach for contact very often, which helps him remain balanced when a pass rusher changes direction. Why The Cowboys Care Offensive tackle will come up a lot in this series since it’s one of the biggest long-term questions on the Dallas roster. The Cowboys will undoubtedly look for better protection around Dak Prescott come draft season and Seaton has the talent to start immediately. Although there’s a chance he may be selected early in the first round, but his current stock value places him as a mid-to-late first-round prospect. Dallas owns Green Bay’s pick in the first round, but may have to move around if it believes Seaton can become the long-term answer at one of football’s most important positions. Ole Miss: Will Echoles, Defensive Line Echoles broke out in 2025 with 68 tackles, 11.5 tackles for loss, five sacks, 39 pressures and six batted passes. At 6-foot-3 and 315 pounds, he has the size to defend the run but enough athletic ability to create problems in the passing game. He plays with powerful hands and does a good job of keeping blockers away from his body. That allows him to see where the ball is going and move into the running lane. Echoles can also push the pocket directly towards the quarterback, preventing him from stepping forward when the outside pass rush arrives. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas has Quinnen Williams at the heart of its defensive front, but the depth around him is less secure. Otito Ogbonnia joined the Cowboys on a short-term contract, while the trades at the position changed the long-term picture at defensive interior. Echoles could play alongside Williams on passing downs or replace him for short periods without removing the threat of interior pressure. His ability to defend the run would also help keep blockers away from Dallas’ linebackers. He looks capable of becoming more than a limited rotational defender, which would make him an attractive early-round option. SMU at Louisville SMU and Louisville both enter this ACC contest with explosive offences. SMU is averaging 6.7 yards per play, while Louisville is producing 6.6. The most important scouting battle, however, will take place between SMU’s left tackle and Louisville’s leading pass rusher. Key Dallas Targets: SMU: P.J. Williams, Offensive Tackle Williams is a 6-foot-5, 306-pound senior with 29 career starts. He played right tackle in 2025 before moving to the left side this season and has not allowed a pressure across his first 57 pass-blocking snaps. He has real long arms and enough movement skills to guide quick defenders away from the quarterback. Williams also plays with patience rather than reacting too early and creating an easy route back towards the inside. In the running game, he uses his size to seal the edge and create space for the back. Williams allowed only two sacks across 448 pass-blocking snaps last season, but how Williams handles Ole Miss’ speed and power could have a large effect on his draft stock. Why The Cowboys Care Unlike Seaton, Williams will be more likely to be available after the opening part of the first round. That could make him a more realistic target if Dallas wants competition at tackle without using its highest selection at the position. His experience on both sides of the line would be valuable because the Cowboys have questions surrounding Terence Steele. Williams could compete for a starting place while also giving Dallas the flexibility to move him if an injury occurs. His experience and balanced skill set should appeal to a team that needs more dependable tackle play. Louisville: Clev Lubin, Edge Rusher Lubin was one of college football’s most disruptive pass rushers in 2025. He finished with 61 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss, 8.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and 64 pressures. His 92.6 PFF pass-rush grade showed that his impact went well beyond his sack total. He wins with a fast first step and the ability to turn speed into power. Lubin can attack either side of the offensive line, which makes it difficult for an offense to plan all its protection towards one area. He also plays with good effort and continues chasing the quarterback when his first move is stopped. Lubin has not recorded a sack through Louisville’s opening two games, although he has forced two fumbles. Beating Williams would show that last year’s production can continue against one of the better tackles in the country. Why The Cowboys Care Last week showed the Cowboys defensive line needs to get more pressure on the quarterback. Lubin could initially enter games in obvious passing situations before developing into a larger role and help create more pressure. His ability to line up on either side would give the Cowboys more freedom to create favourable matchups. Lubin could also play on the same passing downs as Gary and Ezeiruaku, giving Dallas another way to create pressure without sending an extra defender on a blitz.
author: Mike Poland

title: Important Cowboys vs Commanders storylines on Sunday
summary: I don’t think anyone expected things to go the way they did in the Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants game. Without dwelling too much on a game in the rearview mirror, the Dallas defense caught many by surprise considering the overhaul over the offseason. Guys like Jalen Thompson, Rashan Gary, and Caleb Downs were […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 19: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is brought down by Quan Martin #20 of the Washington Commanders during a game at AT&T Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images I don’t think anyone expected things to go the way they did in the Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants game. Without dwelling too much on a game in the rearview mirror, the Dallas defense caught many by surprise considering the overhaul over the offseason. Guys like Jalen Thompson, Rashan Gary, and Caleb Downs were supposed to usher in something different. Unfortunately, it was more of the same. Here’s the good news. It was Week 1. The Cowboys still have 16 regular-season games left, and they have plenty of time to turn things around. They have to do it in a must-win way this week against the Washington Commanders. Here are five points to watch for as the game kicks off on Sunday. First point: More of the same? Heading into their matchup with the Giants, one of last week’s five points was limiting Jaxson Dart in the running game. The Cowboys had 54 yards on the ground to Dart, averaging almost five yards per carry. Dart’s ability to scramble kept Dallas’ defense on the field, which we all know how that went. The Cowboys have another quarterback coming up on Sunday who can hurt them with his legs: Jayden Daniels. Last week against the Philadelphia Eagles, Daniels didn’t run for as many yards as Dart did in Dallas, but he was an effective runner when he had the opportunity or needed to make a play. He had five carries for 31 yards, averaging over six yards every time he would run. Dallas needs to make sure last week’s mistake doesn’t happen again, because it’ll lead to more of the same, with the Commanders extending drives and keeping the Cowboys offense on the sidelines. Second point: The terror twins or the DeVille twins Somehow, someway, the Cowboys need to get CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens the ball early and often against the Commanders. Brian Schottenheimer has talked about wanting to run the ball and set the tone, but the team’s real playmakers are on the outside. On a great day, both wideouts can have over 100 yards each and be a terror to opposing defenses. Against the Giants, it just seemed like Pickens and Prescott weren’t always on the same page, and we’ve seen how Lamb can take time to get going if things don’t go his way early in a game. The best version of Lamb and Pickens earned them the nickname “the terror twins.” That version of the duo needs to be on display vs. the Commanders’ smaller cornerbacks. Last year against the Commanders at AT&T Stadium, Lamb went for 110 receiving yards and Pickens had 85. Both players averaged over 20 yards per catch. What we don’t need to see are the DeVille twins, which, if anyone has seen the show Rugrats , you know what I’m talking about. Third point: A rookie DC in DC The Commanders have the same question at defensive coordinator as the Cowboys do: Is this moment too big for them? Head coach Dan Quinn went out and hired two first-time coordinators on both sides of the ball this offseason, which could make him look like a genius or get him fired. Washington’s DC should be a familiar name to Cowboys fans since he was in the running for the same position with Dallas: Daronte Jones. He spent most of his coaching career with the Minnesota Vikings and learned under Brian Flores over the last three seasons. Unlike Christian Parker, Jones was actually a defensive coordinator in college in 2021 for LSU. That was his only season holding the position. Against the Eagles, the Commanders defense looked good and got the Philly offense out of rhythm on multiple drives. However, a few explosive plays happened where it looked like the secondary didn’t know what was going on (sound familiar). It’ll be interesting to see the storylines coming out of the game because one of these teams will be 0-2, with a ton of questions surrounding their first-time defensive coordinators and whether they were the right guys for the job. Fourth point: Reading between the linebackers Before offseason training and the NFL draft, the Cowboys’ linebacking corps was seen as a glaring need, even with Jaishawn Barham and Dee Winters coming aboard. DeMarvion Overshown’s health was a question, and Dallas needed to keep developing second-year pro Shemar James. As time went on, the questions around linebacker seemed to shift towards the pass rush and secondary. We should have stuck with our first instincts. With Overshown leaving Week 1 with a hamstring injury that could cost him one to two weeks, the Cowboys linebacker room looks even thinner heading into Week 2. Barham could be called upon as the next man up with green-dot responsibilities , but with growing concerns about the defense’s ability to communicate calls properly, should a rookie be trusted to make the right calls? Dallas has Curtis Robinson and Justin Barron on the practice squad and could elevate one of them to the active roster for Sunday, but they aren’t on the same level as Overshown to fill the void. The Cowboys were impressed by what they saw from Barham all offseason and in the first preseason game. If that player is still there, which he should be, the Dallas defense will need him in a big way this weekend. Fifth point: Kicking and screaming No need to panic; this is an under-the-radar point my colleague RJ Ochoa brought up on Twitter . Dating back to last season, Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey has now missed a kick of some kind (field goal or extra point) in 3 straight games. This is the first time in his career he has a 3-game streak of such kind. Aubrey is one of, if not the best, kickers in the NFL. However, if the defense struggles to start the season and the offense needs to score as many points as possible in their opportunities, missing kicks can’t happen. Questions lingered about the special teams unit’s performance last year under Nick Sorensen, and doubt remains about his return this offseason. Sorensen stuck around, and so far, after one game, the special teams unit has not looked any better in year two. Aubrey signed a historic deal this offseason, and deservedly so. But if he starts missing critical kicks in games that could come down to three points, it could raise alarm bells about what’s happened to one of the league’s most clutch kickers.

title: Cowboys news: Jaishawn Barham to start at middle linebacker, wear green dot
summary: Despite a frustrating rookie debut, the Dallas Cowboys will give the green dot to linebacker Jaishawn Barham as he starts in place of the injured DeMarvion Overshown. Another rookie, safety Caleb Downs, performed very well against the Giants, but he’s looking to take his play to an even higher plateau. All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb […]
full_text: Despite a frustrating rookie debut, the Dallas Cowboys will give the green dot to linebacker Jaishawn Barham as he starts in place of the injured DeMarvion Overshown. Another rookie, safety Caleb Downs, performed very well against the Giants, but he’s looking to take his play to an even higher plateau. All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb didn’t have the performance in Week 1 he wanted, but he’s chomping at the bit to play inside AT&T Stadium this Sunday. Starting the season 0-2 in the NFL is all but a guarantee that a team won’t make the playoffs, and Dallas desperately wants to avoid that as well as getting a second loss in NFC East play. Why Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys trust rookie Jaishawn Barham in first start at MLB – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News Jaishawn Barham didn’t have the best game in his first taste of NFL action. However, with DeMarvion Overshown on the shelf, he’ll get the start on Sunday against the Commanders. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer made it official Friday when he named Jaishawn Barham the starting middle linebacker for the home opener against the Washington Commanders . Starter DeMarvion Overshown is out for the game with a hamstring strain, suffered in the season opener against the New York Giants. “He’s got great command of what we’re doing,” Schottenheimer said of Barham. “Again, had to get into a little teaching moment this morning on the radio. Again, the green dot, I think gets overblown at times, basically what you’re doing, you’re repeating the call and then you’re setting the fronts and all that. And then the entire defense needs to communicate.” Caleb Downs looking to build off NFL debut vs. Commanders – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Caleb Downs was among the best defensive players on the Cowboys in their loss to the Giants in Week 1. Now, as the Commanders come to Dallas, he wants to be even better. Cowboys first-round pick Caleb Downs rarely came off the field in his NFL debut last Sunday against the Giants, playing 60 defensive snaps and tallying seven tackles, three quarterback pressures and a sack. On Sunday, Downs will take the field for his first game at AT&T Stadium as a Cowboy, where he’s aiming to build off his start to the year. “Excitement, honestly,” Downs said about Sunday’s game. “It’s the best feeling to be able to play this game. There’s no really other way to feel about it then just straight joy. I’m excited to do that, and we’re excited to do what we need to do to get a win.” Cowboys looking to avoid the wrong side of history in Sunday’s home opener – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys will try to avoid an 0-2 start on Sunday. If not, history shows that they’ll likely be in for a long and disappointing season. Since 1990, only 35 of 287 NFL teams that have started 0-2 have made the playoffs. Of those 35 teams, only four have lost both games to divisional opponents. The Dallas Cowboys will look to avoid having to make that same kind of history this season, as they look to get in the win column for the first time against the Washington Commanders in the home opener on Sunday afternoon in Arlington. Dallas Cowboys’ Friday Injury Report Includes Two Sidelined Starters – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Dallas will be without a couple of key defenders this weekend. A few others dealing with ailments were full participants on Friday. Malik Hooker went down with a forearm injury, which was later deemed to be a fracture that would force him out for a few weeks. Also injured in the loss was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , who suffered a hamstring injury. Neither will play this weekend against the Washington Commanders , but the good news is that Friday’s injury report from practice is thin beyond Hooker and Overshown. CeeDee Lamb ‘can’t wait’ for chance to bounce back in home opener vs. Commanders – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Lamb only had 44 yards on five receptions against the Giants. With the Cowboys staring at an 0-2 hole, he’s ready to have his first big performance of 2026. “Can’t wait. Can’t wait,” the three-time All-Pro receiver said. “ I know the city gonna be rocking. The game iss gonna be fire. I can’t wait to just go out there and have everybody excited, score a couple of touchdowns and blow the roof off the place.” The urgency to dictate terms against the incoming Commanders must also fuel the Cowboys toward getting a fast start, something they failed to do by going three-and-out on their first offensive series from scrimmage at MetLife Stadium. 3 Keys: Big-play shots must return for Cowboys to beat Commanders – Reid D Hanson, Cowboys Wire There’s a lot that the Cowboys have to fix from their performance in their season opener. Here are three things that need to happen. Key No. 1: Stop the run Filed under, “easier said than done,” stopping the run has to be the first priority for the Cowboys this week. Washington ranked right around league average in rushing EPA last week, but they faced off against a talented Philadelphia defense and largely kept their biggest threat, Jayden Daniels, holstered and underutilized. The Commanders pose a much bigger threat on the ground than the numbers indicate, and the Cowboys have to be ready. Daily discussion question: What is the best way that tomorrow can go?

title: Broncos maintain a “high level of confidence and comfort” in OC and play-caller Davis Webb
summary: According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, a team source told him that the Denver Broncos maintain a “high level of confidence and comfort” in offensive coordinator and play-caller Davis Webb. NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport adds that the Broncos kept someone they believe is a rising star in the coaching world […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY , MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos works during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri on Monday, September 14, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, a team source told him that the Denver Broncos maintain a “high level of confidence and comfort” in offensive coordinator and play-caller Davis Webb. NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport adds that the Broncos kept someone they believe is a rising star in the coaching world and still believe it . The Denver Broncos maintain a “high level of confidence and comfort” in Davis Webb as their offensive playcaller heading into today’s game vs. the Jaguars. https://t.co/p48u6TXGXK — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 20, 2026 This offseason, Davis Webb was a wanted man in the NFL. After his work with Broncos quarterback Bo Nix, teams with coaching vacancies brought Webb in for multiple head coaching interviews. Once it became clear he wasn’t getting a head coaching job this offseason, multiple teams also showed interest in him as an offensive coordinator and play caller. However, he decided to return to the Broncos as their offensive coordinator, and in a surprising move, he was also handed play-calling duties by head coach Sean Payton. A lot was made of this move, and many were excited to see the changes and improvements Webb would bring to this offense. Well, it did not go as planned. Webb’s debut as an offensive coordinator and play caller was an epic failure . Nothing went right on Monday Night in Arrowhead vs. the Chiefs. Quarterback Bo Nix had one of the worst games of his career; the Broncos only had 6 rushing attempts at halftime, Jaylen Waddle finished the game with 1 catch for 2 yards, and their top-ranked offensive line struggled throughout the game. It was an ugly performance by the Broncos and a big step back from what we saw last season, specifically in the Divisional Round vs. the Buffalo Bills in the playoffs. This led many to speculate that Head Coach Sean Payton would take over play-calling duties sooner rather than later. However, Payton and the team came out in defense of Webb this week and now have this Sunday morning news dump report further defending their offensive coordinator and play caller. So, it sounds like the Broncos will be sticking with Webb as their play caller moving forward, at least for now. The Broncos are in a Super Bowl window and cannot have patience for a first-time offensive coordinator and play caller to go through growing pains and struggles early on. They are already 0-1 after an embarrassing blowout loss on Monday Night and face a tough Jaguars team that were the only team to beat the Broncos by double digits last season. If the offense struggles and the Broncos fall to 0-2 heading into a Sunday Night showdown vs. the Rams, things could get loud in Broncos Country. With that said, hopefully we see some growth and improvement from the Broncos offense (and defense) today vs. the Jaguars. A good showing and a big win at home vs. the Jags would silence all the doubters and get the Broncos Super Bowl hype train back on track. More struggles and a loss would have all of Broncos Country slamming the panic button. This is a big game for Webb and the Broncos, and hopefully, we are talking about a bounce-back win and performance and not another disappointing loss.

title: Broncos Country lost some faith after Denver lost to KC
summary: Wow. For the first time in a long time, our standing SBNation Reacts confidence poll elicited a very gloomy outlook from Broncos Country. Not even half believe the Denver Broncos are headed in the right direction after that embarrassment we called a football game on Monday Night Football. Now I’m one to overreact in the […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs stiff arms Alex Singleton #49 of the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wow. For the first time in a long time, our standing SBNation Reacts confidence poll elicited a very gloomy outlook from Broncos Country. Not even half believe the Denver Broncos are headed in the right direction after that embarrassment we called a football game on Monday Night Football. Now I’m one to overreact in the moment (just look at my game-day Twitter account), but losing one game — even in horrendous fashion — is still way too soon to lose confidence in the direction of the team. Unless you really think Sean Payton and his coordinators have no idea what they’re doing, the Monday night loss should be viewed for what it was — one really bad game. And until this team has a string of those, it seems a little premature to lose confidence in the overall direction. Let’s pump the brakes on that sentiment until we get a few more games on the season and can actually assess whether this team is falling off the rails. But complaining about and figuring out why the MNF was so atrocious is valid — making the results on our second poll of the week very understandable. And also pretty predictable. Talk all week since Monday’s game (and during it) has focused on Denver’s extremely poor tackling. “It’s all of the above. It’s technique, attention to detail,” head coach Sean Payton said about the reason for so many missed tackles. “It’s all of those things.” The coach wouldn’t give details on how the team plans to fix that issue, but he did plan to fix it. “I won’t get into the drills, and the sequencing of how we handled it, but we are fixing it,” he said. “Certainly there was a lot we had to clean up.” Defensive lineman Dondrea Tillman believes more tackling drills is the answer. “More hats around the ball. Everybody is making sure they’re running to the ball and working on their angles,” he said. “Honestly, just putting a body on a body instead of just wrapping up. You’ve got to put bodies on people.” All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain said the poor tackling overall can be blamed on poor effort and a lack of intention to hit and hit hard. “Tackling is one of those things where you have to be intentional with it. You have to bring pads, feet and you have to wrap your arms,” he said. “I just feel like we were assuming that the ball carrier was going to go down at the moment rather than finishing at the end of the day.” Edge rusher Que Robinson believes Surtain’s point is exactly what the problem was on Monday night. Players were going about 80% and couldn’t wrap up to bring guys down. “Instead of just chasing the ball and hoping we get them on the ground, we’ve got to be more intentional,” Robinson said.

title: Broncos RB R.J. Harvey is unlikely to play vs. the Jaguars
summary: According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, Denver Broncos running back R.J. Harvey is unlikely to play vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars later today. The second-year back was listed as questionable with a hamstring injury and had back-to-back limited practices to end the week, but he is expected to be sidelined for their Week 2 […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos runs with the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs during an NFL football game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, Denver Broncos running back R.J. Harvey is unlikely to play vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars later today. The second-year back was listed as questionable with a hamstring injury and had back-to-back limited practices to end the week, but he is expected to be sidelined for their Week 2 matchup. Broncos RB R.J. Harvey, listed as questionable for Sunday’s game vs. the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury, is unlikely to play, per source. pic.twitter.com/FuuvcZkIZl — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 20, 2026 This is a bit of a loss for the Broncos offense. Harvey is an explosive weapon out of the backfield and had 121 total yards and a touchdown on 9 touches vs. the Jaguars last season. Now, the Broncos will have to attempt to get their first victory of the season without Harvey on the field. With Harvey sidelined, look for starter JK Dobbins to be more involved this week. The veteran was out-snapped by Harvey last week, mostly due to game script, but I anticipate a heavy dose of the Broncos’ starting running back today. We should also see a good bit of rookie Jonah Coleman. He did not play much vs. the Chiefs, but he is expected to be the Broncos’ RB2 today behind Dobbins and should see a decent amount of playing time. With Harvey likely among the Broncos’ inactives, look for backup runner Tyler Badie to be active and play on third downs today. He was their trusted pass blocker last season and made the team again this season due to that skill set, so he should see a decent amount of playing time as well. After the Broncos failed to run the ball last week and struggled mightily on offense, I anticipate them putting an emphasis on the run game early in this one. We should see a heavy dose of Dobbins early on, with Coleman mixing in and Badie playing on key third downs as a pass blocker. Thankfully for the Broncos and Harvey, this doesn’t seem like a long-term injury. He was able to practice this week, so hopefully, he will be able to return to the field next Sunday Night vs. the Los Angeles Rams. However, hamstring injuries can be tricky and linger for a bit, so we will have to see how long this injury sidelines and limits Harvey moving forward.

title: Ultimate Fan: Last week’s reality check should serve Broncos well in home-opener
summary: It’s hard to believe it only took until Week 2 for Broncos Country to hit the panic button! Just kidding. It’s not surprising at all. And I’ll be the first to admit being among them. Last week’s pretend football game was atrocious and I am officially a little worried. But I’m not that worried because […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - DECEMBER 21: Quarterbacks coach Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos speaks to Bo Nix (10) during the first quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, December 21, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images It’s hard to believe it only took until Week 2 for Broncos Country to hit the panic button! Just kidding. It’s not surprising at all. And I’ll be the first to admit being among them. Last week’s pretend football game was atrocious and I am officially a little worried. But I’m not that worried because like our veteran Ultimate Fan, bill2975, points out: “They can’t be that bad two weeks in a row, can they?” No, they can’t. Well, they better not be. And I don’t think they will. Last week’s wake-up call to players and coaches, combined with playing in front of the Mile High crowd, should make for a much better Week 2! See you Sunday. Hear you Sunday. pic.twitter.com/neJKcxC38b — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 20, 2026 Week 2: Broncos v. Jaguars MHR – I hardly know where to start with last week’s game, but after several days and a few deep breaths, it seems ok to just ask, WTF happened? bill2975: Here’s what I posted after the Monday night game, “Reality check! The Broncos played a terrible game, so let’s do better next week. Good thing it’s Game 1, so the coaches will certainly have the team’s attention now. What the hell, we weren’t threatening the 1972 Dolphins, anyway.” MHR – Bo Nix didn’t look “bad” in my opinion but certainly looked rusty. Was it first-game-back-from-injury jitters? Was it prime-time in Week 1? Was it the O-line? Was it Arrowhead? Was it a new play-caller? Was it being a new dad and not having enough sleep? Are you concerned or do you believe it was just a one-off and he’ll be back on track this Sunday? bill2975: I hope the team got a good wakeup call after being humbled by a team they should have beaten, even if it was in a terrible place to play (KC – good BBQ but insufferable fans, aka zealots). Hope the team focused on how to tackle this week; they apparently missed that session last week, and the coaching didn’t help much as they frequently seemed out of position. Oh, hopefully McGlinchey plays better this week,which shouldn’t be difficult. MHR – Depending how you answered the previous question, what was going on with the offensive line on Monday Night? Nix seemed to be running away from trouble most of the game. How does our O-line protect Nix this week from a Jags’ D-line that got five sacks in week 1 (it was against the Browns, but still…)? bill2975:I’m not a football expert, but I wonder if trying to use the middle of the field on passes would have helped a lot. Maybe we could try that THIS week? MHR – Despite the promise of a better rushing attack, the Broncos once again failed “to establish the running game” (15 attempts for 61 yards, compared to 38 attempts by the Chiefs and 173 yards by KWIII alone!) Is this a failure of game planning or was it an issue with “taking what the defense gave us” and not having the right situation to run the ball? Or did we just get behind too early? bill2975:I vote for game planning being much of the problem. And not very many runs. Maybe the first series or two they should run, run, run. Hell, try the single wing offense, if necessary. Show the Jags something they don’t know how to handle. Maybe try the Eagles Tush Push approach every play until they stop it. MHR – Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton – WR1 and 2 – combined for…wait for it…3 catches for 13 yards. It seems like such an absurd stat I don’t even know what question to ask other than…why? bill2975:Wasn’t Nix running for his life much of the time? Try some quick, short passes over the middle after establishing the run game. MHR – Moving to Denver’s defense where we usually ask fun questions about dominance, what in the living hell was that tackling on Monday Night? Or should I say, non-tackling? It’s the most fundamental part of playing defense and our guys looked like my grad-school flag football team. Do you expect them to be back on track this week? bill2975:See my comments above. Maybe they planned a practice session on how to block and tackle, but didn’t get to the latter piece. Good thing we weren’t flying to Australia and back. 🗣️Vance Joseph on watching film from the 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs: "It was like 145 yards after contact…once you watch it, it makes you sick." #broncoscountry pic.twitter.com/qG9oeNSlQI — Guerilla Sports (@guerillasports) September 18, 2026 MHR – Trevor Lawrence has had his ups and downs, but he has hung in there at Jacksonville and last year proved he has staying power in this league. What concerns you the most about him on Sunday? Can Nik Bonitto and Que Robinson and/or Jonah Elliss rattle him enough to keep from getting quick scores? bill2975:Disclaimer – I’ve always liked Trevor Lawrence, and I expect him to be really good on Sunday. Sure would be nice to see the edge rushers get close to him, though, and throw him off his game. MHR – Like Denver, Jacksonville has a slew of decent running backs, but no superstar like KWIII (hopefully!) But Denver’s run defense is still a concern. How do they stop Tuten, Abdullah and Rodriquez – a trio that combined for 121 yards last week? bill2975:Is John Franklin Myers available this week? Oh, you say he moved on? Well, crap… MHR – Looking at the Jacksonville receivers, Parker Washington had a field day against the Browns with 83 receiving yards while Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr. combined for another 80 yards. Will the defensive backs answer Pat Surtain’s call for better “intention” to tackle this weekend? How will our DBs stack up against their WRs? bill2975:I’d be shocked if our DBs had a second bad game in a row on Sunday. Linebackers, though? Eh… MHR – Our best player on Monday was Jeremy Crawshaw, the punter. Which one player/unit on both sides of the ball needs to have a great game this weekend to help the Broncos beat the Jags? bill2975:Riley Moss and Ja’Quan McMillian. I don’t worry very much about Pat. And, Zach Allen’s friends on the DL have to try to make Trevor’s life miserable, too. (Hm.. that’s more than one!) MHR – Aside from obviously coming away with a win, what would you most like to see from the team this week that would indicate progress and a promising season overall? bill2975:Honestly, what I care about is seeing a well-played, well-fought, penalty-free game with several exciting plays. I’d like to see a win, particularly in Denver, but let’s turn things around and get going in the right direction. Davis Webb said his offensive performance against the Chiefs was not good enough and he’s not proud of it pic.twitter.com/3mWYJX7gI4 — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) September 18, 2026 Predictions Stats for BO NIX? Enough to win the game. Stats for each Broncos RB? How about 4+ YPC or better for each one, and enough run plays to matter. Number of yards receiving/TDs for each of the receivers? I vote for at least 180 yards total. How many points for Lutz this week? 3 PATs, 2 FGs. Number of sacks to Trevor Lawrence? 3-4 Broncos player with the most tackles? Sigh, Singleton, preferably at the line of scrimmage. Maybe Murdock, if he’s playing. Who gets the first sack of the game for the Broncos? Bonitto. Who gets the most sacks? Bonitto, tie with Allen and Hufanga. How many INTs/FF/FR for the Jaguars’ D? None How many INTs/FF/FR for the Broncos’ D? More than None. How many penalties between the two teams? Way too fricking many! The Favorites Favorite Broncos win ever? Demarius’ walkoff TD against Steelers Favorite John Elway win outside of the Super Bowls? “The Drive” – 1987 Favorite Peyton Manning win? Broncos 49, Ravens 27; Peyton 7 TDs. Vinovich revenge… Team you love to beat the most in the AFC West? Tie – Chefs, Faders, Charge-its Coach you laugh at the most in the NFL? Mike McDaniel Coach you most want to throat…

We lit up Davis Webb, but Nix left a lot of big plays on the field by turtling up after that early interception. We’ll need to see a lot more confidence from him in Week 2 and Webb needs to commit to the run game a little earlier in this game. title: Broncos defense focused on fixing issues against Jaguars
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos defense had some serious issues in the opener. Namely, the Broncos couldn’t tackle. For an NFL team, it was startling, to say the least. For a defense that was one of the best in the NFL and has sights on that again, it was dumbfounding. Even now. Denver […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs the ball against the Denver Broncos during the first quarter in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos defense had some serious issues in the opener. Namely, the Broncos couldn’t tackle. For an NFL team, it was startling, to say the least. For a defense that was one of the best in the NFL and has sights on that again, it was dumbfounding. Even now. Denver looked like a Pee-Wee team the first time it strapped on pads. Now comes the Jacksonville Jaguars, who embarrassed this same defense last season and should follow the Kansas City Chiefs’ attack plan. Run the ball until the Broncos prove they can stop it and tackle. When asked about the issues from the opener, defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said to the media on Friday: “I saw missed tackles. Just fundamentals, block destruction, open-field tackling angles, those things. Obviously, leaving camp, you would think those things would be fixed and correctable. They are, but it was too much on Monday night. So many explosive plays that came from missed tackles and just simply block destruction, so we have to fix that. We’ve got to work on that. I think time on task and just practicing better, that will get better. “(It was) disappointing, obviously, that we played that way in that part of our game. It wasn’t a bunch of mental mistakes or blown coverage, those things. It was just mostly fundamentals, and for me as a coach, that’s disappointing.” Whether these issues are correctable in a short week remains to be seen. However, these are correctable. Tackling is not about talent; it’s about effort and want-to. Similar to boxing out for rebounds in basketball. It starts with how the Broncos did the work in practice this week. 🏡 sweet 🏡 pic.twitter.com/ISQrRmHZl6 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 19, 2026 “We definitely have self-awareness on our side of the ball,” Joseph said to the media on Friday. “I don’t have to walk in and give a speech after a game like that. They watched the game immediately after the game on the bus and on the plane. Once we landed, everyone knew what the issues were. “It was like 145 yards, I think, after contact. So we felt it during the game, but once you watch it, it makes you sick. We have a self-aware group. We don’t have to walk in and show the tape and say, ‘Guys, this is what happened.’ They know what happened, and we’ve worked on fixing those issues, and again, we’ll see how it falls on Sunday.” Added cornerback Pat Surtain II: “I think it just all goes in towards effort. Tackling is one of those things where you have to be intentional with it. You have to bring pads, feet, and you have to wrap your arms. I just feel like we were assuming that the ball carrier was going to go down at the moment rather than finishing at the end of the day. Hats off to them as well. They were running the ball very hard, but we know we’re better than that defensively, and we’re just going to correct it and move forward with it.” In terms of motivation, Denver doesn’t have to look far to find it. The Broncos have the performance in the opener paired with what happened the last time these two teams. Plus, it’s the home opener in front of the Rocky Mountain Thunder. “It’s significant to defend your home field, and the fans absolutely make a difference,” Broncos head coach Sean Payton said to the media on Friday. “All these problems, let’s say from a week ago for us offensively with crowd noise, get off, cadence, what you do with motions, they all become much more challenging when you’re off a silent snap count. “So when you’re at home, obviously, the defense has to work through the communication, but it’s a significant advantage. Our crowd last year, we feed off that. So when the quarterback’s in the huddle and there’s stress, ‘What was that snap count?’ Or, ‘What was the end of that play?’ That’s problematic.” Broncos links

title: Broncos vs. Jaguars score predictions for Week 2
summary: After a brutal start to the season, the Denver Broncos are looking to right the ship in Week 2 at home against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It’s not going to be easy to do as these same Jaguars were the only team last season that beat the Broncos soundly and they did in Denver’s backyard. However, […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - DECEMBER 21: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after throwing a touchdown pass during the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a brutal start to the season, the Denver Broncos are looking to right the ship in Week 2 at home against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It’s not going to be easy to do as these same Jaguars were the only team last season that beat the Broncos soundly and they did in Denver’s backyard. However, after being totally embarrassed on national television last week, I would expect the Broncos to come out with plenty of fire and passion for this game. Game Overview Denver Broncos vs. Jacksonville Jaguars Sunday, September 20, 2026 at 2:05 P.M. Mile High time Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado ATS Betting Lines: Denver -2.5 Moneyline Odds: Denver -148 / Jacksonville +126 Over/Under: 45.5 Note: All odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Collectively, our Mile High Report staff is predicting a Jaguars 24-19 win over the Broncos. The doomers overcame the bounce-back believers on staff today. Here’s who to disagree (or agree) with in the comments: Broncos 30, Jaguars 16 It’s doom and gloom in Broncos Country after one bad game and they may very well lose this one too given Sean Payton’s track record in September. That said, I think maybe they might be a little pissed off by the way things went down on MNF to open the season and they’ll come out here and punch the Jaguars in the mouth on Sunday giving all the doomers a week to think about how silly their overreactions were after one game. – Tim Lynch Jaguars 27, Broncos 12 The Broncos defense is lost. They are facing a Jaguar team that is a far more complete opponent than who they faced last week. The offense looks disjointed and in need of a few weeks to get online. I think I’ll be optimistic and call the Broncos only losing by 2 scores. – Sadaraine Jaguars 27, Broncos 20 I usually try to be optimistic about the Broncos. Alas, after their brutal loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, I am not sure they are going to be able to rebound on a short week. They seemingly have way too many issues to fix. Jacksonville is a good team. Trevor Lawrence is playing well, and they have an opportunistic defense that is great at stopping the run. All things considered, I believe the Jaguars will find a way to topple the Broncos in Week 2. I hope I’m wrong. – Chris Hart Jaguars 24, Broncos 13 The week 1 loss to the Chiefs has most of us really struggling with the identity of this team. I would like to think that Week 1 is still just a glorified preseason game, but that was ugly. Jacksonville could present another difficult task, and beat up on a well prepared Broncos team last year. It’s hard to feel confident in this team right now, so I won’t try and be Johnny Sunshine here. It’s gonna get worse before it gets better. – Adam Malnati Jaguars 31, Broncos 10 Trevor Lawrence has been on fire recently. Since week 10 of last year, he’s scored four more total touchdowns than any other QB, is first in passer rating and 3rd in yards per attempt. Last week he picked up where he left off and continued looking dominant, so Denver’s defense has their work cut out for them. Ordinarily, I’d say after a performance like last week, the Broncos will have a bounce back get right game after going from a top unit last season to being embarrassed in primetime. However, I don’t think this is the QB or game to get right and I think the panic continues for at least another week as the offense continues to sputter and the defense can’t overcome the hot Jaguars. – Jeff Essary Broncos 27, Jaguars 20 If not just for saving this thread, but this is a week to week league. Yes, the Broncos were embarrassed in KC. Even more motivation is Denver was embarrassed by the Jags at home last season. Every issue Denver faces is correctable. This isn’t rocket science. And tackling is not connected to talent, it’s about effort. I have no doubt that Payton and the leaders had their come to Jesus meeting on Tuesday. As Nix said after the game, the Chiefs loss was a nasty wake up call. The Broncos got the alert and will respond on Sunday. The defense will look like the defense that was atop the league last season, and Nix and the offense will play with way more consistency, execute better, and run the ball. – Ian St. Clair What is your score prediction for the Broncos-Jags game? Let us know in the comments section below.

summary: The Denver Broncos looked absolutely dreadful in their Week 1 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Whether it was on offense or defense, nothing seemed to click or go right for them. This weekend, they host the Jacksonville Jaguars who are 1-0 to start the season after beating the Cleveland Browns last Sunday. In order […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) hands off to Denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins (27) during the second half against the Kansas City Chiefs on September 14th, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos looked absolutely dreadful in their Week 1 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Whether it was on offense or defense, nothing seemed to click or go right for them. This weekend, they host the Jacksonville Jaguars who are 1-0 to start the season after beating the Cleveland Browns last Sunday. In order for the Broncos to have a shot at defeating the Jaguars, these three players have to perform at a high level. J.K. Dobbins — Running Back Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb opted with the bold strategy of barely running the ball on the road at Arrowhead on Monday Night Football . That put an immense amount of pressure on Bo Nix, who wound up struggling and having one of his worst games of his career. This Sunday, establishing the run has to be a focal point of their offensive plans. The Jaguars boast a strong defensive line that is extremely good stopping the run. However, the Broncos have to try and get their ground game going if they want any chance at winning on Sunday. J.K. Dobbins was out due to injury in last year’s loss against Jacksonville. Denver spent all offseason trying to revitalize and improve their rushing attack—let’s see them try and enforce that. If RJ Harvey is dinged up and not available to go due to a hamstring issue, rookie running back Jonah Coleman should see his first carries of the regular season. Courtland Sutton — Wide Receiver Last week against the Chiefs, I noted Jaylen Waddle as a player that needed to have a huge game. Unfortunately, Denver’s prized trade acquisition had one catch for two yards. That’s simply unacceptable. Courtland Sutton also failed to make an impact and had just two catches for 11 yards. This week, Sutton has to rise to the occasion and make an impact in the Broncos’ passing game. In last year’s matchup, Sutton led the Broncos with six receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown. He will have to be at his best to give Denver a chance to win. Whether it’s a touchdown catch or reverting back to form and being a chain-moving machine, the receiver corps elder statesman has to play at a high level. Of course, that also means Bo Nix has to do a better job at quarterback. The Broncos’ aerial attack can’t be flat for the second game in a row. Enough of the slow starts. Alex Singleton — Linebacker Truth be told, you could insert almost any player on defense as someone to watch and hope they improve drastically after what happened against the Chiefs. The defensive line was overmatched, the edge rushers failed to get adequate pressure, and several members of the Broncos’ secondary had a rough outing. For Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, I’m choosing inside linebacker Alex Singleton. His agent went to social media to blast fans and writers for criticizing the team. After the game, Singleton’s comments rubbed a lot of folks across Broncos Country the wrong way. I expect team captains to be more accountable than that. Liam Coen loves to diversify his personnel groupings, work in a lot of motion, and do whatever it’s necessary to try and confuse opposing defenses pre-snap. He also likes to utilize running backs in the passing game. I think that will pose a challenge for Singleton who has struggled with the latter on more than one occasion. Will he rise up to the challenge and play better on Sunday? You’ll just have to tune in and find out.

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 3 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Happy Saturday, Broncos Country. Welcome to another edition of Future Broncos. A lot of you had some great insight on prospects and questions for me after last week’s installment. Feel free to keep giving your opinions on the players I discuss, as well as any other prospects that have caught your eye early on in […]
full_text: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 29: Kj Duff #8 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights looks on against the Penn State Nittany Lions at SHI Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Piscataway, New Jersey. The Penn State Nittany Lions defeated the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 40-36. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Saturday, Broncos Country. Welcome to another edition of Future Broncos . A lot of you had some great insight on prospects and questions for me after last week’s installment. Feel free to keep giving your opinions on the players I discuss, as well as any other prospects that have caught your eye early on in the collegiate football season. Here are three more prospects to watch this week—all at different positions than I’ve discussed prior. Clev Lubin — Edge Rusher — Louisville The Broncos are beginning their 2026 regular season without multi-year starter Jonathon Cooper in the fold. Who knows when he will be back this year, and it’s anyone’s guess how things will shake out with the ongoing legal process related to his off-the-field issues that transpired this summer. That is giving players like Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman some extended reps to see how they perform. In turn, it will be helpful for the coaching staff to evaluate their future potential. Pending the outcome of Cooper’s situation and how the aforementioned trio perform, edge rusher could be in play early on for the Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. One player I’m keeping tabs on is Louisville edge rusher Clev Lubin . He initially started his collegiate football career at Army in 2022 but was redshirted the entire year. The next season, he transferred to Iowa Western where he posted 55 tackles, 23.5 tackles for loss, and 11.5 sacks. His top-notch play led him to the Sun Belt conference with Coastal Carolina for the 2024 season. He notched 44 tackles, 12 tackles for loss, and 9.5 sacks in 2024. Last season, Lubin earned third-team All-ACC honors after posting 61 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss, and 8.5 sacks for the Cardinals defense. So far in 2026, Lubin has been quiet with respect to sacks . However, he has continued his penchant for forced fumbles with two on the season—bringing that total to 12 in just over four seasons of play. He has totaled over 110 pressures the past 25 games which ranks third in the NCAA in that timeframe. If Denver wants to bolster their pass rush, he is a player for them to consider. As of now, a lot of outlets have him ranked as a Top 75 player. You can catch him in action when the 23rd ranked Cardinals host the 16th ranked SMU Mustangs this afternoon on ESPN2. KJ Duff — Wide Receiver — Rutgers The Broncos revamped their wide receiver core this offseason making a big trade for Jaylen Waddle. However, he failed to make an impact in his first game with the Broncos, and no other receiver stood out in Denver’s woeful aerial attack on Monday Night Football versus the Kansas City Chiefs . Courtland Sutton has had an impressive career in Denver. However, with a huge cap hit the next several seasons and only continuing to get older, there is a shot the Broncos opt to move on from him at the end of the season. I’m not sure there is anyone in the fold on their current roster who can replace him. Sure, the Broncos are going to try and feature Pat Bryant a lot this season. Though I believe Denver can’t bank on him being the heir to Sutton. They certainly need to add to the room. That’s where Rutgers standout KJ Duff comes into play. At 6’5” and 225 pounds, Duff boasts the physical profile Head Coach Sean Payton covets at the position. As a freshman, Duff played in thirteen games for the Scarlett Knights and came down with 27 receptions for 42 yards and 1 touchdown. Last season, he really took off and reeled in 60 receptions for 1,084 yards and 7 touchdowns. Rutgers has struggled out the gate during their ’26 season, but Duff has been a bright spot . In their two losses, he already has 17 receptions for 333 yards and 5 touchdowns. He impresses with his contested catch ability and dominance in the red zone. He is only a junior, though the Scarlett Knights’ quarterback situation will almost have him declaring early to take his talents to the NFL. Does that seem like something the Broncos could use for their offense moving forward? Absolutely. If he continues to dominate, I have no doubt he will merit first round consideration next April. You can catch Duff in action this afternoon when Rutgers hosts 12th ranked USC. Greg Johnson — Offensive Lineman — Minnesota Virtually every outlet had the Broncos’ offensive line ranked as the top, or at least near it, entering the 2026 season. Though I felt their play against the Chiefs left a lot to be desired. That made me think about what the overall future might be for the unit. The Broncos drafted Boise State’s Kage Casey in the fourth round in the 2026 NFL Draft. Casey has the potential to be a future starter at left guard and also saw some reps during training camp at center. However, his addition to the line shouldn’t preclude Denver from making draft day investments on the offensive line in ‘27. One prospect down the highway from me is Minnesota senior offensive lineman Greg Johnson . Johnson appeared in just two games as a freshman. Since then, has been a key cog in P.J. Fleck’s offensive line for the Golden Gophers with over 1,900 starting reps under his belt. In 2024, Johnson was a thirteen-game starter at center. Last season, he started all thirteen games again with 11 at left guard, one at right tackle, and another at left tackle. This year, he will be manning down the left guard position for Minnesota and hopes his high level of play can make him an early round draft pick. At 6’6” and 325 pounds, Johnson is an imposing player in the offensive trenches. He is a big reason Minnesota’s ground game has been strong. Quite simply, he is an absolute bully with elite strength to level defenders while paving the way for Minnesota’s backs. He has performed well protecting Drake Lindsey the past two seasons. I wouldn’t be the least bit surprised if Johnson winds up being a Top 32 selection next Spring. He has positional flexibility and the talent to be a Day 1 starter on any offensive line in the NFL. You can watch him when the Golden Gophers host the Akron Zips this morning.

title: Discussion: What gives you hope about the 2026 Detroit Lions?
summary: Things have gotten a little dark around here since Thursday night. Of course, all of that is warranted. The Lions may have been underdogs against the Buffalo Bills, but there was an expectation for them to fight better than that. Falling behind 21-0 and showing no life of defense was undoubtedly a concerning development, especially […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell reacts to a play against Buffalo Bills during the first half at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, NY, on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Things have gotten a little dark around here since Thursday night. Of course, all of that is warranted. The Lions may have been underdogs against the Buffalo Bills, but there was an expectation for them to fight better than that. Falling behind 21-0 and showing no life of defense was undoubtedly a concerning development, especially off the heels of nearly blowing a 21-0 lead of their own. But we’ve spent plenty of time, space , and breath on the serious concerns about the defense . Let’s spend some time talking about the positives for a minute, because this is far from a lost season just two weeks into the year. So today’s Question of the Day is: What gives you hope about the 2026 Lions? My answer: I still feel pretty darn good about the Lions’ offense. I think offensive coordinator Drew Petzing has designed some creative and effective plays in both the run and the pass game. That’s been especially true in the red zone, where the Lions have converted nine trips into seven touchdowns. And while the run defense took a significant step back from Week 1 to Week 2, I feel confident that when/if the offensive line gets healthy, they’ll be just fine on that front. Jahmyr Gibbs still looks like an absolute stud, and Detroit is finding ways to get him more involved in the passing game, as well. Jared Goff is still playing at a very high level, Amon-Ra St. Brown has looked uncoverable at times, and Sam LaPorta looks like himself after last year’s scary back injury. If the Lions offense can continue to average 31 points a game (or close to it), they will be in every game this season, even if the defense can’t find a way to improve. summary: The NFL releases its list of fines every Saturday afternoon for the previous week’s infractions. For Week 1 of the 2026 season, the NFL announced 20 different fines across 16 games. In Detroit Lions vs. New Orleans Saints, there was just one fined infraction: a lowering-of-the-helmet violation by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. The foul, […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) breaks a tackle attempt by New Orleans Saints cornerback Quincy Riley (29) to score a touchdown during the third quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The NFL releases its list of fines every Saturday afternoon for the previous week’s infractions . For Week 1 of the 2026 season, the NFL announced 20 different fines across 16 games. In Detroit Lions vs. New Orleans Saints, there was just one fined infraction: a lowering-of-the-helmet violation by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. The foul, which was not called a penalty on the field, occured on Gibbs’ 1-yard touchdown run in the third quarter that gave the Lions a 13-0 lead in the game. Gibbs took the handoff, bounced outside, and lowered his helmet into the neck/chest area of Saints cornerback Quincy Riley. You can see the replay below: #Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs was fined $23,027 for use of the helmet on this play. He was not flagged. pic.twitter.com/SyadclKrg9 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) September 19, 2026 If you’re wondering what is illegal about that play, here’s the relevant rule in the NFL’s official rulebook: [Rule 12, Article 10] IMPERMISSIBLE USE OF THE HELMET. It is a foul if a player: (a) lowers his head and makes forcible contact with his helmet against an opponent This was a new rule the NFL added in 2023 as an effort to protect players’ health. Previously, it had been a common occurrence for running backs to lower their head in order to get lower than the defender, gain leverage, and physically blow through contract. That naturally led to a lot of violent collisions, particularly to the head. “That will have the longest lasting impact,” the NFL’s executive vice president, communications, public affairs and policy Jeff Miller said of the new rule when installed . “You can’t use your helmet to hit somebody in the head. The goal is to change the culture.” If there were any fines from the Lions vs. Bills game on Thursday night, the NFL will reveal them next Saturday.

title: Discussion: What should the Detroit Lions do to fix their defense?
summary: The Detroit Lions defense is a major problem. I could use the next 500 words to lay out all the data to support that statement, but you all have eyeballs. You saw what happened in the second half against the New Orleans Saints. You witnessed Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills move through the Lions’ […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions reacts against the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions defense is a major problem. I could use the next 500 words to lay out all the data to support that statement, but you all have eyeballs. You saw what happened in the second half against the New Orleans Saints. You witnessed Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills move through the Lions’ defense like a knife through butter…. melted butter. The good news is that it’s early in the season, and there is plenty of time to make adjustments, change personnel, or do whatever it takes to get this defense on track to… not be the worst defense in the NFL. So today’s Question of the Day is: What is the first thing you’d do to fix the Lions defense? My answer: I’m going to address the obvious up top, because I assume this is going to be a popular answer: the Lions won’t and shouldn’t fire defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard right now. Don’t get me wrong, I think Sheppard is largely to blame for the unit’s struggles right now and his seat should be, at least, heating up. I’ll go more into that in a second. But as coach Dan Campbell pointed out on Monday before the game, Detroit didn’t have any time to make any serious corrections from Week 1 on a short week. You have to at least give Sheppard the chance to go over the tape, come up with some solutions, and try to implement those over the next couple weeks. How Detroit started the season is absolutely unacceptable, and that’s why Sheppard’s seat should be warm, but not giving him the opportunity to adjust and adapt is silly. That’s what the first month of the season is all about. And that’s not even touching the topic of who else on staff is even capable of taking over. But let’s put that aside and go with my proposed solution: simplify everything. This offseason, Sheppard and company went out and made some significant changes to the scheme. While the overall principles are the same, Sheppard added a lot of window dressing. Defensive lineman are stunting and stemming a lot more. The back end is disguising their coverages with inverted looks and a much healthier mix of man and zone. Defensive linemen are regularly dropping into coverage, and defensive backs are blitzing the quarterback and extremely high rates. On the surface, those sort of changes were welcomed. The Lions defense was stale and passive last year. Changes needed to be made, and I was excited to see how it all played out. After all, it was a promising training camp for that unit. But through two weeks, it’s clear these players are not currently capable of running this much flash and flare. They are few reasons for that. Maybe they’re not understanding basic principles. Maybe it’s just too much on their plate. Or maybe it’s just not being taught well enough. It would be one thing if it was one player or one unit that was making the mental mistakes. But it’s everyone . Trusted veterans like Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox are making poor reads. Jack Campbell—who is this defense—is off to a miserable start. Aidan Hutchinson is jumping into the wrong gaps. When literally everyone is making mental errors, you’ve overloaded them—forcing them to play slow and reactive rather than fast and proactive. Overthinking is a death sentence on defense, and so it’s on Sheppard to pare this thing down considerably. Give the secondary simpler rules and keys to deal with. Allow the defensive linemen to hone in on the things they do well, rather than focusing on trying to confuse quarterbacks with endless combinations. Maybe later in the season when some of the basics are set Detroit can expand upon what they do best, but it’s clear they’re too occupied mentally to perform well right now. title: Lions defense fails to deliver on Kelvin Sheppard’s offseason commitments
summary: The Detroit Lions could not get out of their own way in an embarrassing 41-31 loss to christen the Buffalo Bills’ new Highmark Stadium. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is very direct with his players and staff when leading his defense. I think he would appreciate fair and respectful directness in return. Dan Campbell did not […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard speaks before OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, June 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions could not get out of their own way in an embarrassing 41-31 loss to christen the Buffalo Bills’ new Highmark Stadium. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is very direct with his players and staff when leading his defense. I think he would appreciate fair and respectful directness in return. Dan Campbell did not mince words at half time. "The little shit is killing us right now." – Dan Campbell — Pride of Detroit (@PrideOfDetroit) September 18, 2026 The presnap penalties are infuriating for all head coaches. But what is most infuriating to me about Thursday night’s performance was that the Lions defense failed miserably in three distinct areas of the game that second-year defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard put an emphasis on fixing this off season. Explosive plays Run defense Third-and-long situations Three commitments from Sheppard. Three failures against the Bills. 1. Explosive plays: “unacceptable” The first commitment for correction this off season was to reduce the high number of explosive plays the defense gave up in 2025. “It’s the first thing we started self-scout with, and there was overlap because you go to then doing a self-scout and we’re gonna watch it again,” Sheppard said . “And when the players come in Phase Two, Phase Three, guess what? I got 105 plays, and we gonna watch them again, and when we get to training camp and we need general reminders and subtle reminders of what to do in certain situations, we gonna watch them again.” Well, explosive plays were an issue as the Bills generated eleven explosives to the Lions five. Below is a 25-yard pass in the first quarter that simply cannot happen. It appears Sheppard calls a Cover 3 zone, but disguises with split safeties presnap. Thomas Harper, the safety at the top of the screen, sits on the snap and is responsible for the outside-1 wide receiver in-break. We can see this with cornerback Rock Ya-Sin points this communication at the break for Harper. Credit to the Bills, they are in a good concept to attack Cover 3 with tight end Dalton Kincaid attacking the seam. One issue that makes this completion easier for quarterback Josh Allen is that the hook zone player in that seam is defensive end DJ Wonnum while linebacker Jack Campbell replaces with the rush. As a result, Wonnum cannot get enough depth in his drop to make that seam through a tighter window. Now, we do not know Harper’s rules and keys for the play, or whether he should have subtle awareness that the scheme called for Wonnum to drop and play the seam tighter before breaking into his responsibility. But these subtleties may be the difference between having a young Thomas Harper compared to Brian Branch. In the meantime, these are problems the Lions need to clean up on the back end. Dan Campbell: "We've got to clean up a lot of things on defense right now, particularly in the back end." — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) September 18, 2026 2. Run defense: “it starts there” “We have to get back to playing elite run defense here because to me it starts there,” Sheppard said . “So, guys are going to go in and they’ve already been told we will get back to playing elite run defense here. And it starts with the front seven. It starts when the pads come on and it starts there.” This is the area of the game that I was most disappointed in. The Lions run a stunt up front in one of their new looks implemented this offseason . A critical element of this is that while the stunts wipe blocks and change gaps for the offensive line, linebackers must fill and replace the gaps that are moved. Here, we see a stunt left at the snap, with defensive end Aiden Hutchinson angling inside, leaving linebacker Jack Campbell to fill the gap behind him. Again, we don’t know Jack Campbell’s responsibility in this situation per se, but here he gets sealed by the tight end as cornerback D.J. Reed is tight to the line of scrimmage responsible for spill. Should Jack Campbell have attacked the outside shoulder of the tight end to play the gap differently and force the spill? Or did nickel safety Christian Izien fail to play the inside shoulder of his blocker to force the spill? These issues are unacceptable. 3. Third-and-long: “the fixes are simple” Lastly, the Lions need to play better situational football. Blown coverages on third-and-long is the fastest way to lose to an MVP-caliber quarterback. “We were outstanding on third down, but it was actually third-and-10 plus is like, why are we in the bottom tier in the league in that category?” Sheppard said . “Why aren’t we executing? And then you turn on the tape and it’s very eye-opening to what’s happening. It sounds easy, but it is. It’s simple solutions, man.” Simple solutions. The breakdown here is somewhere between safety Avonte Maddox and nickel cornerback Roger McCreary. With trips receivers to the field side, Maddox breaks on the wide receiver-3 when the route breaks inside. McCreary also sits as the wide reciever-2 in the trips set continues with the vertical route. At the end of the game, three off season commitments to fix three glaring issues from the end of the 2025 season failed to take shape. Is there hope for the Lions defense? The solutions are simple.

title: The Jets’ interception-less streak is incredible
summary: One of my biggest fears this week, in what is likely to be a very wet MetLife Stadium, is that Jordan Love is the unfortunate quarterback to end the New York Jets’ interception-less streak. This streak dates back to January 5th of 2025 when current 49er Ashtyn Davis picked off former Pro Bowl quarterback Snoop […]
full_text: One of my biggest fears this week, in what is likely to be a very wet MetLife Stadium, is that Jordan Love is the unfortunate quarterback to end the New York Jets’ interception-less streak. This streak dates back to January 5 th of 2025 when current 49er Ashtyn Davis picked off former Pro Bowl quarterback Snoop Huntley in the second quarter of the Jets’ 32-20 win over the Miami Dolphins. The Jets then went through the entire 2025 season without recording a single interception and failed to get one against Cam Ward in Week 1. It’s an unprecedented streak in the modern NFL, and it’s also likely to come to an end shortly because, while the Jets were bad last year and are likely still pretty bad this year, they were also colossally unlucky. Over the long haul, about 20% of all passes defended become interceptions. Last season the Jets had a perfectly respectable number of passes defended at 67, ranking 20 th overall and tied with the New England Patriots. Unlike the New England Patriots, who picked off 10 of those passes, the Jets had zero. The Jets also recovered just three fumbles on defense for the season (and forced only eight) meaning that only 1.7% of opposing offensive drives resulted in a turnover in 2025, which is the lowest mark in the NFL since at least 1993. The Jets did manage three sacks in their game against the Titans last Sunday, a number that they only achieved three times in 17 games last season, and perhaps a more consistent pass rush will create more opportunities as well. The weather is supposed to be sloppy on Sunday in New Jersey, and poor weather often brings chaos with it. The Green Bay Packers have a lot of weapons, but with their interior line struggling and no running back talent to speak of, they basically must pass to move the ball. Passing in poor weather can lead to all sorts of bad outcomes. Let’s hope regression to the mean decides to hold off for one more week.
