title: What the Packers’ game-day roster could look like: Week 2, New York Jets
summary: A couple of weeks ago, we did an exercise on what the Green Bay Packers’ game-day roster would look like, and I want to update that projection for Week 2 based on new information we have. To recap, here was my prediction on how the Packers would drop their 53-man active roster to their 48-man […]
full_text: (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images A couple of weeks ago, we did an exercise on what the Green Bay Packers’ game-day roster would look like , and I want to update that projection for Week 2 based on new information we have. To recap, here was my prediction on how the Packers would drop their 53-man active roster to their 48-man game-day roster: One tight end inactive (WRONG, all four tight ends were active in Week 1) Two offensive linemen inactive (CORRECT, it was Aaron Banks out with injury and Travis Glover being a healthy scratch) At least one defensive lineman inactive (CORRECT, Warren Brinson was out with an injury and Anthony Campbell was a healthy scratch) One choose-your-own-adventure spot between receiver, defensive lineman and off-ball linebacker (WRONG, it was two of these players, not one, because the team kept four tight ends) For the most part, I feel like I was on the right track going into Week 1 (even before that week’s set of practices began), but if you can’t tell…yes, I was surprised they used four tight ends. Maybe that was just a Minnesota Vikings game-planned thing (I think it’s going to be very hard to keep four tight ends when injuries start to pile up), but it’s not like the New York Jets don’t blitz , either, if that was the justification for the volume at tight end. Before we dig into the nuts and bolts of the roster, we should lay out the Packers’ injury report, which was finalized on Friday : DL Warren Brinson (out, calf) DL Javon Hargrave (doubtful, concussion/knee) OL Zach Bako-Bewele (questionable, knee) OL Aaron Banks (questionable, knee) ED Lukas Van Ness (questionable, concussion) CB Benjamin St-Juste (questionable, hamstring) With seven defensive linemen on the roster (Packers used five last week) and ten offensive linemen (Packers used eight last week), Green Bay should be able to handle those positions — at least from a numbers perspective — even in an absolute worst-case scenario where Brinson, Hargrave, Bako-Bewele and Banks don’t play against the Jets. The real pressure points on the roster, injury-wise, this week are with Van Ness and St-Juste. On the edge, the Packers only have four total players at the position — including Van Ness — a pretty low number for them historically. If Van Ness can’t go, they will almost certainly have to call up either Arron Mosby or rookie Nyjalik Kelly from the practice squad. In my opinion, Kelly seems like the more likely candidate, as Mosby is more of a special teamer than a true defender; thus, Mosby doesn’t really fix Green Bay’s “we only have one backup” issue. If the Packers think they’re going to be down Van Ness, they’ll probably let us know by calling up a practice squad player at the position (likely Kelly) on Saturday. In theory, the Packers could keep just four “cornerbacks” if St-Juste’s hamstring injury issue keeps him off the field, but one of the problems there is that Kamal Hadden, officially listed as a cornerback, was actually a full-time slot player for Green Bay this preseason. Hadden worked out with the safeties, not cornerbacks, in individual drills, common for a slot defender. A question I have is how much Hadden has been working with outside cornerbacks in-season, because if Hadden hasn’t been doing that before St-Juste first popped up on the injury report on Friday, will the team really want to rely on Hadden leaning on banked reps from 2024-2025 under a different defensive coordinator to be the “break in case of two injuries emergency” player on Sunday? If not, I could see a second practice squad call-up (rookie sixth-round pick Domani Jackson is the only practice squad cornerback for the Packers) this weekend, depending on St-Juste’s health. So, how do we get to a 48-man gameday roster? First, it’s important to remember that practice squad call-ups aren’t extra players on game day. These players get added to the pool of players who could potentially suit up for game days, almost like the 53-man roster expands up to a 55-man roster, but the game-day roster still has a hard cap at 48 players. For every practice squad player elevated, another inactive must be made. With all that said, here’s my prediction for Sunday: QB: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor RB: MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson WR: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed, Bo Melton and Skyy Moore J. Michael Sturdivant healthy scratch (was in Week 1) TE: Tucker Kraft, Jonnu Smith, Mark Redman and Josh Whyle OL: Jordan Morgan, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk, Donovan Jennings, Jager Burton and Anthony Belton Two of: Zach Bako-Bewele (questionable), Aaron Banks (questionable), John Williams or Travis Glover (Week 1 healthy scratch) DL: Karl Brooks, Jonathan Ford, Devonte Wyatt and Chris McClellan One of: Javon Hargrave (doubtful) or Anthony Campbell Warren Brinson (calf) out ED: Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani Dennis-Sutton One of: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) or Nyjalik Kelly (practice squad call-up) LB: Zaire Franklin, Edgerrin Cooper, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper and Niemann CB: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine and Kamal Hadden One of: Benjamin St-Juste (questionable) or Domani Jackson (practice squad call-up) S: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard and Kitan Oladapo SPT: Trey Smack (K), Daniel Whelan (P) and Matt Orzech (LS) There might be an outside chance that the team elects to replace the St-Juste spot on the game-day roster with undrafted rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, if the team believes that St-Juste’s special teams contributions are more important to replace than depth at the cornerback position, but that’s really the only alternative path that I can realistically see. For what it’s worth, St-Juste is a special teams ace, something backup cornerbacks Carrington Valentine and Kamal Hadden very much are not. Sturdivant was onboarded to play a lot of special teams in the summer (he was a difference-maker dating back to college), so I don’t want to rule out that option fully. — Let me know what you think about this in the comments section. Tell me how you see it differently. For reference, below is the Packers’ practice squad (they are allowed to, but not required to, call up as many as two players from there): QB: Kedon Slovis RB: Pierre Strong Jr. and Damon Bankston WR: Isaiah Neyor and Quincy Skinner Jr. TE: Drake Dabney OL: Dalton Cooper, Josh Gesky, Dillon Wade and Cordell Volson DL: Eric Johnson II ED: Nyjalik Kelly and Arron Mosby LB: Kristian Welch (called up Week 1, but Ty’Ron Hopper is cleared now) CB: Domani Jackson S: Kahlef Hailassie K: Lenniy Krieg (international exemption) Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . — Update, 9/19: The Packers ruled out defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion) but upgraded Lukas Van Ness to being cleared from concussion protocol on Saturday. This leaves the Packers’ injury report as: RT Zach Bako-Bewele (knee, questionable) LG Aaron Banks (knee, questionable) CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring, questionable) The Packers have the numbers on the offensive line right now to sustain the questionable injuries, but they’ll be thinner than usual at cornerback if they’re out St-Juste. The team did not call up rookie Domani Jackson (or anyone at all), so they probably either feel good about St-Juste going tomorrow, or they are more focused on replacing his special teams reps — which could be filled by receiver J. Michael Sturdivant — rather than his contributions on defense (the only snap St-Juste played on defense in Week 1 was on a kneel-down). Yes, you can officially pen in Anthony Campbell making his regular-season debut, as the 3-4 defense will need the minimum five interior defensive linemen to get through a game. Hopefully, he makes a splash after a hot preseason.

title: Remembering a Random Packers Game: The New York Jets
summary: Last week, we looked back on a randomly selected game between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings. That’s the only game against the Vikings we’ll be looking back on until further notice. Thank you. This week, we’ve got the New York Jets, whom the Packers have played 14 times. The random game? Their third-ever […]
full_text: (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, we looked back on a randomly selected game between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings. That’s the only game against the Vikings we’ll be looking back on until further notice. Thank you. This week, we’ve got the New York Jets, whom the Packers have played 14 times. The random game? Their third-ever matchup, way back on December 20th of 1981. I didn’t like this one, and you probably won’t either. Entering the Game It was the final week of the 1981 regular season. The Packers, coached by Bart Starr and helmed by Lynn Dickey at QB, found themselves in a “win and in” scenario. The New York Giants were vying for that same Wild Card playoff spot, but the Packers had the edge after beating the Giants twice during the season. Also fighting for a playoff spot were the Jets, who had not been to the postseason since 1969. With a win, they were also in. The entire city of New York was rooting against the Packers. The storied Packers had fallen into a bit of a slump. After dominating in the ‘60s, a series of poor personnel decisions led to the team making the playoffs just once in the ‘70s. With 9 years since their last postseason appearance, they were hungry. They were coming off of their third straight win, and had scored 101 points combined in those three previous games. All they needed was one more win. Dear reader, I am so sorry for what you’re about to see. Key Moments The Packers’ first drive was a doozy. After a couple of incomplete passes and a 6-yard sack, the team punted. Well, they tried to punt. Suddenly, it was 1st and 10 for the Jets at the Packers’ 11. What do you know, they promptly scored. I’m sorry, I thought I specifically said I did NOT want to look back on last week’s Vikings game? After another failed drive by the Packers, they conjured up a momentum shift after Mark Murphy (not him!) intercepted Jets QB Richard Todd. Lynn Dickey responded by getting intercepted himself. After some back and forth between the two teams, the Packers finally put points on the board in the 2nd quarter with a Jan Stenerud field goal. After this, the Packers offense fell victim to the New York Sack Exchange. Joe Klecko, Mark Gastineau, Marty Lyons, and Abdul Salaam hounded Lynn Dickey all afternoon, and Dickey was sacked 9 times as a result. I’m very tired of talking about last week’s Vikings game. The Packers offense had a total of 84 yards, compared to the Jets’ 393. Lynn Dickey finished the game with 39 passing yards, and the Packers turned the ball over 3 times (the Jets turned it over 4 times!) The Outcome The Packers went on to lose the game 28-3, missing out on the Wild Card spot, and sending not one, but two New York teams to the playoffs in the same season for the very first time. In celebration of making the playoffs for the first time since 1969, hundreds of Jets fans stormed the field and tore down the goalposts. The Giants were handed their first postseason appearance in 17 years. The Packers playoff drought would finally end the next year, when the team qualified for the postseason after a 5-3-1 record (7 games were wiped out from the 1982 season after a labor strike). Despite what many Packers doomers are telling you online about the current team, these were the dark ages, and I’m very happy I wasn’t alive to see them. The Packers face off against the New York Jets at 1:00 ET/12:00 CT on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, in search of their first win of the 2026 season.

title: Packers Week 2 Opponent Preview: The New York Jets
summary: With a late week one loss behind them, the Green Bay Packers have prepared this week to face the New York Jets in week two at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, Jersey on Sunday. The Jets went through a major overhaul during the offseason with Aaron Glenn going into his second year as head coach, […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets runs the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the second quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a late week one loss behind them, the Green Bay Packers have prepared this week to face the New York Jets in week two at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, Jersey on Sunday. The Jets went through a major overhaul during the offseason with Aaron Glenn going into his second year as head coach, so let’s take a look at how things changed in the Meadowlands. Key Additions The Jets overhauled their roster (~$85M in free agency spend) with the theme “buy immediate two-way improvement.” Geno Smith (QB) — Traded for from the Raiders, returning to the franchise that drafted him in 2013 to be the 2026 starter. Minkah Fitzpatrick (S) — Acquired via trade with Miami, then signed to a 3-year, $40M extension. Joseph Ossai & Kingsley Enagbare (Edge) , David Onyemeta (DT) — Defensive line infusion aimed at fixing a pass rush that managed just 26 sacks last season. Nahshon Wright (DB) , Dane Belton (S) — Secondary depth. Draft class led by three first-round picks (below). Key Losses Alijah Vera-Tucker (G) — Signed with New England, a real hole at left guard. John Simpson (G) — Also departed, compounding the interior O-line question. Nick Folk (K) — Longtime steady kicker left for Atlanta; replaced by Cade York. Aaron Glenn returns for Year 2 after a 3-14 debut season, but he rebuilt almost his entire staff around him. Offensive Coordinator: Out with Tanner Engstrand (parted ways in January); in with veteran Frank Reich , who now calls the offense. Defensive Coordinator: Steve Wilks was fired late in the 2025 season; Brian Duker (previously Miami’s secondary coach/defensive pass-game coordinator, and a former Glenn assistant in Detroit) takes over. He has no prior play-calling experience, so there’s some chance Glenn — a defensive-minded coach himself — stays heavily involved in defensive play-calling. QB Coach: Charles London out; Bill Musgrave (former Broncos/Raiders/Vikings/Jaguars OC) in Passing Game Coordinator: Scott Turner out; Seth Ryan in. Additional turnover across both lines and the linebacker room, including new hires Ben Boling (LBs, ex-Texans) and Ronald Booker (nickel corners, ex-Cardinals). The through-line: New York fired essentially everyone tied to a bottom-three offense and a defense that collapsed under Wilks, betting on experienced coordinators (Reich, Musgrave) to stabilize the offense around Geno Smith while Duker retools the defense. 2026 Jets Draft Class R1, No. 2 — David Bailey, Edge, Texas Tech R1, No. 16 — Kenyon Sadiq, TE, Oregon R1, No. 30 — Omar Cooper Jr., WR R2, No. 50 — D’Angelo Ponds, CB, Indiana R4, No. 103 — Darrell Jackson Jr., DT, Florida State R6, No. 188 — Anez Cooper, G, Miami (FL) R7, No. 228 — VJ Payne, S, Kansas State Bailey addresses the pass-rush need directly; Sadiq (16th-overall TE, ran a 4.39) gives Frank Reich a mismatch weapon; Ponds was already a Week 1 contributor in the slot. New York opened the season with a comprehensive road win over the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium, snapping a Week 1 losing pattern. They earned a 23-10 with the Titans under the helm of new head coach Robert Saleh, who was also the former coach of the Jets just two seasons ago. What worked: Both first-round rookies produced immediately. On the Jets first drive, Sadiq scored on a jet-sweep run set up by an earlier Cooper Jr. 30-yard catch-and-run. And Breece Hall looked fully healthy, posting his third career 100-yard rushing game and adding a touchdown. Smith was efficient and turnover-free in his first Jets start since 2016, connecting on a 40-yard shot to Adonai Mitchell. He finished week the 11th best EPA per play. The defense held Tennessee scoreless across eight straight drives and limited the Titans to 195 total yards. Areas to watch Minkah Fitzpatrick left last week’s with an apparent groin injury and Cooper also was injured, and both players will be out for the matchup with the Packers on Sunday. Meanwhile, the Jets’ offense stalled with penalties late in the first half, and the final score (23-10) was tightened only by a garbage-time TD. Week one is generally not a good barometer of how teams will look as the season progresses and I fully expect the the Packers to control of this game early and not look back. A week 2 road game will be another good test for the Packers.

title: Weekend Musings: A tough week for the Houston Texans after a tough loss
summary: Bad enough the Texans lost a game that they felt they should have one against the Bills at home. However, they didn’t exactly get a lot of respite this week, for on and off-field reasons. A few events of note: Off-Field Considerations: Hard to find a player under more of a microscope than CJ Stroud. […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 13: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans reacts in the first half against the Buffalo Bills at Reliant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bad enough the Texans lost a game that they felt they should have one against the Bills at home. However, they didn’t exactly get a lot of respite this week, for on and off-field reasons. A few events of note: Off-Field Considerations: Hard to find a player under more of a microscope than CJ Stroud. In his last 3 official games, he has 9 attributed turnovers, including the two fumbles in Week 1. Yet, aside from those significant miscues, he did look solid against Buffalo, (26 of 38 for 274 yards and 2 TDs). The offense did put up 31 points, and likely had the line held up on the final drive and Stroud not been strip-sacked, that total could have been at least 37. Yet, the game was not where the controversy lay. Later in the week, on a podcast, Texans’ legend Andre Johnson offered his take on CJ Stroud. The general gist of the conversation, discussing Stroud’s body language and how that reflects negatively, has not been a topic of much discussion before. A significant amount of offseason reporting indicated that Stroud was taking on more a leadership role with the offense and by extension, the team. His position within the team has evolved as he gained experience. An NFL starting QB can’t help but be the center of attention, with every action and word parsed to a degree that only the highest level of celebrities or politicians face. Few would be surprised if Stroud was upset and showing it after this past game. To this point, at least publicly, the team has taken Johnson’s critique as just part of the NFL media landscape. There is obvious respect for Johnson, given what he has done, and if nothing else, he saw enough bad leadership and execution as a player to know it when he sees it. The team is still backing Stroud, and we haven’t gotten the dreaded “vote of confidence” remark. Yet, that wasn’t the only off-field headline the team generated. No sooner did the Andre Johnson news break then the league revealed that they fined LB Azeez Al-Shaair over $11K for violating league policy. The policy: writing the name Hind Rajab on his eye tape under his eyes for the Week 1 game. Hind Rajab was a 5-year-old Palestinian killed by the Israel Defense Forces in 2024, one of the thousands killed in the near 3-year war in Gaza. This is not the first time that Al-Shaair has run afoul of the NFL for taking a stance over Palestine, as he was fined for a similar action back in January. Upon news of that action by the NFL (which indicated they fined Al-Shaair because he did not clear his intent with the league before the game), Kyrie Irving of the Dallas Mavericks stated that he would pay Shaair’s fine. Given that Shaair just signed a nice new extension in the offseason, the LB is likely not sweating the money. Any mention of Gaza/Palestine/Israel is going to generate emotion/passion. The NFL is not the first entity that most would think would get wrapped up with that international nightmare, but this past week says otherwise. Al-Shaair’s stance was one action, and then you had the whole Robert Kraft/Ed Sheeran controversy, driven by one of Sheeran’s fellow performers, Macklemore, and his pro-Palestinian stances. Not going to argue who is right or wrong in that situation, but it goes to show that even the NFL can’t keep everything out. As for the Texans, the off-field issues don’t seem to be doing a whole lot to disrupt the team aside from having to answer questions about said topics more than they might like. Of course, should the Texans get back to their winning ways, these all become footnotes. If the team struggles…well, would we be surprised if they come back to the forefront? Hope that Depth Can Step Up: While the team generated some off-field material for the press, they also have more than enough on-field type news as well. As of the time of this writing, the following players are out for the coming game: LB To’oTo’o, DE Clowney, WR Collins, RG Ingram. That would be three starters and one significant contributor on the DL. Of the four, perhaps the Collins loss hurts the most. He was Stroud’s leading target (10) in Week 1, and generally, the offense is not as effective when he is out (see the Divisional Round against New England). Now we are about to find out if all of the other depth moves by Caserio and the front office can and will pay off. Wyatt Teller will likely man the RG spot, but given how Ingram struggled in Week 1, and that Teller was behind Ingram, does that give you much confidence? With both Collins and Higgins out, can someone like Boutte or Noel step up? What about the TEs like Schultz and Klein? For a defense that got gashed by Josh Allen, and now down a starting LB and a top DL player, facing Joe Burrow is probably not what the doctor ordered. Outside of Al-Shaair, the LB situation is going to be quite…interesting. Provided Anderson and Hunter can stay healthy and get back to game-wrecking mode, Clowney’s absence may not hurt all that much. Overall, Houston is just increasing the degree of difficulty coming into what might be considered a near-must win. One can only hope that the injury demons are sated and that they will not demand more tribute. Speaking of Week 1: If there is a silver lining from this week for Houston, it is that perhaps Josh Allen might be set up for a season for the ages. No need to repeat how he killed his NRG/Reliant demons this past week, but then on Thursday Night, against a dangerous Detroit team in Buffalo’s new stadium, Allen accounted for 5 more TDs, leading the Bills to a 41-31 victory. Early season results are not assured to continue deep into the year, but Buffalo might be showcasing their most explosive offense since the peak of the K-Gun era. For what has been a tough week for the Texans, you’ll take whatever positives you can. Granted, any negative vibes from his past week can quickly fade away if Houston manages to rebound and thwart Joe Burrow and the Bengals this Sunday. Let us hope that is the case.

title: It is on Steichen and Anarumo to lift the Colts
summary: I should start by acknowledging just how foolish my declaration that the AFC was not the same gauntlet that it has previously been during the Mahomes/Chiefs heyday. The rumors of their demise were greatly exaggerated and I helped exaggerate them. The Chiefs, Bills and Ravens all announced their presence with authority last week. The Bills […]
full_text: Apr 28, 2023; Los Angeles, California, USA; Jack Nicholson attends game six of the 2023 NBA playoffs between the Los Angeles Lakers and the Memphis Grizzlies at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con I should start by acknowledging just how foolish my declaration that the AFC was not the same gauntlet that it has previously been during the Mahomes/Chiefs heyday. The rumors of their demise were greatly exaggerated and I helped exaggerate them. The Chiefs, Bills and Ravens all announced their presence with authority last week. The Bills added another big win on TNF. If you count us as a threat, it means that all three teams took down quality opponents. The Texans, Jags and Bengals didn’t disappoint either, so we may be looking at the Usual Suspects, when handicapping this NFL season in the AFC. A week’s worth of games sees us with a lot of catching up to do. I am taken back to the courtroom scene in A Few Good Men, when Col. Jessup has had to detail his plans for leaving the base. He tells Kaffee “Please tell me that you have something more, Lieutenant. These two Marines are on trial for their lives. Please tell me their lawyer hasn’t pinned their hopes to a phone bill.” I feel the same about the Colts. Please tell me that there is a plan for better LB play. Please tell me that the entire off-season was not dedicated to one scripted series of plays. Please tell me that there was some truth to how well Walley plays in practice. At least outwardly, I believe we are being told that changing the green dot from Bynum to a LB will improve the LB play and possibly the secondary’s as well. Less distance for communication to travel and such. I still did not see a Colts player that I would trust stop Kelce from getting whatever he wants in the middle of the field? I’m also not sure that the entire unit will hold up any better against K-9, than they did against Henry. Then there is the matter of trying to beat the mad blitzer in Spagnuola. Please tell me there is a play to beat the all-out blitz that we will surely see. Actually, I’d hope that there were multiple plays to beat this and that they are called when the situation warrants, not after we see what looks to be 17 guys at the line of scrimmage. If the situation calls for a blitz, you can rest assured that one will be dialed up. I did think we put better pressure on Jackson last week, than I have seen us show in a good while. Mahomes is just as elusive and you have to stay on your feet, or he’s around you. He will even simulate a pass once he is across the line of scrimmage and make it work. When teams beat the Chiefs, they usually do so with a relentless pass rush, so we not only need to keep him moving, but get him on the ground when in arm’s reach. Shane, please tell us that if scripting plays is this easy, you will script at least a half’s worth. Getting us off the rails should not be as easy as it was last week. We have to take some shots and if Pierce cant succeed in that role yet, figure out a way to get Downs downfield. Heck, anyone for that matter, but you have stretch the field vertically, as well as horizontally. Lastly, tell me that the O-line has more tools available. Chop blocks are illegal, but cut blocks are not. Get a guy to the ground and maybe the next wave of rusher has to at least move around a pile of 650 pounds worth of players. You may also get a little line of site for that slant that I am still waiting to see. You all know me as an optimist and I remain so. I do have some fear that we could look a lot better than we did last week and still come up short. KC in Arrowhead has been as hard as it gets, especially over the last 10 Mahomes years. I’ll be honest, I saw it more achievable before seeing our struggles and watching the Chiefs not be the team ready for a decline. One thing to ponder. Jones 19 – 31, 1 TD, 1 INT, 2 Sacks. Mahomes 15 – 27, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 2 Sacks. Somehow Mahomes is back, but Jones is still injured? One win changes a lot, so I’m thinking we feel much better about Jones after this week. What are your thoughts on what the Colts have to do to come back to town 1 – 1?

title: Can the Colts avoid the dreaded 0-2 start?
summary: We knew things weren’t going to get any easier. After getting demolished at home by the Ravens, the road for the Indianapolis Colts gets worse. A prime time date with the Chiefs on the road is about as tough a start as you could ask for. Fail to win and the alternative is a hard […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 23: Grover Stewart #90 of the Indianapolis Colts is called for roughing the passer on Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs in the second quarter of the game at Arrowhead Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images We knew things weren’t going to get any easier. After getting demolished at home by the Ravens, the road for the Indianapolis Colts gets worse. A prime time date with the Chiefs on the road is about as tough a start as you could ask for. Fail to win and the alternative is a hard road back; the dreaded 0-2 start. Teams that start 0-2 make the playoffs about 10% of the time. That’s since the merger. If you want a glass half-full look, since 2020, the percentage actually rises to 16%. On one hand, the Colts aren’t necessarily a Super Bowl caliber team. A top tier team would have more resources and abilities to make it out of that type of hole. On the other, the Colts would have played two of the better teams in the conference. That leaves room for hope. Is this putting the cart before the horse? Certainly. Is it giving up before the game has even been played? Maybe. We have to look at what we all witnessed last week, though. If that Colts team and that Chiefs team meet, it’s going to be ugly. The Colts must elevate their game immediately. With games against the Texans, Commanders, and Steelers in their next three, this one is pivotal. They have fared well against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs before, even when it seemed like they would be doomed. That is a positive the Colts will have to cling to for now. The Colts aren’t strangers to starting 0-2 over the last decade or so, but most of those seasons were lost. Nothing is set yet, though. The Colts could leave Arrowhead 1-1 feeling great about their season going forward. Then again, 0-2 is staring them in the face. It won’t be easy, but the Colts have to find a way.
author: Jon Spradley

title: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride: does Indy stand a chance?
summary: In Week 2 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will hit the road to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. Knowing the party was headed to KC, I sat down with Maurice Elston of Arrowhead Pride, SB Nation’s Chiefs blog. You can find him on Twitter @MrMauriceElston. We swapped questions and answers about both the Chiefs […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 16: Head Coach Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs watch a field goal against the Denver Broncos during the NFL 2025 game between Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 2 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will hit the road to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. Knowing the party was headed to KC, I sat down with Maurice Elston of Arrowhead Pride , SB Nation’s Chiefs blog. You can find him on Twitter @MrMauriceElston . We swapped questions and answers about both the Chiefs and Colts and what follows is what I’ve learned about this week’s opponent. You can find my answers to his questions here. Chris Shepherd: Based on Week 1, if you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to attack the Chiefs’ defense, what would your plan look like? What areas of the field would you attack, what weaknesses would you target and how would you try to beat this Chiefs defense? Maurice Elston: I would do anything possible to force Kansas City’s linebackers—primarily Nick Bolton—to cover in space or match up one-on-one. Bolton is an excellent run defender and the commander of the Chiefs’ defense, but operating in coverage over a large area is not his greatest strength. I would attack the middle of the field with tight ends and running backs, using motion and different formations to create favorable matchups against the linebackers. The Colts have a tight end in Tyler Warren who is capable of presenting that type of problem. Getting Warren matched against Bolton or another linebacker in space could give Indianapolis an opportunity to consistently move the football. Chris Shepherd: In Week 1, Colts fans watched in horror as the Ravens moved Zay Flowers all over the field to exploit favorable matchups that the discombobulated Colts secondary never figured out how to adjust to. Do you think the Chiefs will try to exploit those same issues, and if so, who will Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy slot into the Zay Flowers role for Kansas City? Maurice Elston: I don’t believe the Chiefs will copy Baltimore’s strategy exactly because Kansas City doesn’t have to lean on one receiver the way the Ravens leaned on Flowers. I absolutely expect Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy to test the same communication problems Indianapolis experienced in Week 1, but they will likely do it with several different players. The Chiefs can use motion, shifts and formations to create favorable matchups for Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker III. Instead of putting one player in the Flowers role, Kansas City can force the Colts to identify and communicate against multiple threats before the snap. That unpredictability could make the assignment even more difficult for Indianapolis’ secondary. Chris Shepherd: In Week 1, Patrick Mahomes made his return after recovering from last season’s torn ACL. He completed 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Did Mahomes look like the Patrick of old? Was he still the player who can take over games, or will he need some time to regain that form? Maurice Elston: I wouldn’t say Mahomes completely looked like his old self, but he did look healthy—and that was the most important thing Kansas City needed to see. Mahomes demonstrated that his knee is fine, he can still scramble and he remains capable of making plays outside the pocket. From a passing standpoint, however, there was some understandable rust. He opened the game completing only two of his first 12 attempts and missed a few routine throws that we normally see him make. He eventually settled down and completed 13 of his final 15 attempts, including two touchdown passes. Because he couldn’t participate in his normal offseason routine and did not play during the preseason, some early rust should have been expected. He may not be completely back to his old form yet, but the second half showed that he is getting there. Chris Shepherd: Can you give me one player on offense and one on defense whom Colts fans might not be familiar with but who you expect to make an impact Sunday night? Maurice Elston: Offensively, I would watch rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen. He became one of the Chiefs’ most talked-about young players during training camp and the preseason. Allen received only one target and did not record a catch in Week 1, but I expect Kansas City to begin incorporating him into the offense. In my opinion, Allen may already be the best pure route runner in the Chiefs’ wide receiver room. His ability to separate could become especially valuable against the man-to-man coverage Kansas City’s receivers have consistently faced. Defensively, I’ll go with L’Jarius Sneed. It may seem strange to call Sneed an under-the-radar player considering what he has accomplished, but much of the attention surrounding Kansas City’s secondary has focused on young outside cornerbacks Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams. Sneed’s return to the slot gives Steve Spagnuolo a trusted defender who can cover, blitz and handle several different assignments. Having someone Spagnuolo trusts to lock down the slot changes what the Chiefs can do schematically, making Sneed an important piece of this defense even if he isn’t receiving the most attention . Chris Shepherd: How do you predict this game will play out? What does each team do well, where will they struggle and what is the final score? Maurice Elston : I expect the Chiefs to win, although I don’t anticipate the margin being as large as it was against Denver. Indianapolis’ best path to keeping the game close is through Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren. The Colts must remain committed to Taylor, stay ahead of the chains and use Warren to attack Kansas City’s linebackers and safeties in coverage. There is no completely stopping Taylor because he is too talented, but if the Chiefs can contain him enough to force Indianapolis into third-and-long situations, Kansas City’s pass rush and pressure packages can take control. For the Colts defensively, the challenge will be handling Kansas City’s motion, personnel groupings and improved running game without experiencing the communication breakdowns that hurt them against Baltimore. If those problems continue, Reid and Bieniemy will find ways to exploit them. I believe Indianapolis keeps the game competitive for a while, but Kansas City eventually creates some separation and wins 24-14. I can’t thank Maurice enough for answering this week’s questions. Make sure you head over to Arrowhead Pride and @MrMauriceElston on Twitter to check out his work. As always, go Colts.

title: Jaguars vs. Broncos: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 2
summary: Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! Today, we’re previewing Week 2’s matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Denver Broncos at Mile High. Question 1: What did you learn about the Jaguars in their decisive Week 1 win? Travis Holmes: I learned, in a small way, what type of offense they want to be, while still acknowledging who […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 21: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs for a third quarter touchdown against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! Today, we’re previewing Week 2’s matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Denver Broncos at Mile High. Question 1: What did you learn about the Jaguars in their decisive Week 1 win ? Travis Holmes : I learned, in a small way, what type of offense they want to be, while still acknowledging who they are. Opening the game with four straight rushes and two play-action passes (out of three attempts in the opening drive) clearly drew a line in the sand on this staff’s expectations for 2026. Their desire to be a run-the-ball, play-action squad, while still featuring an extremely deep receiving room, provides a lot of flexibility for Coen and his staff. They’re aware that the passing game needs to better flow through the run and called the game accordingly, with 11 of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez’s 21 combined carries coming in the first half. That clearly spells balance and a purposeful push for a run game not impacted by game script. Gus Logue : I learned that Jacksonville will get contributions from its rookie class sooner than we all thought. TE Nate Boerkircher’s blocking ability offers Liam Coen immediate personnel flexibility; LG Emmanuel Pregnon looks like a rare plug-and-play first-year lineman; and WR Josh Cameron already earned snaps in high-leverage spots like red zone, where he caught one of the best touchdowns of Trevor Lawrence’s career in Week 1. The Jaguars didn’t make any splashy additions in the offseason, but clearly, that doesn’t mean that they didn’t get better. Henry Zimmer : I think the Jaguars, and specifically Trevor Lawrence, proved this passing attack is legit. The second year of this offense looks polished, and the wide receivers clearly have trust and a connection with Lawrence. The more time, the better for that specific group. Question 2: Who’s a player who wasn’t a major factor in last season’s win at Denver but will make their presence felt on Sunday? Travis : Dennis Gardeck and Branson Combs both have an opportunity to make a major impact after not factoring much into last season’s dominant victory at Mile High. Both Gardeck and Combs ended that matchup with just one tackle each, with Combs being primarily a depth special teams player at the time. Enter 2026, with the Broncos offense struggling mightily against pressure in Week 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs. In limited Week 1 snaps, both Combs and Gardeck showed an ability to pressure the quarterback, with Gardeck providing two pressures on nine rushes (22.2% pressure rate) and Combs getting home on his lone Week 1 blitz. Both ended the game with a quarterback hit, with Combs also collecting the aforementioned sack. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix was pressured on 45.5% of his dropbacks last week, and he was sacked four times, finishing 2-of-10 for five yards, an interception, and two strip-sacks on those pressured attempts. The primary candidates (Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, Arik Armstead) will rightfully grab much of the attention and snaps. However, I think the role players, such as these two, may eventually make the key plays in this one when all is said and done. Gus : Travis Hunter, who was already on injured reserve by the time these teams matched up last season. I found his All-22 tape from last week encouraging. If the Jaguars are really a Super Bowl contender , their best players have to step up in big-time moments, and Hunter is among that group. Sunday is a prime opportunity for him to come down with his first career interception. Henry : Last year’s game only featured one sack of quarterback Bo Nix. Can Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen continue from last week and run up the sacks against the Broncos? Nix showed a shakiness against the Chiefs that the Jags could seemingly exploit. If the defensive line steps up, it could be a long day for Nix and company. Question 3: What’s a matchup you’re looking forward to watching? Travis : Broncos linebacker Nik Bonitto against Anton Harrison will be a popcorn-worthy matchup on Sunday. The two-time All-Pro pass rusher is coming off a 14-sack 2025 season, while Harrison is entering his second regular-season game as an NFL left tackle. Following the Browns matchup, where Harrison gave up just one pressure while facing Jared Verse, his next test will be a significantly larger challenge. Gus : Bhayshul Tuten against Nick Singleton, who missed a whopping 5 tackles in Denver’s season-opening loss at Kansas City. The entire Broncos defense looked like they had never tackled before in that game, but Singleton especially is a weak link for what was the No. 3 scoring defense a season ago. Expect Liam Coen to go after the soon-to-be 33-year-old linebacker. Tuten… let’s see what you got! Henry : I want to see how the Jags receivers stack up against the Broncos secondary again. Everyone knows that Pat Surtain II is legit, but Parker Washington did have almost 150 yards against this defensive backfield last season. The Chiefs ran the ball super effectively against the Broncos, but this is a pass-first offense in Jacksonville. Let’s see how they continue to throw it around. Final score prediction? Travis : Jaguars 31, Broncos 17 Gus : Jaguars 34, Broncos 14 Henry : Jaguars 24, Broncos 17 What are your Week 2 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments! Join the conversation! title: Kingdom Keys: 3 keys to a Chiefs victory over the Colts in Week 2
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs need greater production from their wide receivers, disciplined defense against Indianapolis’ top two weapons and a cleaner performance Sunday night. Patrick Mahomes showed some understandable rust in his return from a torn ACL, completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Kansas City’s defense and running […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Running back Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs watches game action from the sidelines of an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs need greater production from their wide receivers, disciplined defense against Indianapolis’ top two weapons and a cleaner performance Sunday night. Patrick Mahomes showed some understandable rust in his return from a torn ACL, completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Kansas City’s defense and running game controlled the action, but the passing attack struggled to consistently threaten Denver. That will need to improve when the Chiefs welcome the Indianapolis Colts to Arrowhead Stadium on “Sunday Night Football.” Here are three keys to a Chiefs victory in Week 2: Offensive key: Get the wide receivers involved Kansas City’s revamped running game delivered everything it could have hoped for against Denver. Kenneth Walker III rushed for 173 yards, and the Chiefs finished with 208 yards on the ground. The wide receivers, however, combined for only five receptions and 37 yards. Xavier Worthy caught three passes, while Rashee Rice recorded two receptions — including a 13-yard touchdown. No other Chiefs wide receiver caught a pass. Mahomes missed a few throws he would normally complete, but the lack of production was not entirely on the quarterback. Kansas City’s receivers also struggled to consistently create separation, continuing one of the offense’s biggest problems from last season. Baltimore showed how vulnerable the Indianapolis secondary can be. Zay Flowers caught five passes for 150 yards and a touchdown against the Colts — and he produced all of it in the first half before leaving with a hamstring injury. The Ravens finished with 324 passing yards in their 41-23 victory. The Chiefs do not need one receiver to duplicate Flowers’ performance. They do need their receiving corps to collectively make a much greater impact. A good benchmark would be at least 150 receiving yards combined between Kansas City’s wideouts. Whether those yards come from Rice, Worthy, Tyquan Thornton or Cyrus Allen matters less than making sure the production is spread beyond Travis Kelce and the running backs. The running game carried Kansas City in Week 1. To develop into a complete offense, the Chiefs must prove their wide receivers can punish defenses that commit additional resources to stopping it. Defensive key: Contain Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren Indianapolis’ offense begins with running back Jonathan Taylor. Even while the Colts struggled in their season-opening loss, Taylor rushed 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns. That followed a 2025 season in which he finished third in the NFL with 1,585 rushing yards and led the league with 18 rushing touchdowns. The Chiefs should not expect to completely stop him. The more realistic objective is to contain him — keeping Taylor near 75 yards and limiting him to no more than one touchdown. Kansas City held Taylor to 58 yards on 17 carries when the teams met last season. The defense also allowed Denver’s running backs only 54 yards in Week 1, although the Broncos attempted just 11 handoffs. Keeping Taylor under control would put Indianapolis into longer third-down situations and place more responsibility on Daniel Jones, who is still working his way back from the Achilles tear that ended his 2025 season. Jones completed 19 of 31 passes for 166 yards, one touchdown and an interception against Baltimore. The Chiefs must also account for tight end Tyler Warren, particularly when Indianapolis attempts to create favorable matchups against Kansas City’s linebackers. Warren caught only three passes for 13 yards in Week 1, but one of them produced a touchdown. He is coming off a rookie season in which he recorded 76 receptions for 817 yards and four touchdowns. Kansas City should avoid leaving Warren isolated against its linebackers in space. Using safety help, mixing coverages and disrupting him at the line of scrimmage would help take away one of Jones’ most dependable options. If the Chiefs contain Taylor and prevent Warren from exploiting favorable matchups, they can force Jones to carry the Indianapolis offense. X-Factor: Win the field-position battle The Chiefs overcame seven penalties for 60 yards against Denver, but that is not a habit they want to carry forward. Penalties repeatedly hurt Kansas City last season. The Chiefs finished with 119 accepted penalties for 951 yards, including a 10-penalty, 119-yard performance in their Week 13 loss to the Dallas Cowboys . Kansas City was good enough to overcome its mistakes against Denver, but the Chiefs cannot continue giving opponents free yardage and additional opportunities. Offensively, holding penalties and false starts can turn manageable situations into second-and-long or third-and-long. Defensively, penalties that produce automatic first downs can keep drives alive after the unit has done everything necessary to get off the field. The Chiefs should aim to stay below five penalties Sunday night. Against a Colts team trying to rebound from a difficult opener, Kansas City cannot provide assistance by extending Indianapolis drives or stopping its own momentum. The bottom line The Chiefs cannot expect Kenneth Walker III to produce 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns every week. Kansas City needs its wide receivers to combine for at least 150 receiving yards and provide Mahomes with consistent options in the passing game. Defensively, the group must contain Jonathan Taylor, limit Tyler Warren’s favorable matchups and force Daniel Jones to carry the Colts’ offense. The Chiefs must also avoid costly penalties that extend Indianapolis drives or put their own offense behind the chains. If Kansas City can accomplish those three things, it will have an excellent opportunity to defeat the Colts on Sunday night and improve to 2-0.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to Colts DC Lou Anarumo
summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to playing against a Lou Anarumo-coached defense. Sunday night’s game will be the eighth meeting between Mahomes and the Indianapolis Colts defensive coordinator. Mahomes and the Chiefs are 4-3 all time against Anarumo. Before coaching in Indianapolis, Anarumo was the defensive coordinator for the Cincinnati Bengals […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 23: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs looks to throw the football during the fourth quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Arrowhead Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to playing against a Lou Anarumo-coached defense. Sunday night’s game will be the eighth meeting between Mahomes and the Indianapolis Colts defensive coordinator. Mahomes and the Chiefs are 4-3 all time against Anarumo. Before coaching in Indianapolis, Anarumo was the defensive coordinator for the Cincinnati Bengals from 2019-2024. The most famous of these matchups was the 2022 AFC Championship Game , AKA The “Burrowhead” Game. The Bengals were flying high, coming off a Super Bowl appearance the previous season that came immediately after beat the Chiefs in the AFC Championship at Arrowhead, in what may have been the biggest collapse of the Patrick Mahomes era. This prompted many players on the Bengals team to get big heads and talk out of their backsides, especially defensive back Mike Hilton, who famously referred to Arrowhead Stadium as “Burrowhead,” a reference to Bengals starting quarterback Joe Burrow. The Chiefs went on to defeat the Bengals, 23-20, en route to their third Super Bowl appearance in the Patrick Mahomes era. This also gave us one of the greatest Travis Kelce postgame moments of his career. “Burrowhead, my ass!” pic.twitter.com/vKCt7KSZ84 — Arrowhead Pride (@ArrowheadPride) January 30, 2023 In their seven previous matchups, the Chiefs have scored an average of 24.7 points per game. But the Colts are coming off a Week 1 trouncing, when they gave up over 500 yards of total offense to the Baltimore Ravens ; 202 of those yards came on the ground, with running back Derrick Henry gashing them for 144 yards and three touchdowns. The Colts ranked 31st in passing yards allowed last season. The team did, however, finish seventh in the league in rushing yards allowed. So only time will tell if Week 1 was who the Colts are in 2026 or if the Ravens game was an anomaly. Despite the seemingly favorable matchup for the Chiefs, Mahomes isn’t taking Anarumo or the Colts’ defense lightly, telling reporters on Thursday afternoon that “Coach (Lou) Anarumo is one of the best defensive coordinators I’ve went up against.” “If you look at their defensive line, their safeties, their corners, they have really good football players or linebackers. And so, they’ll have a lot of pride, and they’ll come out with the right mentality.” Patrick Mahomes on #Colts DC Lou Anarumo: “I think what makes him such a great DC is he tailors his scheme to the team. He wants to go with their strengths.” “Something that makes him a great coach is that he’s not stuck in his ways of how he calls a game.” 🎥: @Chiefs pic.twitter.com/oTa1E5hYsM — Noah Compton (@nerlens_) November 21, 2025 Mahomes also highlighted that Anarumo is adept at tailoring his scheme and game plan around the team he is going up against. So wait and see if the Colts come out determined to stop the run, or if Kenneth Walker III will have another field day in Week 2.

title: Matthew Stafford can silence plenty of doubt with a big Week 2
summary: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford needs a bounce back performance from Week 1 as much as anyone on the roster. Sure, there were plenty of expected contributors who struggled mightily in the opener, from Myles Garrett’s quiet game to nearly zero production from Davante Adams and plenty of others in between. But nothing may […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford needs a bounce back performance from Week 1 as much as anyone on the roster. Sure, there were plenty of expected contributors who struggled mightily in the opener, from Myles Garrett’s quiet game to nearly zero production from Davante Adams and plenty of others in between. But nothing may be as concerning as the shaky-at-best start for the reigning NFL MVP. There’s no getting around how poorly Stafford performed last week. He went 15-of-25 passing for merely 155 yards and no touchdowns with an interception. Throw on a generic jersey and change the nameplate, and anyone who follows the league will tell you that’s not the type of quarterback performance you can live with. He didn’t move fluidly, his decision making was iffy, it felt like a shocking departure from who we saw dice up defenses last year. Obviously, a lot of factors are at play here. He’s another year older, sometimes it takes a while to get your legs back when you don’t play at all in the preseason, then there’s the fact Week 1 is often just a mess. Plus, did you hear about the Rams’ travel plans for the Australia trip ? Certainly that hasn’t been beaten to death over the last week. Whatever the reasoning is, Stafford didn’t cover himself in glory in Week 1, and it’s led to plenty of consternation around the NFL ecosystem, including worries about whether or not we’ve witnessed the beginning of the end for the Super Bowl LVI champion. waited this whole summer for the Rams to use no huddle and they finally do in the 2nd quarter (right on schedule). *sad trombone* pic.twitter.com/bvSMN1bnyQ — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 11, 2026 You know what would assuage a lot of those concerns? Shredding the New York Giants’ defense on Monday night. And it’s more than fair to think that’s on the table in the Week 2 finale. The Giants were one of the big winners beyond the basic record ledger in Week 1, thoroughly controlling their game against the Dallas Cowboys and earning some early praise for the start of John Harbaugh’s second act. But look under the hood and you’ll find reasons to believe that the opportunity is there for big quarterbacks performances. New York has one of the more fearsome groups of young pass rushers in the NFL, headlined by Brian Burns, 2025 third-overall pick Abdul Carter and this year’s fifth-overall pick, Arvell Reese. Despite all that raw talent, the Giants generated just a 33.3% pressure rate in Week 1 according to Next Gen Stats/NFL Pro, which was good for 18th in the NFL last week. Not terrible but not good, either, just fully mediocre. It’s understandable if you’re skeptical still of the Rams’ offensive line, which ranked 22 nd in the NFL in Pass Rush Win Rate last week per ESPN, but the early returns don’t indicate anything especially sinister from the New York pass rush.\ What’s more, the Giants’ defense was 28 th in EPA/dropback last week and 22 nd in dropback success rate. The Cowboys were still able to move the ball in chunks and with consistency against that defense. If the Rams are fundamentally broken, those numbers don’t mean as much. But it’s far too early for that to be proven true, even if the vibes are low, so to see a team on the schedule that gave up plenty of ground to Dak Prescott a week ago hopefully bodes well for the Rams and Stafford this week. If Monday night goes poorly for the passing game and the MVP looks progressively more pedestrian, concern levels will predictably and fairly rise. But this is simultaneously a great opportunity for Stafford to quiet the outside noise and the concerns about what his 18 th season will look like.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: What’s your favorite Rams season when they didn’t win the Super Bowl?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are trying to win their third Super Bowl in franchise history, but the road to the first win of the season won’t come on Sunday. The Rams are off today and will not come back until Monday night against the New York Giants. Super Bowl expectations were as high as ever […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are trying to win their third Super Bowl in franchise history, but the road to the first win of the season won’t come on Sunday. The Rams are off today and will not come back until Monday night against the New York Giants. Super Bowl expectations were as high as ever coming into the 2026, and they can still get back there with a couple of wins in a row to wash the bitter taste of a 49ers loss out of their mouths. In the meantime, what do you think is the most satisfying or best season in Rams franchise history that didn’t end in a Super Bowl win? It can be your personal experience, like maybe it was the year you became a Rams fan or at a time something great happened in your own life. Or it can be based simply on the football. A time when you think the Rams were making football fun for you, it just didn’t end in a Super Bowl. A few seasons that come to mind: 2023 Coming off of a 5-12 season, Sean McVay was questioning his commitment to the NFL. The Rams didn’t have a first-round pick to try and rebuild with and Aaron Donald’s salary accounted for more than 50% of all the money invested into the defense that year. To make matters worse, Cooper Kupp missed the first month of the season and the Rams started 3-6. But in the meantime, the rookie class looked amazing without a first-round pick: Puka Nacua was making history Kobie Turner and Byron Young were bargains on defense Steve Avila and Davis Allen were also rookie contributors 2023 is one of the best draft classes in team history, and since then has gotten even better with improvements by Warren McClendon, Desjuan Johnson, and the continued presence of Stetson Bennett and Davis Allen a few years later. Then the Rams rebounded, winning seven of their last eight games and making the playoffs out of nowhere. Just a one-point loss to the Lions separated L.A. from the second round of the postseason. 2017 Sean McVay took over a 4-12 team and immediately flipped the 32nd-ranked scoring offense to the top-ranked scoring offense. As usual, he did it without a first-round pick. The emergence of Todd Gurley as an MVP runner-up and Jared Goff as a decent starting quarterback really saved the franchise’s potential plunging into the ocean if those picks had been busts, as they were starting to become under Jeff Fisher. Cooper Kupp was one of the great picks of all-time for the Rams and Andrew Whitworth, Robert Woods were two of the best free agent signings. Aaron Donald won his first career Defensive Player of the Year award. The Rams did lose to the Falcons in the wild card round, but had set themselves up for a deep Super Bowl run in 2018. 1979 One of the all-time underdog stories, the Rams held a fourth quarter lead in the Super Bowl against the mighty Pittsburgh Steelers. L.A. had finished 9-7. Pittsburgh went 12-4 and had already won three Super Bowls in the 70s. A 24-yard touchdown pass from Lawrence McCutcheon to Ron Smith gave the Rams a 19-17 lead in the third quarter, but they just couldn’t hang on. A Cinderella team that had been 5-6 midseason, the Rams won four in a row, then made the playoffs at 9-7. Jack Youngblood has since been credited with 18 sacks that year. Wendell Tyler led the league with 5.1 yards per carry. Larry Brooks was an All-Pro defensive tackle. The Rams upended the Cowboys and Bucs in the playoffs to reach the Super Bowl, a win that would have been historic. I’m sure for many fans reading this, 1979 still was historic anyway. What is your favorite non-Super Bowl winning Rams season?
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams rule out Kam Kinchens with hamstring injury
summary: The Los Angeles Rams continue to lose players to injury, this time ruling out starting safety Kam Kinchens with a hamstring injury for Monday night’s game against the New York Giants. It is the first career missed game for Kinchens, a player with six interceptions in 35 games. The Rams listed Puka Nacua as questionable […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams continue to lose players to injury, this time ruling out starting safety Kam Kinchens with a hamstring injury for Monday night’s game against the New York Giants . It is the first career missed game for Kinchens, a player with six interceptions in 35 games. The Rams listed Puka Nacua as questionable on the final injury report , while fellow receiver Jordan Whittington is doubtful. After just placing Myles Garrett on IR, the Rams are down two starters on defense. In the interim, it appears Tanner Ingle, who was just elevated to the 53-man roster last week, and Jaylen McCollough will need to step up at safety. L.A. could also elevate Nick Andersen from the practice squad. On offense, the loss of Nacua would be a brutal blow for Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford, but the hits keep on coming with Whittington probably ruled out. Few players ever play after being listed as doubtful. In that case, the Rams would be leaning heavily on Davante Adams, Konata Mumpfield, and their tight ends. Not to mention the running game. Tutu Atwell and C.J. Daniels were inactive last week, so they could both be on the active roster on Monday if both Nacua and Whittington are ruled out. It looks as though Nacua is a game-day decision. At least the Rams are expected to get back Aaron Donald , although they wish his return was coupled with better news on the injury front.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Puka Nacua questionable for Monday Night Football
summary: Puka Nacua missed his second straight day of practice on Saturday due to a hip injury and Sean McVay says that the Los Angeles Rams will list him as questionable for Monday Night Football against the Giants. Nacua suffered a psoas injury in training camp but participated in Week 1’s loss to the San Francisco […]
full_text: Puka Nacua missed his second straight day of practice on Saturday due to a hip injury and Sean McVay says that the Los Angeles Rams will list him as questionable for Monday Night Football against the Giants . Nacua suffered a psoas injury in training camp but participated in Week 1’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers without any noticeable setbacks. Now over a week later, Nacua is in danger of missing a game that the Rams can’t afford to lose any more key players. Rams HC Sean McVay said WR Puka Nacua will not practice today due to his hip injury and he will be listed as questionable for Monday night’s game against the Giants. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 19, 2026 The Rams have already placed Myles Garrett on IR, keeping the star edge rusher out for at least four games. That was an injury that went from being dismissed as “no big deal” but onlookers in training camp to now costing Garrett at least a month. Similarly, Nacua’s injury was scoffed at as preseason caution, if not a “smoke screen”, and he’s not practicing with a huge game coming up against the Giants. Davante Adams would assume the role of Matthew Stafford’s top receiver, but tight ends Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson should prepare for elevated roles if Nacua is out. Jordan Whittington also missed practice on Friday, so the Rams could be down two receivers instead of one. It may be the first time that fans see either Tutu Atwell or C.J. Daniels this season if Nacua is inactive; both receivers were a healthy scratch in Week 1. Nacua missed one game in 2025 and six games in 2024. The Rams would not like to see him miss any games in 2026.

title: Aaron Donald can solidify himself as the best (again)
summary: Aaron Donald is expecting to play for the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football, and if things go bad, there will be plenty to talk about. But if Donald can find a way to help the Rams win or simply dominate on his own accord, then he’ll once again solidify himself as one of […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 31: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on before the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on December 31, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Donald is expecting to play for the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football , and if things go bad, there will be plenty to talk about . But if Donald can find a way to help the Rams win or simply dominate on his own accord, then he’ll once again solidify himself as one of the best to ever play the game. A lot is at stake Monday night as the Rams do not want to fall to the dreaded 0-2 mark. For Donald, he’s coming back (in theory) to the Rams after a couple/few years off, and the expectation going into 2026 is if Donald returned, he’d likely be playing with Myles Garrett. That will not be happening for at least the next for games, maybe longer. So, can Donald still handle his business without another Defensive Player of the Year at his side? If Donald plays, we’re going to find out. And it won’t just be Rams fans watching Donald’s return, everyone who has any interest in football will want to see what AD does, and how he holds up his legacy, or doesn’t. If Donald doesn’t play, then we can basically copy and paste today’s Random Ramsdom for another time. Aaron Donald has blunt response to Myles Garrett’s IR news (ramswire) “I think we’ve got a great defense, a great team, a lot of great pieces,” Donald said. “Obviously, I would love for him to be out there, but he won’t be gone forever. … Hold it down while he’s gone.” The blockbuster trade that sent Garrett to Los Angeles this offseason was the move that likely helped prompt Donald to come out of retirement in the first place. After two years away from the game, the future Hall of Famer decided the chance to pair with Garrett was too good to pass up. Together, the two were supposed to form one of the scariest defensive fronts in recent memory, and the Rams entered the season as a popular pick to make a run at back-to-back titles.“ Aaron Donald plans to play on Monday night (nbcsports) “Donald, the Rams defensive tackle who hasn’t played since announcing his retirement after the 2023 season, said today that he expects to play against the Giants on Monday Night Football. “That’s the plan,” Donald said when asked if he is playing. Donald, who did not make the trip to Australia for the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers, said he has been feeling like his old self while practicing this week. “Have another practice tomorrow, and then we’ll see, but feeling good,” Donald said.“ Rams’ Donald plans to play vs. Giants; Nacua (hip) misses practice (espn) “On Friday, wide receiver Puka Nacua did not practice with a hip injury. Nacua, who had five catches for 74 yards in Week 1, was not on the injury report on Thursday. On Thursday, Rams coach Sean McVay said Donald would go through the week of practice but that he was hopeful the defensive tackle would be able to play on “Monday Night Football.” Donald said Friday that he was able to take part in team drills on back-to-back days and that he feels like himself.“ Rams News: Cam Skattebo ‘Excited’ To Face Aaron Donald In First Game Back (ramsnewswire) “Donald, of course, is one of the greatest defensive players to ever step foot on a football field so all eyes will be on him and how he looks in his comeback. But the Giants aren’t afraid and their star running back Cam Skattebo is actually excited to face off against the all-time great. “Yeah, I mean, he’s had a couple years off and I’m sure he’s ready to go and excited to play. But he’s still got to play football,” Skattebo said on Thursday . “He hasn’t practiced a ton. He hasn’t played in a game yet or played a ton. So, I mean, if it is his first game, then he’s got to be ready for it just like we do. So, I’m excited to play against him. He’s one of the best to ever do it. It’s going to be fun. It’s going to be a good challenge for the guys up front. It’s going to be a good challenge. If I have to meet him in the hole on third and one, then so be it. I’ve got to get one yard. But he’s a good player. He’s one of the best to ever do it. So, all respect to him.” Giants Mailbag: Tyrone Tracy’s Fumbles, Aaron Donald’s Return and Adebo’s Future (si.com) “ Welcome to the weekly New York Giants On SI mailbag! From offseason moves to game-day strategies, we’ll do our best to answer your questions. (Some questions have been edited for brevity and clarity.) “ Aaron Donald, Chris Shula & Nate Scheelhaase talk players to watch vs. the Giants, Week 2 practice reps & more (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams defensive end Aaron Donald, defensive coordinator Chris Shula, and offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase address the media on Friday. Watch them discuss Monday’s matchup and players to watch vs. the New York Giants, Week 2 practice reps, and more.” Aaron Donald sends ‘That’s the plan’ message to New York Giants as Los Angeles Rams prepare for his long-awaited return (hitc.com) “Although Donald has not played an NFL game for two seasons, his return comes with plenty of attention given his record during his career with the Rams. New York opened the season with a win over the Dallas Cowboys, but now face a much tougher test against a Rams team looking to respond after its defeat in Melbourne. Los Angeles will, however, be without Myles Garrett after the star pass rusher was placed on injured reserve. Garrett, who joined the Rams during the offseason, is expected to miss at least four games after undergoing knee surgery.“ LA Rams Send ‘Hair on Fire’ Notice About Giants Ahead of Week 2 Matchup (heavy.com) ““They have great players across the board. They do a great job schematically,” McVay told Nick Hamilton on Sept. 17. “But then you look at it, whether you’re talking about [Kayvon] Thibodeaux, obviously, [Brian] Burns and Abdul Carter, you feel their presence. Then [Arvell] Reese was an excellent player in college and you see why he was picked where he was, doing a good job as an inside backer.” McVay: Myles Garrett (knee) ‘feeling good’ post-surgery, but Rams ‘not going to rush him back’ from Injured Reserve (therams.com) “Head coach Sean McVay on Monday did not want to put a timetable on Garrett’s return until he had all the information post-surgery. While the surgery has been completed, McVay on Thursday was still reluctant to do so, other than saying the team would not rush Garrett back from IR after missing at least the next four games. “He’s feeling good,” McVay said. “… He had crutches yesterday, and then he was walking without crutches today, so he’s like Wolverine, healing fast. I’m reluctant to put a timeline on it. We’ve kind of talked about it, but we know that he’s going to miss those four weeks at a minimum, and we’re not going to rush him back. We want to make sure that he’s feeling good, (that) he’s able to get out on the practice field and do all the things that are necessary for him to perform at a level that he’s been accustomed to. And so that’ll be something that I’ll kind of keep you guys posted as we have updates as we go.” Behind enemy lines: Previewing Rams-Giants with 5 key questions (ramswire.com) “ Giants Wire: I think it’s important to remember that the Dallas defense was terrible in 2025 and really doesn’t look much better after one week this season. That’s not to be a Debbie Downer or dismiss the Giants’ obvious offensive improvements, but reality always lies somewhere in the middle. They fumbled four times, and had they lost more than one, we’d all have a very different vision of that game in our heads. With all of that having been said, there is a reason for optimism in East Rutherford — the offensive scheme was night and day compared to the Daboll era. From Greg Roman to Matt Nagy to John Harbaugh, you can see the many years of experience and success. Still, it’s early in the season, and the identity of this offense is only just…
