title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Green Bay Packers
summary: The New York Jets welcome the Green Bay Packers for their home opener on Sunday afternoon. While New York is seeking to start 2-0 for the first time since 2015, the Packers are under pressure not to drop to 0-2. They gave up 29 unanswered points as they blew a double-digit lead in their opener […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 09: Will McDonald IV #9 of the New York Jets hands a fan a glove during the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers during the NFL Preseason 2025 game between New York Jets and Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 09, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets welcome the Green Bay Packers for their home opener on Sunday afternoon. While New York is seeking to start 2-0 for the first time since 2015, the Packers are under pressure not to drop to 0-2. They gave up 29 unanswered points as they blew a double-digit lead in their opener against the Vikings. The Jets won in Green Bay in the last meeting between the teams back in 2022, but that was their first win over the Packers since 2006. However, they lead the all-time series by nine wins to five. Let’s break down the Packers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Packers quarterback Jordan Love is coming off his best season as a full time starter in terms of completion percentage, quarterback rating and touchdown-to-interception ratio. However, he still hasn’t earned pro bowl recognition as he enters his fourth year as a starter. In game one, Love passed for 387 yards; just two less than his career-high. However, he only completed 50 percent of his passes, was sacked four times, fumbled twice and threw an interception. Can the Jets put some pressure on him? In the event Love gets knocked out of the game, their backup is a familiar face: former Jets quarterback Tyrod Taylor. As we’ve seen, he is still capable of being a competent short-term option. Offensive Line As noted, the Packers gave up four sacks on Sunday, and they also averaged just 3.1 yards per rush, but the more alarming number was 15 quarterback hits. The Vikings blitzed more than any other team in the league in week one, though. However, at the same time, Green Bay left more extra blockers in to pass protect. The main issue was probably the fact that undrafted rookie Donovan Jennings was forced to start at left guard due to an injury to Aaron Banks. He was an obvious weak link. Banks is the Packers’ highest-paid player other than Love, but he’s not exactly lived up to that price-point, as he was very inconsistent in his first year in Green Bay last season. His return in place of Jennings will still obviously help matters, but despite his return to practice, he is still bothered by a knee issue and is not certain to play. They listed him as questionable. The Packers’ most reliable lineman is their right tackle, Zach Bako-Bewele (who changed his name from Zach Tom in the offseason). Last year, he didn’t give up a sack in over 600 snaps. However, he already gave up his first sack of 2026 in the opener. Bako-Bewele is also listed as questionable but it seems unfathomable that he wouldn’t play. The current left tackle is former first round pick Jordan Morgan, who started games at four different positions last season. Center Sean Rhyan is also versatile, having started last year as the right guard until Elgton Jenkins’ season-ending injury in November. The fifth starter is another inexperienced player, as Jacob Monk is the current right guard. He started the season finale last season, but otherwise had only played six offensive snaps in his career. Green Bay’s main backup is Anthony Belton, who started eight games last year, including the last six games of the regular season, and the wild card game. The rest of their bench has no starting experience between them. John Williams was a seventh round rookie last year, but did not play. Travis Glover was inactive last week and rookie Jager Burton was in uniform but did not see action. Running Backs Green Bay’s running game suffered a blow when Josh Jacobs was placed on the exempt list due to an arrest in connection with a domestic incident. He looks set to miss 4-6 weeks based on the latest reports. Jacobs rushed for over 900 yards and 13 touchdowns last season, so his absence will be felt. MarShawn Lloyd is currently listed as a starter but was held to 37 yards on 13 carries in the opener. The former third rounder barely played as a rookie in 2024, then missed the entire 2025 season due to injury. Chris Brooks is back in a reserve role, while Kaleb Johnson is also on the roster but didn’t play any offensive snaps in the first game. Pass catchers The Packers’ leading receiver in 2025 was Romeo Doubs, but he signed a free agent deal with New England, so Green Bay will be hoping for one or more of their recent draft picks to step up. Christian Watson and Jayden Reed were day two picks in 2022 and 2023, while Matthew Golden was a first round pick last season. Watson was the one to step up in week one as he had 147 yards and two touchdowns, including an 81-yarder. However, the speedster Golden saw the most targets and was also effective. He put up the most productive game of his career with six catches for 95 yards. Reed, who averaged over 800 yards in his first two seasons, and caught 14 touchdown passes, was limited to just three starts last season. Bo Melton provides depth off the bench, but had just one catch in the opener. Skyy Moore is mostly on the team for special teams duties and undrafted rookie J. Michael Sturdivant was a healthy scratch to start the season. At tight end, Tucker Kraft is a productive pass catcher who had 469 receiving yards and six touchdowns in just eight games last season. They also added another veteran who Jets fans will recognize as a passing game threat in Jonnu Smith, as the Packers will employ plenty of two tight-end personnel packages. Josh Whyle is back in a reserve role and youngster Mark Redman was added via trade in the offseason. Luke Musgrave, who started 10 games last year, is on the PUP list. Defensive Line The Packers operate with a 3-4 base defense and their starting linemen are listed as Karl Brooks, Javon Hargrave and Devonte Wyatt. However, it was a five-deep rotation on Sunday, also including Jonathan Ford, who started in place of Hargrave, and third round rookie Chris McClellan. The 2022 first round pick Wyatt is probably the best known player in this group. He had four sacks in just 10 games last season. The 33-year old Hargrave has been in concussion protocol and did not practice on Thursday, though. He’s listed as doubtful. Green Bay did a decent job against the run in the first game, holding the Vikings to just 3.1 yards per carry. Backups Warren Brinson and Anthony Campbell were both inactive on Sunday and Brinson has been ruled out due to a calf issue. Linebackers The Packers’ defensive star is edge rusher Micah Parsons. However, he got injured with four games to go in the 2025 season and the Packers haven’t won a game since. He remains on the PUP list as Green Bay tries to avoid a seventh straight loss, a stretch which includes last year’s wild card game. With Parsons out, and both Rashan Gary and Kingsley Enagbare having departed during the offseason, the starters are currently former first round pick Lukas Van Ness and Barryn Sorrell, who started just one game as a rookie last year. Van Ness, who has been a disappointment, has also been in concussion protocol this week. He did practice on a limited basis all week, though, and is listed as questionable. Fourth round rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton provides depth off the edge along with Brenton Cox Jr., who has just one career start. The inside linebackers are Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin, who each played a full time role on Sunday. Cooper had 118 tackles as he played over 1,000 snaps last season. The 30-year old Franklin, who has had 125 or more tackles in each of the past four seasons in Indianapolis, was acquired via trade in March. Ty’Ron Hopper, Isaiah McDuffie and Nick Niemann provide depth off the bench. McDuffie played over 550 snaps last season but only played one defensive snap in the opener. Hopper was inactive in game one. Defensive Backs Packers cornerback Keisean…

title: Eagles reportedly change two spots on the starting offensive line
summary: The Eagles are in Nashville this weekend to face the Titans in extremely hot conditions for their Week 2 matchup. There were a few unknowns heading into the game, including how the team would handle the offensive line after having to put Landon Dickerson on injured reserve earlier in the week. Several different combinations had […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: Drew Kendall #66 of the Philadelphia Eagles takes the field prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on November 10, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are in Nashville this weekend to face the Titans in extremely hot conditions for their Week 2 matchup . There were a few unknowns heading into the game, including how the team would handle the offensive line after having to put Landon Dickerson on injured reserve earlier in the week . Several different combinations had been considered, but Cameron Wolfe reported before the game that the Eagles plan to move Cam Jurgens over to left guard, and then put Drew Kendall in at center. Eagles will move Cam Jurgens to guard and Drew Kendall to start at center today vs. Titans, sources tell @RapSheet and me. More on OL change + Eagles prep for blazing Nashville heat: pic.twitter.com/KRXmjh9baw — Cameron Wolfe (@CameronWolfe) September 20, 2026 The team has confidence in Kendall, who had an impressive training camp and looked good during preseason games, but they also had Willie Lampkin as an option. It’s interesting that they would choose to move Jurgens to guard, who hasn’t played in that role — and that was at right guard, not the left side — since Jason Kelce retired after the 2023 season. Still, the coaches were impressed by Kendall’s understanding of protections and overall football IQ this offseason, which may have contributed to the decision. Before making the trip to Nashville, the Eagles tried to hide their choice for up front and even had Fred Johnson taking snaps at left guard during the portion of practice available to the media. Everyone knew that was a bit of a smoke screen, and now we know why — it was more than just one change they were making. … BLG thoughts: My first reaction to this news is that it’s not ideal to be changing two offensive line spots. If the Eagles felt great about Dickerson’s chances of returning and being effective, I’m not sure they make these two changes. I feel like they would just put Kendall at left guard for the time being. Jurgens lacks experience at left guard. Doesn’t seem great! There’s been talk about how the Eagles really value Dickerson’s intelligence as it relates to pre-snap responsibility. With Dickerson not around, maybe they don’t feel as good about Jurgens in that role? And maybe better about Kendall in that capacity? Perhaps the Eagles feel like it’s easier to help Kendall at center than it would be to help him at guard?

Lotta green at Nissan Stadium tomorrow.” Eagles vs. Titans Game Preview: 6 questions and answers with the Week 2 enemy – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road for the first time this season to take on the Tennessee Titans. Man, it’s (going to be) a hot one with a projected feels like temperature of 94 degrees Fahrenheit at Sunday’s 1:00 PM kickoff. In order to preview this Week 2 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Music City Miracles. The jovial Jimmy Morris kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. Titans vs. Eagles preview: 5 questions with Bleeding Green Nation – Music City Miracles Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation was nice enough to answer 5 questions about his Philadelphia Eagles ahead of tomorrow’s matchup. I did the same for him, and you can read his questions with my answers here . I long for the day when I can answer the opposing team’s questions with some confidence in the Tennessee Titans. That day is not today. NFL Week 2 betting primer: 15 games, trends and key numbers – The Athletic Bad offense: Under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, the Philadelphia Eagles featured five three-and-outs and only 10 first downs, far below the league average of 19.8 first downs in Week 1. More bad offense: The Tennessee Titans managed only 195 total yards in their home opener against the Jets, had just 194 yards in the 2025 season finale at Jacksonville and failed to break 200 total yards in three other games last year. Road warriors: Since Nick Sirianni took over in 2021, Philadelphia is 30-13 on the road, a near 70 percent win rate — the best in the NFL over that span. NFL Week 2 betting guide: Top plays for Sunday afternoon’s games – ESPN Tennessee Titans team total UNDER 15.5 (-105). The Titans’ offensive operation was the worst I saw in Week 1: play designs that were dead in the water, offensive linemen uncertain of their assignments, easy drops and bad routes from receivers and poor accuracy and timing from Cam Ward at quarterback. It’s tough to find anything to hang their hat on from a 23-10 loss to the Jets. It’s worth remarking that Brian Daboll’s offenses have been poor in Week 1 — six, six and and zero points in the three seasons previous — and then stronger in Week 2. Philadelphia’s defensive front looked as deep and disruptive as ever against an average Washington Commanders front, and the Titans are comfortably one of the eight worst lines in football. Though defensive back Cooper DeJean was banged up in the Week 1 game and sat out practice Wednesday, the Eagles’ outside corner duo of Quinyon Mitchell and Riq Woolen still poses a huge problem for the Titans’ ability to create explosive plays through the air. That news comes one day after the Giants put cornerback Paulson Adebo on injured reserve with a knee injury. Banks was in and out of the Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys with what was said to be cramping. Commanders WR Stefon Diggs fined for goalpost celebration vs. Eagles – Hogs Haven Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs was fined for a post-touchdown celebration where he score and then jumped onto the goalpost padding. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 04: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles catches a touchdown pass in the first quarter of a game against the Tennessee Titans at Lincoln Financial Field on December 04, 2022 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 1-0 heading into their Week 2 matchup on the road against the Tennessee Titans. Thanks to Jalen Hurts, the Eagles were able to do enough offensively to get a win in the team’s season opener, and the defense learned a lesson early in the season by letting the Commanders come back in that game. Still, there were flashes of things to be really excited about, including Dontayvion Wicks being a nice deep threat, Jalen Carter still blocking kicks, and Moro Ojomo sniffing out a way to stop the 2-point conversion at the end of the game. And, while a win is a win, the Eagles looked far from a finished product, which is to be expected — especially considering the starters didn’t play in the preseason, and Week 1 was their first time in their new scheme in a game. Given that, the group did just fine. But, they’ll still need to improve, and will be facing a Titans team that is mad that they lost to the Jets. Make the SB Nation app part of Eagles game day! Whomever the Eagles go with up front, the group as a whole will need to play a lot better than they did to open the season, especially to get the run game going and give Jalen Hurts a little help. The QB had a great game, and took matters into his own hands more than once, but the group had three consecutive three-and-outs in the second half, which wasted a lot of good-field opportunities by the defense. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with Tank Bigsby #8 after scoring a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. EAGLES GAME PHILADELPHIA EAGLES at TENNESSEE TITANS: There’s every reason to believe the Eagles should win this game and advance to 2-0. Go Birds. NFC EAST WASHINGTON COMMANDERS at DALLAS COWBOYS: The Commanders played the Eagles close, sure, but the Cowboys are still the bigger threat in the division. Would be glorious to see Dallas drop to 0-2 … ahead of a Week 3 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Root for the Commanders. NEW YORK GIANTS at LOS ANGELES RAMS: If the Giants beat the Rams on Monday night, they’ll be 2-0 before hosting the Titans in Week 3 and the Cardinals in Week 4. The G-Men could very well start 4-0 and perhaps even 5-0 with a game against Washington in Week 5. The Eagles shouldn’t want to see the Giants get rolling, even if a Rams win isn’t really ideal as it relates to potential playoff seeding scenarios down the line. Root for the Rams. NFC PLAYOFF PICTURE CAROLINA PANTHERS at ATLANTA FALCONS: The Falcons are an ideal NFC South winner because they’re just not very threatening. Root for the Falcons. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at BALTIMORE RAVENS: The Saints might be interesting. Would be good to see them not build momentum as an NFC contender. Root for the Ravens. MINNESOTA VIKINGS at CHICAGO BEARS: The Vikings might not be bad but the Bears seem like the bigger threat in the NFC. Root for the Vikings. GREEN BAY PACKERS at NEW YORK JETS: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Jets. CLEVELAND BROWNS at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS: AFC team over NFC team … even though it’s probably an exercise in futility in this case. Root for the Browns. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS at ARIZONA CARDINALS: The reigning Super Bowl champs are obviously the bigger threat. Root for the Cardinals. MIAMI DOLPHINS at SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS: AFC team over NFC team. PITTSBURGH STEELERS at NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS: The Eagles play the Steelers later this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Steelers to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Also, the Eagles own the more favorable of two 2027 fifth-round picks either from the Pats or Bears. Might as well root against New England. Root for the Steelers. JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS at DENVER BRONCOS: The Eagles play the Jags this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Jags to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Jaguars. INDIANAPOLIS COLTS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS: The Eagles play the Colts later this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Colts to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Colts. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS: No Eagles impact but could be fun to cheer on Nakobe Dean, who now plays for the Raiders.

title: Eagles vs. Titans Game Preview: 6 questions and answers with the Week 2 enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road for the first time this season to take on the Tennessee Titans. Man, it’s (going to be) a hot one with a projected feels like temperature of 94 degrees Fahrenheit at Sunday’s 1:00 PM kickoff. In order to preview this Week 2 matchup, I reached out to our […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans is tackled by Will McDonald IV #9 of the New York Jets during the fourth quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road for the first time this season to take on the Tennessee Titans. Man, it’s (going to be) a hot one with a projected feels like temperature of 94 degrees Fahrenheit at Sunday’s 1:00 PM kickoff. In order to preview this Week 2 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Music City Miracles . The jovial Jimmy Morris kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Jimmy’s questions about the Eagles, check out MCM .] 1 – The Titans are 0-1 after losing to the Jets. On a scale of 1-10 (10 being total panic), what’s the concern level about this team after Week 1? It’s pretty much a full-on 10. There were people around here calling that game a must-win for the Titans. There is a scenario where the Titans could have lost that game, and the panic wouldn’t be as high, but that’s not the Titans’ way. They looked abysmal in pretty much every aspect of the game on Sunday. They were dominated on both lines of scrimmage by the New York Jets. Now, I think the Jets are going to be better than most people think this year, but they are certainly not a team that is going to be contending for a Super Bowl. The defense was bad. The offense, especially Cam Ward, was bad. The special teams unit was bad. There was absolutely nothing positive to give us any hope for the season. That was a tough blow after back-to-back 3-win seasons. 2 – What’s the feeling on Cam Ward? How good do you think he can be? And what do you expect from him this week? It’s time for Ward to take a step forward. He was in a really tough spot last year. Everything around him – the coaching staff, the offensive line, the weapons – was bad. That’s not the case this year. He has a good offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll. The Titans signed Wan’Dale Robinson in free agency and drafted Carnell Tate with the fourth overall pick in the draft. The offensive line still isn’t great, but they should be at least a league-average unit. If you watch the tape from last week , you see that Ward just doesn’t look comfortable in the pocket. He is still missing way too many easy throws, and he is bailing from the pocket too early. The offensive line didn’t play great last week, but a lot of the pressure Ward felt was his own creation. The only good thing about his performance last week was that he didn’t turn the ball over. I expect him to struggle on Sunday. In fact, my expectation is that he is going to struggle in every game until he can put three or four solid performances together. A lot has to change about the way he is playing the position before that has the possibility of happening. 3 – As you know, the Eagles and Titans don’t play very often. Who are some of the under-the-radar players that we should keep an eye out for? On defense, that guy is rookie LB Anthony Hill, Jr . He had a really solid preseason but wasn’t expected to start until LB Cedric Gray suffered a concussion in a UTV accident before Week 1. Hill filled in for Gray and was credited with 16 tackles in the loss to the Jets. That performance earned him another start this week. He’s a really rangy linebacker who has a knack for being around the ball. On offense, it would be second-year receiver Elic Ayomanor. With the additions of Robinson and Tate this offseason, Ayomanor got pushed down to fourth on the depth chart, but he scored the Titans’ only touchdown last week. The former fourth-round pick had four touchdowns last year. He’s not going to blow anyone away with his speed, but he is a good route runner who knows how to get open. With that being said, there aren’t really a lot of players on this team that are going to blow you away. 4 – If the Titans could steal one player from the Eagles’ roster, who would it be and why? (And if it’s Jalen Hurts, which non-QB?) Jalen Hurts is the obvious answer here, but since you asked for someone who is not Hurts, I’ll go with Saquon Barkley. Ward being able to turn around and hand the ball to Barkley 20+ times per game would take some of the pressure off. A dynamic running back can be a young quarterback’s best friend. The Titans have a solid running back in Tony Pollard, but he doesn’t have the home run ability at this point in his career. It would have been smart for the Titans not to let Derrick Henry walk away two years ago, but the Titans aren’t really known for making smart decisions. 5 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Titans’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The only advantage the Titans ever have from a matchup perspective is Jeffery Simmons. That should be especially advantageous this week with Landon Dickerson out. Simmons is one of the best interior defensive linemen in the league. A lot more people would be talking about him if he played on a big-market team. He should be able to take advantage of a backup offensive lineman and wreak havoc on the interior. The biggest matchup in the Eagles’ favor is Vic Fangio against Ward. Fangio is one of the best defensive coordinators in the league. He will probably have Ward confused for most of the game. If the Eagles are able to force Ward into a couple of turnovers, things will get out of hand in a hurry. 6 – Who wins this game and why? With the Eagles currently listed as 7-point road favorites, what’s your score prediction? If I were a betting man, I would bet the Eagles in this one all the way up to -10. There is just no way the Titans are going to be able to keep this game close. Eagles 31, Titans 10 .
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles roster news: Maximus Pulley temporarily elevated for Titans game
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced one roster move ahead of their Week 2 road game against the Tennessee Titans. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game. A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Maximus Pulley #36 is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced one roster move ahead of their Week 2 road game against the Tennessee Titans. S Maximus Pulley was temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. MAXIMUS PULLEY The Eagles are elevating Pulley to give themselves more depth on the back end of their defense. Starting safety Andrew Mukuba was ruled questionable to play after suffering a knee injury in practice this week. If Mukuba is unable to play, the Eagles will presumably go with Cooper DeJean and Marcus Epps as their top two safeties in base packages. With DeJean shifting to the slot in nickel formations, Michael Carter II figures to take his place at safety. Pulley is then the break glass in case of emergency backup who will ideally only play on special teams, if at all. The undrafted rookie defensive back showed some level of promise in training camp practices and preseason games but he’s more of a developmental player at this point in time. It’s at least a little interesting to see that the Eagles are temporarily elevating Pulley and NOT 2026 draft pick Cole Wisniewski. The latter spent most of the offseason injured, though, so it’s not totally shocking that Pulley is ahead of him on the depth chart right now. Had Andre’ Sam not suffered a serious injury in the Eagles’ preseason finale, he likely would’ve been the call up in this kind of situation where the team needs more safety depth. But alas. OPEN ROSTER SPOT The Eagles still have an open roster spot. They placed both Eli Stowers and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve over the past week and only signed Britian Covey. EAGLES PRACTICE SQUAD Each player below is eligible to be temporarily elevated to the active roster up to three times in the regular season unless otherwise noted. S Maximus Pulley (two elevations remaining) OL Kiran Amegadjie RB Jaydon Blue LB Chance Campbell TE Josiah Deguara WR Xavier Gipson DT Gabe Hall EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby CB Robert Longerbeam C/G Jake Majors OT John Ojukwu RB Dameon Pierce EDGE Mason Reiger RB Carson Steele EDGE Joshua Weru S Cole Wisniewski DT Uar Bernard (international exemption) … Note: the Eagles officially cut wide receiver Danny Gray from their practice squad injured list via an injury settlement on Friday.

title: NFL Picks Against the Spread: Week 2 Games
summary: Before the second Sunday of the 2026 regular season kicks off, let’s have some fun by taking a look at the lines for the NFL Week 2 games. You can CLICK HERE for straight up NFL picks without regards to the spread. My overall record this season is 9-7, which is tied with the collective […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 celebrates with his teammate DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles after scoring a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before the second Sunday of the 2026 regular season kicks off, let’s have some fun by taking a look at the lines for the NFL Week 2 games. You can CLICK HERE for straight up NFL picks without regards to the spread. My overall record this season is 9-7, which is tied with the collective BGN community at the same mark. Good to be on the right side of .500. Here are suggestions when trying to beat the odds. NFL WEEK 2 GAMES CAROLINA PANTHERS (-2.5) at ATLANTA FALCONS: The Panthers got boat-raced in Week 1 … but that game was more of a testament to the Chicago Bears than it was a massive indictment of Carolina. At least, that’s what I’m telling myself here as I refuse to bet on the team starting Cooper Rush at quarterback. PICK: Panthers -2.5 Loading… NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at BALTIMORE RAVENS (-8.5): The Saints looked mighty scrappy in Week 1. But part of the equation there is that the Detroit Lions’ defense looks atrocious. Not so sure New Orleans will have the same kind of success in Baltimore, as the Saints play back-to-back road games. The Ravens looked really good in Week 1 and I’m buying that their new coaching staff could be good. PICK: Ravens -8.5 Loading… GREEN BAY PACKERS (-3.5) at NEW YORK JETS: Not really (Jordan) loving giving either side the benefit of the doubt in this situation. The Jets aren’t for real just because they beat the lowly Titans. But maybe they’re somewhat competent? And maybe the Packers aren’t all that great if they’re getting cooked by Carson Wentz in the year 2026? I’ll roll with the home dogs. PICK: Jets +3.5 Loading… MINNESOTA VIKINGS at CHICAGO BEARS (-4.5): Worth noting that two of the Bears’ five lowest yardage outputs on offense last year came against Brian Flores. But I don’t want to bet on the combination of believing in Wentz and doubting Ben Johnson. Chicago is certainly capable of scoring enough to cover the spread. PICK: Bears -4.5 Loading… CINCINNATI BENGALS at HOUSTON TEXANS (-2.5): I’m not down on the Texans, who are in very real danger of dropping to 0-2, but I’m more comfortable backing Joe Burrow than C.J. Stroud right now. PICK: Bengals +2.5 Loading… PITTSBURGH STEELERS at NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS (-4.5): The Pats will bounce back and win this game. But losing A.J. Brown hurts and Pittsburgh should cause some issues for New England up front. The Stillers cover in a game decided by a Pats field goal. PICK: Steelers +4.5 Loading… CLEVELAND BROWNS at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS (-8.5): The Browns’ vibes are horrendous. Happy to avoid counting on Deshaun Watson to deliver. PICK: Buccaneers -8.5 Loading… PHILADELPHIA EAGLES (-7) at TENNESSEE TITANS: Let’s not overthink it: the Titans are really bad. The Eagles didn’t exactly look like a well-oiled machine in Week 1 but they should emerge victorious in this one. Vic Fanigo’s defense should cause problems for Cam Ward. The Eagles’ offensive line could be better with an ineffective Landon Dickerson coming off the field. PICK: Eagles -7 Loading… JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS at DENVER BRONCOS (-2.5): The Broncos are coming off short rest to play a Jags team that seems like they might be getting slept on. I’ll fade Denver, a prime regression candidate in 2026. PICK: Jaguars +2.5 Loading… LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS (-6.5): It’s not just about overreacting to a Week 1 loss. It’s about reaching a point with the Bolts where it’s simply impossible to give them any benefit of the doubt. I can’t possibly regret picking against them here. Even if they win, it could be a close game. PICK: Raiders +6.5 Loading… SEATTLE SEAHAWKS (-4.5) at ARIZONA CARDINALS: The reigning Super Bowl champs enter this game with extra rest having last played on September 9. And the Cards had their cute upset moment last weekend. The Seahawks won’t take them as lightly as the Chargers did. PICK: Seahawks -4.5 MIAMI DOLPHINS at SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS (-13.5): The 49ers were praised for their approach to their Week 1 Australia game. But maybe staying overseas helped them in that spot … only to hurt them coming back home to the United States? It’s a big spread to cover. Maybe the Dolphins get a little frisky. PICK: Dolphins +13.5 Loading… WASHINGTON COMMANDERS at DALLAS COWBOYS (-4.5): I’ll buy the dip on the Cowboys. If we’re going to talk about how certain teams might need some time adjusting to a new coordinator (see: Sean Mannion in Philly), then we probably shouldn’t write off Christian Parker just yet. The Commanders’ defense is the bigger concern in this matchup; Washington is weak at cornerback and Dallas obviously has the horses at wide receiver to take advantage of that secondary. PICK: Cowboys -4.5 Loading… INDIANAPOLIS COLTS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS (-6.5): The Chiefs are back. PICK: Chiefs -6.5 Loading… NEW YORK GIANTS at LOS ANGELES RAMS (-7.5): Nothing about the Giants’ Week 1 win was fluky. We’ll see if they can sustain their bully ball over the course of an entire season. But, for now, they appear to be formidable. And the Rams are taking on water as they lose Myles Garrett. The biggest hesitation here is the line seeming too good to be true. PICK: Giants +7.5 Loading…

title: The Titans are already in trouble
summary: The Titans looked really good last week. I am referring to their Houston Oilers quasi-throwback jerseys. Those are great. Their football was disgusting. The Titans offense: definitely offensive  If you thought the Eagles offense was a chore to watch last week, and it was, then avert your eyes for the Titans. At least people didn’t […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans throws a pass against the New York Jets during the second half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Titans looked really good last week. I am referring to their Houston Oilers quasi-throwback jerseys. Those are great. Their football was disgusting. The Titans offense : definitely offensive If you thought the Eagles offense was a chore to watch last week, and it was, then avert your eyes for the Titans. 3rd worst yards per play Worst yards per passing attempt Worst yards per completion They did have the 9th best yards per rushing attempt but… Fewest rushing attempts At least people didn’t have to watch a lot of it, they had the third fewest offensive plays run. They lost by 13 to the Jets . The Jets now already have a greater margin of victory in wins then they did all of last year combined , when they won three games by a total of 11 points. The Jets haven’t won by 13 or more points since Week 3 of 2024 when they beat the 3-14 Patriots 24-3. The Titans were basically the Jim Mora diddly poo rant: “Well, what happened was, that second game we got our ass kicked… or the second half, we just got our ass totally kicked. We couldn’t do diddly poo offensively. We couldn’t make a first down. We couldn’t run the ball, we didn’t try to run the ball, we couldn’t complete a pass. We sucked. The second half, we sucked. We couldn’t stop the run. Every time they got the ball, they went down and got points. We got our ass totally kicked in the second half. That’s what it boiled down to. It was a horseshit performance in the second half. Horseshit. I’m totally embarrassed and totally ashamed. Coaching we all… coaching did a horrible job. The players did a horrible job. We got our ass kicked in that second half. It sucked. It stunk.” QBs vs QBs Jeffrey Simmons got some flak for saying that the Titans defense needs to make Jalen Hurts play QB. He is correct. The Eagles offense struggles when Hurts doesn’t break defenses with his legs. The Titans best chance to win is by keeping Hurts behind the line of scrimmage. We already know this. With Jeffery Simmons and rookie LB Anthony Hill, who had bit of a breakout against the Jets, they have a puncher’s chance. But for the Eagles, their key to winning is also to make their opponent’s QB play QB because Cam Ward has simply been awful at it so far. 37 QBs have attempted at least 200 passes since the start of last season. Among them, Cam Ward is 7th worst in sack rate 5th worst in completion percentage 4th worst on target percentage 4th worst bad pass percentage 4th worst in adjusted yards per attempt 2nd worst in yards per completion 2nd worst in success rate Worst in sack yards Worst in yards per attempt Worst in pass yards per attempt on play action Worst in TD percentage Something is very wrong with the Eagles if they do not pummel the Titans. College Football Watch List 12:00 – Georgia at Arkansas Arkansas football is in a really bad spot right now, and it’s not going to get better with the Bulldogs in town. But EDGE Quincy Rhodes, Jr. , is a guy to watch. Arkansas, at least last year, lined him up all over the DL, and he produced with 8 sacks and 15.5 tackles for loss. He should test well, per Bruce Feldman’s Freaks List, where he was 66th: At 6-6, 277, he’s super strong, having bench-pressed 405 pounds, squatted 585 and power-cleaned 375. He broad-jumped 10-2, vertical-jumped 30 inches and clocked 19.97 mph on the GPS. 3:30 – SMU at Louisville Howie Roseman loves his raw international prospects. SMU TE Theo Melin Ohrstrom (6’6”, 250) is a fifth year senior from Sweden who spent the past four seasons at Texas A&M. He has just 32 career catches, all in the last three years, so while he has more polish than the international players the Eagles have brought in, he is still far from a finished prospect. He had two easy TDs last week against UC-Davis, perhaps that gets him a little more playing time this week. 7:30 – LSU at Ole Miss Suddenly, but not really that suddenly, guard is an issue for the Eagles. Ole Miss RG Patrick Kutas fits the Eagles profile: he’s 6’6” and 315 pounds. He’s also played right tackle, left guard, and center. Good luck against LSU!

title: Eagles News: Makai Lemon “just doesn’t look ready”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles aren’t being fair to Makai Lemon by putting him on the field before he’s fully ready. There should be more of a timeshare when it comes to the third wide receiver role, at least early on in the season […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles aren’t being fair to Makai Lemon by putting him on the field before he’s fully ready. There should be more of a timeshare when it comes to the third wide receiver role, at least early on in the season as Lemon is still catching up to speed. They’re also not doing him any favors by how they’re utilizing him on designed touches where the defense does not look fooled at all. Now, watch Lemon go out and have a big game against the Titans on Sunday. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Random Observations: What do the Eagles need to fix immediately? – NBCSP GET MAKAI LEMON OUTTA THERE: Not saying Makai Lemon is a bust. Way too early for that kind of talk. But he just doesn’t seem to be in a place right now where he’s confident enough in himself and comfortable enough in this offense to make plays to help the Eagles win football games. The Eagles have a pretty good slot option in Elijah Moore, who averaged 50 catches for over 500 yards per season from 2021 through 2024 and is coming off a solid training camp. Moore isn’t a superstar, but he’s a proven NFL veteran who looked good in this offense while Lemon was sitting out camp with a hamstring injury. Why Lemon played 35 offensive snaps Sunday while Moore was inactive, I don’t understand. Lemon had four targets for negative-five yards Sunday, becoming the sixth NFL WR since 1977, as far back as target totals are available on Stathead, to have at least four targets for negative five yards or less. He’s the second WR since 1977 with negative-five or fewer yards in his NFL debut, following Brandon Banks of Washington in 2010. And he’s the first 1st-round WR with negative-5 or fewer yards in a game since Jalen Reagor had minus-6 against the Chargers in 2021 . He’s also the first 1st-round WR ever with minus-5 or fewer yards in his NFL debut. He just doesn’t look ready. The Eagles seem committed to getting him going and maybe he’ll start turning things around Sunday against a bad Titans team. But the guy I saw out there against Washington just didn’t look NFL ready. Film Preview: Eagles should have success against this Titans defense – BGN I expected a Robert Saleh defense to be relatively simple to identify. He usually has plenty of zone coverage, four-man rushes, and a front that lets its best players get after the quarterback. That is broadly what Tennessee showed against the Jets. I did not expect so much confusion behind it. The secondary repeatedly lost track of assignments after ordinary motion and shifts, the pass rush barely affected Geno Smith, and the run fits broke down in some surprisingly basic ways. This was a poor defensive performance. The Eagles just have to hope for more of the same this week… NFC East Mixtape Vol. 190: Week 2 Preview | Someone Will Be 0-2 – NFC East Mixtape YouTube A new week is upon us and it is a big one for the NFC East. The currently first-place New York Giants will look to prove to everyone that they are fully for real, and with a Monday Night Football stage against the Los Angeles Rams if they do so… things might really be legitimate. This should be an easy week for the Philadelphia Eagles with the Tennessee Titans on deck… right? Elsewhere the battle of the 0-1 teams is upon us as the Dallas Cowboys host the Washington Commanders. Somebody will find some optimism with a win… and somebody is going to fall to 0-2 overall AND within the division. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Gowton discuss it all on the latest NFC East Mixtape! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Titans vs. Eagles predictions: Pain – Music City Miracles I’d love to have a positive prediction for the Tennessee Titans in their week two matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles, but I honestly cannot come up with one. The Titans looked so bad against the New York Jets last week. The Eagles are a much better team than the Jets. There is no reason to think this week will look any different. Hats off to any of you who are going to the game on Sunday. It is going to be 100 degrees, and the stadium is going to be mostly Eagles fans. That doesn’t sound like a fun afternoon to me. Game Preview – PHI at TEN – Iggles Blitz Improved OL play will help the passing game as well. Geno Smith was 19 for 24 last week vs Tennessee and wasn’t sacked once. Hurts was 14 for 25 vs Washington and got sacked 3 times. Give Hurts a cleaner pocket and his numbers should go up. It will also help if the Eagles face fewer 3rd & long situations. As for the Eagles defense, they won’t be facing a dynamic QB or offense this week. Tennessee gained 195 yards and scored 10 points last week. Cam Ward is 3-15 in his 18 career starts. The Titans have scored more than 24 points three times in that stretch. Ward is an athletic QB with good mobility, but he doesn’t like to run. He moves around to buy time as a passer. That would be great if he had a better OL and his receivers got open more consistently. Ward has developed bad habits with his mechanics and that leads to some erratic throws. Eagles’ new perspective for ’26: Don’t ‘let anyone steal our joy’ – ESPN The Philadelphia Eagles beat the Washington Commanders 24-22 in the season opener and were consciously making an effort in the game’s aftermath to let that be enough. “Last year, I know everyone [would] try to make something of, we won by two points. We’re not getting on that this year. And that’s a beautiful thing,” running back Saquon Barkley said. “We come out with a win, we’re going to be happy, we’re going to celebrate and we’re going to flush it and move on and get ready for next week.” That was the core of coach Nick Sirianni’s postgame message to the team, players said: that, as receiver/returner Britain Covey put it, “We’re not going to let anyone steal our joy from the wins.” Philadelphia has felt like Whoville at times in recent years, with inflated expectations and over analysis swiping the gift of victory with a Grinch-like harshness. Such an environment — where there’s such angst over a four-year stretch in which the team has gone 51-18, reached two Super Bowl and won one — is only possible when outsized standards are enforced by members of the organization and its city alike. And it’s no coincidence that the mood inside the locker room and out was at its most sullen in 2023 and ’25, two seasons following Super Bowl runs when good was in the shadows of great. Eagles vs. Titans: Predictions, odds, injury updates, and why everyone is talking about the weather in Week 2 – Inquirer Davis, who is from North Carolina and played his college football at Georgia and all across the American South, knew he was in for a long day long before the game started. “It’s when you’re walking out, the warmup before the warmup, and you’re already sweating in like two minutes,” he said. “You didn’t even finish stretching yet, and you’re dripping. “I don’t like that feeling.” He won’t be able to avoid it Sunday. The Eagles and Titans play in Nashville at noon local time, and the city is under a heat advisory. Temperatures are expected to be in the mid-90s, and the feel on the field could reach triple digits, just like it did in Tampa, Fla., each of the last two years. Nick Sirianni studies everything his team does, down to travel times and all that goes into a trip. The Eagles had another early-season game in Tampa last year, and they took their data from…

title: Steelers expect Joey Porter Jr to play Week 3
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will be without Joey Porter Jr for the second straight game to open the 2026 season. Porter spent the offseason and training camp hoping to get a contract extension. A deal didn’t get done, and Porter has been dealing with what the team classified as a back injury during the process. However, […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 2: Joey Porter Jr. #24 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Pittsburgh, United States. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers will be without Joey Porter Jr for the second straight game to open the 2026 season. Porter spent the offseason and training camp hoping to get a contract extension. A deal didn’t get done, and Porter has been dealing with what the team classified as a back injury during the process. However, he could take the field in Week 3. Per Adam Schefter, the Steelers are planning for Porter to play next week against the Cincinnati Bengals. “The Pittsburgh Steelers are planning for Joey Porter Jr., who has missed the first two games of the season, to potentially return for their Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals, sources told ESPN,” Schefter reports . That said, as there has been with every step of the way, there is another potential turn to the story. Schefter adds that Porter is seeking a second opinion on his back injury. “Porter’s back, according to a source, has ‘flared up when he’s tried to go full speed, and they haven’t been able to get it where it needs to be.‘ Porter has been considering getting a second opinion on his back,” Schefter notes. As this seemingly never-ending saga continues, the Steelers will take the field at 1:00 EST to try to get to 2-0 on the year when they face the New England Patriots. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Steelers Week 2 game picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and New England Patriots will square off today in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. Pittsburgh won this matchup last season by the score of 21-14 off the strength of five takeaways. Can they win consecutive matchups against New England and get to 2-0? Here is how our staff sees things […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 21: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scrambles during the second quarter against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers and New England Patriots will square off today in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. Pittsburgh won this matchup last season by the score of 21-14 off the strength of five takeaways. Can they win consecutive matchups against New England and get to 2-0? Here is how our staff sees things playing out. Ryan Parish (1-0): The Steelers won this matchup a year ago thanks to some turnover luck. I think they will need more of that as the Patriots were a much different team by the end of the season.Fortunately for Pittsburgh, the Patriots’ offense is in a bit of disarray and is shorthanded following the injury to A.J. Brown. The Pats do get TreVeyon Henderson back, but how effective will he be in his first game back? The Steelers’ offense will likely still be uneven, especially with wide receiver Michael Pittman out, but I think the defense can lead them to another ugly win. Steelers 20, Patriots 17 Ryland Bickley (1-0): I was leaning towards a Steelers win, but Michael Pittman Jr.’s sudden absence feels like a big deal after he was the team’s most consistent wide receiver last week. I’m confident Germie Bernard will step into a bigger role on offense some time this season, but after barely seeing the field last week, it might be too early to expect much –especially considering Aaron Rodgers’ demands of receivers. The Patriots are certainly a beatable team, especially with wide receiver AJ Brown out, but Drake Maye is a different class of quarterback from the Falcons’ Cooper Rush, who the Pittsburgh defense easily handled last week. It could be a different story Week 2. I’m expecting a close game that could go either way. Steelers 20, Patriots 17 Austin Bechtold (1-0): I’m concerned with the Steelers offensive line facing a more vaunted pass rush than the Falcons. Missing Michael Pittman Jr. should unlock playing time for Germie Bernard, but does Aaron Rodgers trust him? Does DK Metcalf bounce back? Drake Maye can’t possibly be as bad as he was against the Steelers last year. New England might not be the house of horrors it used to be for the Steelers, but I think the Patriots do enough in the 4th quarter with multiple question marks surrounding the Steelers offense and its capabilities. The defense should force a turnover or two, but I don’t see it being enough and the absence of Joey Porter Jr. will be felt more than most of us think. Patriots 24, Steelers 21 . Mike Nicastro (1-0): The Steelers and Patriots rosters are comparable, but this is a tough spot for Pittsburgh in what feels like a must win for New England. After losing to Seattle on opening night, they risk falling to 0-2, prior to heading to play on the road at Jacksonville and Buffalo. The Steelers defense will most certainly keep them in the game, but ultimately Drake Maye will make too many plays with his legs. The potential absence of Michael Pittman Jr. looms large, as shutdown corner Christian Gonzalez will likely blanket DK Metcalf most of the game. For the Steelers to win, Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard will need to have the games of their lives. It’s a tough spot in wet conditions. Patriots 20 Steelers 16 . Joey Bray (1-0): The Pittsburgh Steelers beat this same team in this same location last season. However, it’s hard to imagine the Steelers force five turnovers this time around against a very well coached New England team. The absence of key pass catchers should make offense harder to come by in his contest. Drake Maye will be without AJ Brown, while Aaron Rodgers will be without Michael Pittman Jr. I’ll take New England to get back on track and pick up a win at home. Patriots 17, Steelers 13 . Jason Aponte (1-0): Michael Pittman is down, but this feels like a perfect squeaky wheel game for DK Metcalf. Christian Gonzalez is a problem, but he’ll still be involved. The Patriots missing A.J. brown means more than anyone wants to let on. It’ll be ugly, but Pittsburgh goes 2-0. Steelers 21, Patriots 17. Jarrett Bailey (1-0): I’ve gone back and forth on what I believe will happen here. No Michael Pittman means Roman Wilson and/or Germie Bernard need to step up. The Steelers also need to be able to have some semblance of a ground attack, which they didn’t have against the Falcons in Week 1. I picked the Patriots on the latest episode of The Pump Fake (shameless plug, join me and Todd Haley for three shows per week), so I’ll stick with that here, though I certainly do see a path where the Steelers prove me wrong. Patriots 24, Steelers 23. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! Kindle Vildor an option on practice squad. — Mike Reiss (@MikeReiss) September 19, 2026 Davis is a 6’1 and 200-pound cornerback in his ninth NFL season. He’s been a starter for two defenses that have made the Super Bowl: last year’s Patriots, as well as the Super Bowl LV-winning Buccaneers. Davis has never made a Pro Bowl, but he has quietly become one of the better No. 2 corners on an NFL depth chart. In 2025, among defensive backs with at least 300 coverage snaps, he was ranked 25th in Tight Window percentage (27.5%) and tied for 19th in average yards of separation allowed (2.3), according to Next Gen stats. Davis allowed a catch rate of just 56.5% and a catch rate over expectation (CROE) of -1.1%. To give you an idea of how those numbers compare to an elite cover corner, just look at his teammate Christian Gonzalez, who posted a 52.5% catch rate, -7.8% CROE, and a 20% tight window rate a year ago. To make another comparison, Marcus Jones — who is expected to slide into Davis’ spot — had a catch rate of 68.7%, a +3.7% CROE, and a 26.9% tight window rate while allowing 3.3 average yards of separation. This is a big loss for New England and could provide an opportunity for Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers to exploit on Sunday. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Patriots DC calls Darnell Washington a ‘big challenge’
summary: The New England Patriots have plenty to prepare for as they get set to face the Pittsburgh Steelers, and tight end Darnell Washington presents a particularly difficult matchup. Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr singled out Washington as a “big challenge,” pointing to the fourth-year tight end’s rare combination of size, strength and athleticism. Washington has […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Darnell Washington #80 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs the ball against Xavier Watts #31 of the Atlanta Falcons during the fourth quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots have plenty to prepare for as they get set to face the Pittsburgh Steelers, and tight end Darnell Washington presents a particularly difficult matchup. Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr singled out Washington as a “big challenge,” pointing to the fourth-year tight end’s rare combination of size, strength and athleticism. Washington has increasingly become an important part of the Steelers’ offense, particularly in the running game. His ability to block at the point of attack while also serving as a legitimate receiving threat makes him a difficult player for opposing defenses to account for. “He’s athletic,” Kuhr said. “Obviously, his size and strength are no joke.” Kuhr noted that Washington’s impact as a blocker has been evident on film, but his versatility extends beyond simply creating running lanes. When Washington gets the ball in his hands, his combination of power and athleticism can create problems for defenders. Despite the Steelers running a less tight end-heavy offense under new head coach Mike McCarthy, Washington played 43 of the team’s 67 total offensive snaps last week. Kuhr also emphasized that Washington can make the first defender miss, putting additional pressure on the Patriots to tackle well and maintain proper technique. “He’s a great piece to have,” Kuhr said. “He is a conflict piece.” That description could be particularly significant against Pittsburgh. Washington’s presence can force New England to account for both his blocking ability and what he can do as a receiver, creating uncertainty for the defense before the snap. For the Steelers, Washington’s continued development gives them another way to stress opposing defenses — and New England clearly views the 6-foot-7 tight end as one of the more difficult players it will have to handle. Last year, Washington didn’t record a single catch against the Patriots. This year, he’ll hope to change that.

title: What the Seahawks need less of, more of in Week 2: The Price of penalties
summary: Let’s open up a new series highlighting underrated storylines in the positive and “negative” as we transition between matchups throughout the season. Every week there will be the things that the Seattle Seahawks will want to mash the gas on, and things they will want to rethink or address. This is an offense-heavy look at […]
full_text: Let’s open up a new series highlighting underrated storylines in the positive and “negative” as we transition between matchups throughout the season. Every week there will be the things that the Seattle Seahawks will want to mash the gas on, and things they will want to rethink or address. This is an offense-heavy look at the Seahawks against the New England Patriots, and how it can translate into the next matchup against the Cardinals. That’s because nobody in Seattle-land is very worried about the defense after that opening performance. Patriots quarterback and former MVP runner-up, Drake Maye, was 1-6 with 3 interceptions on throws over 15 air yards, according to ESPN Insights . Now, the question is, can the ‘Hawks score without Sam Darnold? Because I believe in the bad news first, and ending on a positive, let’s do it this way: Less of … Procedural penalties The Seattle Seahawks committed seven pre-play penalties in the NFL opener. The first seven flags in total all went against the Hawks, and 10 of 15 total. Seattle drew seven or more total penalties in only five instances in the entire previous season. Opening the year with 10 total penalties, seven before the other team is even flagged, and seven on play infrastructure and operations ALONE is a dramatic uptick. Those procedural fouls included: four false starts (Saubert, Lucas, Bradford, and Barner), one offsides penalty (Lucas again, who had a surprisingly rough game), one illegal shift and one delay of game. That’s not great. Should we chalk it up to first-time action for starters, a new offensive coordinator, or a replacement at QB? That very OC, Brian Fleury, talked about how he called plays that were not originally in the gameplan against the Patriots, but, “it was not because of Drew, it was more because of how New England came out and played us in a four down nickel package — which was not what we expected — so we were able to adjust to that pretty quickly, as a coaching staff.” He goes on to say that “I go through an absurd amount of contingency plans.” The Seattle offense gained traction, however, in the 2nd half and scored all 13 of their points after the break. Drew Lock was safe, mobile and decisive, and earned a QB Rating (113.3) that dwarfed that of young star, Drake Maye’s (54.9). Fleury in the desired quadrant https://t.co/ulk0gW3wrE — Seahawk Nerd (@SeahawkNerd) September 15, 2026 We might be seeing the very best version of Andrew Lock, in this offense. Oh, and Coach Fleury has been game planning against Arizona, and specifically holdover, Nick Rallis as a DC for a few years now. The QB-OC tandem may not be the biggest concern going into the Seahawks’ first divisional matchup. Still, the Cardinals should not be overlooked. They put belt to biscuits against the heavily favored L.A. Chargers last week. They picked off Justin Herbert, sacked him 3 times and forced a fumble on Omarion Hampton. Arizona held the Bolts under 200 passing yards and under 100 rushing yards while not turning the ball over on offense. Sure, the Patriots defense has stars, newly formed cohesion and great coaching. They do not have a Josh Sweat as a pass rusher, and they do not have Budda Baker (with all due respect to the emerging Craig Woodson and the still-kickin’ Kevin Byard III) roaming the back end who has seen it all. Fleury stated that “I didn’t have any concerns about handing it to Drew.” Where does the Seahawks OC’s calm demeanor come from? The coordinator explained: “I’ve been through losing quarterbacks, and unfortunately, challenging circumstances before.” Touché. Remember that Fleury was a run game coordinator for the 49ers and had a hand in game planning as well as gameday play-calling suggestions when Mac Jones took over for an injured Brock Purdy. Jones drummed up a slight QB controversy (on the notoriously level-headed app called X) with his play in relief, because he had a higher QB Rating than the starter for a good portion of the season. Two different situations — and I don’t expect for things to look exactly the same here, but we can expect Fleury, Macdonald and the offense to have a plan. At least to spend a little time ironing out all the pre-snap stutters that sabotaged drives and put the offense behind the sticks. The red birds at least deserve that much respect. More of! Jadarian Price Nehemiah Pritchett was my first instinct. Filling in for Nick Emmanwori, the young player they call “Mighty” lived up to that name, as Pritchett was a force against the run and the pass. Him coming in as the 3rd cornerback and sliding Devon Witherspoon into the slot looked good, even against a running team. Can he relegate both Trevon Diggs and Terrion Arnold to simply depth pieces? Seattle will probably also want to utilize Tyrice Knight in early down scenarios, but his play did not jump off the tape in the same way as Pritchett’s did. Still, I trust Macdonald to get that ratio right. Especially with a unique threat, such as Trey McBride next on the docket. The true “More of” this week is more of rookie half back, Jadarian Price in a somewhat contrived “revenge game.” The media will make light of who makes more of an impact this week: he, or his former Notre Dame backfield mate, Jeremiyah Love of Arizona. It’s not that reason (alone) that 12’s will want to see Price get more play. Seattle likes what George Holani brings to the table on 3rd downs, and they likely want to make sure he’s an established threat on the ground in his own right, so as not to tip off a pass play, but the rookie proved significantly more efficient with his carries. More bell cow! View Link Price rumbled for 5.2 yards per carry on 10 attempts, while Holani picked up 3.6 on his 8 attempts. Former Seahawks fullback Michael Robinson accidentally came up with an incredible new nickname for Holani, when he was on the call for their preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys. I do not want you all to be confused when I start using it, so here is the story. During the game, Mike Rob mentioned George Holani as “Steady Eddie” (like the colloquialism) George… then realized what he said was confusing, not meaning to call him Eddie George. And thus, the nickname Steady George is born! There were some pass plays that worked out for Drew Lock and the Seattle Seahawks last Wednesday because of the elite pass protection reps of “Steady George” Holani. And yet, seeing what Price can do with a full workload remains an enticing thought, heading to the desert. This is especially true with Christian Haynes set to start in Anthony Bradford’s stead at right guard . Keep that line moving forward! Fleury mentioned that “it was his very first NFL game,” and that the 1st-Round rookie has “obviously earned more reps moving forward.” Yes, please.

title: Seahawks injury update: Anthony Bradford ruled out of Cardinals game
summary: The Seattle Seahawks officially downgraded starting right guard Anthony Bradford to out on Saturday, ahead of their matchup with the Arizona Cardinals. Bradford was limited throughout the week with a knee and hip injury and listed as questionable on the Seahawks’ Friday injury report. With Bradford out, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Anthony Bradford #75 of the Seattle Seahawks defends during an NFC Championship NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks officially downgraded starting right guard Anthony Bradford to out on Saturday, ahead of their matchup with the Arizona Cardinals. Bradford was limited throughout the week with a knee and hip injury and listed as questionable on the Seahawks’ Friday injury report . With Bradford out, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team will look to third-year guard Christian Haynes to fill his role up front. If Haynes gets the start, it will be his first since he was drafted by the Seahawks in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft. This will be the first game that Bradford has not started for the Seahawks since the back-end of the 2024 season, when he hurt his ankle against the Cardinals. In addition to downgrading Bradford, the Seahawks activated safety Rodney Thomas II from the practice squad. Thomas fills an obvious need at safety with Ty Okada ruled out and Nick Emmanwori listed as questionable for Sunday’s divisional game. Thomas, a 2022 seventh-round pick by the Indianapolis Colts, signed to Seattle’s practice squad this offseason after four years with the Colts. The Yale grad starred in his first year in Indy, recording four interceptions and 52 tackles, but gradually fell out of favor and started zero games last year. The Seahawks elevated Thomas in Week 1 against the New England Patriots, where he contributed four tackles and deflected the pass that became Nehemiah Pritchett’s interception in Seattle’s 13-10 win. Seattle may need another impressive outing from Thomas against a red-hot Cardinals team fresh off upsetting the Los Angeles Chargers last week.

title: An All-22 review of the good and bad from Seahawks vs. Patriots
summary: After months of waiting to finally see this version of the Seattle Seahawks on the field, the season opener quickly looked like it might turn into a disaster. The Seahawks had spent the offseason trying to maintain the defense that carried them to a Super Bowl title, only to see injuries hit the secondary before […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Nehemiah Pritchett #28 of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass intended for Romeo Doubs #87 of the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images After months of waiting to finally see this version of the Seattle Seahawks on the field, the season opener quickly looked like it might turn into a disaster. The Seahawks had spent the offseason trying to maintain the defense that carried them to a Super Bowl title, only to see injuries hit the secondary before the game. Then, just five plays into the season, Sam Darnold went down with a glute injury and suddenly Drew Lock was running the offense. Seattle eventually rallied for a 13-10 victory over the New England Patriots , but the final score doesn’t tell the whole story. There were plenty of things to like on the tape, particularly from Mike Macdonald’s defense, but there were also some issues that could become much more costly against better opponents. Let’s get into the good and bad from Seattle’s season opener. The Bad Too many self-inflicted wounds Seattle committed 10 accepted penalties for 98 yards against New England. That is a difficult number to overcome under any circumstances, but it becomes even more concerning when you consider how those penalties affected the scoreboard. The Patriots scored all 10 of their points with the help of Seattle penalties. The first touchdown drive was extended by a defensive pass interference penalty on Josh Jobe, while another drive that could have ended with Seattle getting the football back was revived by a penalty on the punting unit by Chazz Surratt. Those mistakes gave New England extra opportunities and helped turn what should have been defensive wins into points. That’s the kind of thing that can be brushed aside when you win 13-10. It becomes much harder to overlook when you’re playing a team that can actually punish you consistently. And there were other penalties that didn’t directly produce points but still put Seattle behind the chains or erased positive plays. For a team that was already dealing with injuries in the secondary and eventually had to play without its starting quarterback, giving an opponent free yardage and extra possessions was about as close to shooting yourself in the foot as it gets. Seattle’s defense was good enough to overcome it this time. It won’t always be. Keep the quarterback in the pocket The Seahawks need to improve their discipline in keeping the QB inside the pocket. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-18T20:05:50.493Z This was another issue that stood out on tape. Drake Maye finished the game with seven carries for 47 yards, including five first downs on the ground. That’s far too much production from a quarterback who was already struggling to consistently create through the air. And this wasn’t simply about Maye being a good athlete. Drake Maye escaping from the pressure — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-19T01:30:05.139Z Seattle occasionally lost contain while trying to collapse the pocket, giving Maye opportunities to escape rather than forcing him to throw from a shrinking pocket. Those extra yards kept drives alive and put additional stress on a defense that was otherwise doing a very good job of limiting New England’s offense. Maye ultimately finished with 178 passing yards and three interceptions, but the rushing production was one of the few ways New England consistently created positive plays. This is something to monitor going forward, particularly against quarterbacks who are even more dangerous as runners. Abe Lucas was not quite himself The offensive line overall had a pretty solid night. That might sound strange considering Seattle’s offense struggled for long stretches, but the unit did enough to keep the offense functional after Drew Lock entered the game. Lock was sacked only once (Sam Darnold was also sacked on the play in which he got injured), and Seattle finished with 200 gross passing yards and 188 net passing yards. But if there was one offensive lineman who looked a little below his usual standard, it was Abe Lucas. That’s notable because Lucas has generally been one of the more consistent pieces of this offensive line when healthy. His ability to quietly win reps on the edge has made him one of the more dependable players up front. Seattle runs play-action with a simulated pull from RG Anthony Bradford, a concept Brian Fleury uses often. Lucas should work inside-out on No. 5, but after losing his first step, he can't recover and gives up pressure. pic.twitter.com/bv8BEQYpsa — Alexandre Castro (@alexcastrofilho) September 19, 2026 Seattle runs a play-action concept with a simulated pull from right guard Anthony Bradford, something Brian Fleury has gone to fairly often. I think Lucas’ approach here should be to block No. 5 (Dre’Mont Jones) from the inside out. After losing on his first step, Lucas can’t recover quickly enough and ultimately gives up pressure. The fateful play that ended Darnold’s day. Lucas starts well with good posture, a clean pass set and solid contact on Dre’ Jones. Pressure isn’t immediate, but Lucas gets turned around and ends the rep trying to block Jones with his back. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-19T01:50:54.309Z This was the fateful play that ended Sam Darnold’s day. Lucas starts well: good posture, clean pass set and solid contact on Dre’ Jones. The pressure isn’t immediate, but as the rep develops, Lucas gets turned around and ends up trying to block Jones with his back. That’s where the rep goes wrong. Great effort sack by Gabe Jacas. Lucas takes an inside set while watching the No. 4 blitz threat. His hand placement is off, and he has to let Jacas go to avoid a hold. That gives Jacas the opening to finish the sack. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-19T01:57:19.214Z This was a great effort sack by Gabe Jacas. Abe Lucas takes an inside set while keeping his eyes on the blitz threat from No. 4. Maybe he loses his vision at some point, but his hand placement is wrong, forcing him to let Jacas go to avoid a holding penalty. Jacas finishes the play. It wasn’t a disastrous performance, and I wouldn’t read too much into one game. But compared with what we’ve come to expect from Lucas, this was a step down. The Good Mike Macdonald is still finding new ways to attack quarterbacks Mike Macdonald is a maniac with Drake Thomas as Cloud CB, but Maye never should have thrown that pass. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-19T02:49:20.282Z One of the hardest things about staying at the top of the NFL is finding ways to remain unpredictable. Defenses eventually get studied. Tendencies get identified. Opposing quarterbacks become more comfortable recognizing your structures. Mike Macdonald still found ways to make Drake Maye uncomfortable. Mike Macdonald blitz from slot. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-19T02:11:34.473Z Macdonald repeatedly sent pressure from the slot, something that worked well in the Super Bowl. New England countered by having quick flat options for Drake Maye to get the ball out before pressure arrived. Seattle crowds the line, showing a heavy blitz with the LBs and Julian Love. Hall and DeMarcus Lawrence occupy the OL before dropping, while Spoon comes free from the slot. New England keeps seven in protection but has no answer, forcing Maye to throw it away. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-19T02:12:52.855Z Here, Seattle crowds the line, showing a heavy blitz with the LBs and Julian Love. It initially looks like Spoon won’t rush, and the defense executes with great communication. Derick Hall and DeMarcus Lawrence occupy the OL until they see Love and Spoon coming, then drop into coverage. New England keeps seven in protection but has no answer for Spoon, who comes free and forces Maye to throw it away. Brian Fleury had a good debut, all things…
