title: Seahawks Reacts results: Fans expect Jadarian Price to out-rush Jeremiyah Love in Week 2
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys.  Entering Week 2 of the 2026 season, the Seattle Seahawks seem to be riding a cautiously […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up prior to an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. Entering Week 2 of the 2026 season, the Seattle Seahawks seem to be riding a cautiously optimistic wave. The defending Super Bowl champions are 1-0 after narrowly defeating the New England Patriots. However, in that effort they lost their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold for at least a few weeks . With these highs and lows of week one, how do Seahawk fans feel heading into their week two game against the Arizona Cardinals? Well, it appears that Seattle fans are feeling quite confident. When asked if the Seahawks are heading in the right direction, a whopping 95% of polled fans said the team is headed in the right direction. And honestly, who could blame them. Despite losing Darnold to a glute injury, Mike Macdonald’s defense put on a show against the Patriots. In addition to this, backup quarterback, Drew Lock has proven multiple times now that he can lead the team to a victory. Another positive coming out of week one for the Seahawks was how Jadarian Price looked in his NFL debut. Although Price only had 24 snaps in week one, his workload is expected to increase. When asked about the light workload for Price, offensive coordinator, Brian Fleury stated that they “ wanted to be cautious in terms of his workload.” Fleury went on to state that Price has “earned more reps moving forward .” Perhaps this statement from Fleury helped inspire Seahawk fans’ optimism in Price as well. When asked which former Notre Dame running back will have more rushing yards on Sunday, 82% of polled Seahawk fans voted for Price. The other 18% of polled Seahawk fans voted for Price’s former teammate, and fellow rookie, Jeremiyah Love. In week one, Price ran the ball 10 times for 52 yards . In comparison, Love ran the ball 11 times for 41 yards . Although the poll only looked at rushing yards, for those who are curious, Price also caught two passes for six yards, while Love caught two passes for nine yards. As you can see, these stat lines are awfully close with Price having the slight edge after week one. It will be fascinating to see how these two former teammates compare not only next week against the Cardinals, but also deeper into the 2026 season. Both are in somewhat similar positions on the depth chart this season. Both backs are number one, however they both have some veteran running backs in their room who will steal some carries away. In Arizona, Love has Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight behind him. In Seattle, Price has George Holani and Emanuel Wilson behind him. Both backs also have big name veterans currently on injured lists who will surely take carries away when they both get back healthy. For Love in Arizona, that is James Conner (who is currently on injured reserve). For Price in Seattle, that is Charbonnet (who is currently on the physically unable to perform list.) This will surely be one to watch all season. Check out FanDuel , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.

title: Seahawks vs. Cardinals, Week 2 preview: Can Seattle win its 12th straight?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are heading to Arizona for their first road game of the 2026 season, and if history is any indication, we probably shouldn’t expect a normal afternoon. State Farm Stadium has been the setting for some particularly memorable moments in Seahawks history. It was where Quandre Diggs suffered a gruesome leg injury in […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are heading to Arizona for their first road game of the 2026 season, and if history is any indication, we probably shouldn’t expect a normal afternoon. State Farm Stadium has been the setting for some particularly memorable moments in Seahawks history. It was where Quandre Diggs suffered a gruesome leg injury in Seattle’s 2021 season finale, a game that also turned out to be Russell Wilson’s final game in a Seahawks uniform. It was also the site of Super Bowl XLIX, one of the most painful games in franchise history. More recently, last year’s meeting in Glendale followed the same general script: Seattle appeared to have control before Arizona made things unnecessarily interesting. The Seahawks led 20-6 in the fourth quarter, only to watch the Cardinals tie the game before Jason Myers hit a 52-yard field goal with 28 seconds remaining. And even that doesn’t tell the whole story. In that 2025 game, Seattle cornerback Coby Bryant intercepted Kyler Murray, only to fumble the ball and have Arizona recover it. So, yeah. Nothing normal. Before the season began, this looked like a game Seattle should win comfortably. The Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions, Arizona went 3-14 last season, and Seattle appeared to have the more talented roster. Then Week 1 happened. Seattle lost Sam Darnold on the fifth play of the season before rallying behind Drew Lock and its defense to beat New England 13-10. Arizona, meanwhile, walked into SoFi Stadium and upset the Chargers 26-14. Suddenly, this doesn’t look quite so straightforward. What can Drew Lock show with a full week as the starter? Drew Lock is no longer being thrown into the game with almost no preparation. That’s the biggest difference between Week 1 and Week 2. Against New England, Lock entered after Darnold was injured and initially looked understandably uncomfortable. The offense struggled to find much rhythm, and Seattle remained scoreless until late in the third quarter. But as the game progressed, Lock settled down and helped lead two fourth-quarter scoring drives. He finished 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown, with no interceptions, while also adding 13 rushing yards. The numbers are encouraging, but the more interesting question is what happens when Arizona takes away the first read. Drew Lock went 3-8 for 35 yards against man coverage against man coverage. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-18T19:52:30.351Z That’s where Lock’s performance against man coverage becomes particularly important. Arizona will have to decide how aggressively it wants to play Seattle’s receivers. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba coming off an eight-catch, 122-yard performance against New England, the Cardinals can’t just sit in soft zone and allow Lock to take easy completions underneath. That should create opportunities for man coverage, especially on third downs and in the red zone. This is where Lock has to show that the Week 1 comeback wasn’t a product of the defense giving him favorable circumstances. Can he identify leverage before the snap? Can he recognize when the Cardinals are playing true man versus a zone structure that initially looks like man? And, most importantly, can he deliver the ball on time when the receiver wins immediately? He’ll have a full week of starting reps to answer those questions. That’s a very different situation from what he faced against New England. The Seahawks cannot afford to beat themselves If there was one obvious problem in Seattle’s season opener, it wasn’t the offense or Drew Lock. It was discipline. The Seahawks were flagged 10 times for 98 yards against the Patriots. But the raw number doesn’t fully explain the problem. Seattle effectively gifted New England all 10 of its points through two separate penalties. The first came when Josh Jobe was flagged for defensive pass interference on an underthrown ball at the goal line, putting the Patriots in position to score a touchdown. Later, a roughing-the-punter penalty on fourth down revived another New England drive that should have ended with Seattle getting the ball back. Those are exactly the kinds of mistakes a team cannot afford on the road, particularly when playing without its starting quarterback. Seattle was already making life difficult for itself offensively. Adding free yards and extra possessions to the equation is asking the defense to do too much. And this becomes even more important in the red zone. The Seahawks committed several penalties in situations where they had forced New England into difficult spots. Against the Patriots, the defense was good enough to overcome those mistakes. The Seahawks need to improve their discipline in keeping the QB inside the pocket. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-18T20:05:50.493Z Discipline also extends beyond penalties. Seattle has to maintain discipline in its pass rush. One thing that showed up at times last season was the defense getting too aggressive trying to hunt the quarterback. The result was an occasional loss of rush-lane integrity, allowing mobile quarterbacks to step through the pocket or escape through an open edge. Drake Maye rushed for 47 yards against Seattle in Week 1, including several scrambles created when the pocket broke down. Jacoby Brissett is not the same type of athlete, but he’s also not a statue. He showed against the Chargers that he can make plays with his legs when necessary, and Arizona’s offense doesn’t need him to become a dual-threat quarterback to make those plays matter. Seattle’s pass rush needs to collapse the pocket without creating escape lanes. The goal isn’t to get pressure; it’s to get pressure while keeping the quarterback contained. Can Seattle find answers for Trey McBride? This might be the most interesting matchup on the other side of the ball. Trey McBride just finished Arizona’s opener with nine receptions for 95 yards and a touchdown. That wasn’t particularly surprising for anyone who has watched him against Seattle. McBride has consistently been a problem for the Seahawks. In eight career games against the Seahawks, he has totaled 36 catches for 579 yards and two touchdowns , averaging 72.4 yards per game. His production has also increased significantly in recent meetings. In 2024, he caught 12 passes for 133 yards in Seattle’s 16-6 win in November, setting a career high in receptions at the time, before following it up with seven catches for 70 yards in the rematch later that season. Then, in the most recent meeting between the teams, McBride caught nine of 13 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown despite Arizona losing 44-22. That’s three games of at least 70 receiving yards in a four-game span against Seattle, including two 100-yard performances. The earlier meetings were much quieter — he had three catches for 29 yards in 2023, three for 34 yards and a touchdown in the 2023 finale, and no catches in either of his two meetings with Seattle as a rookie in 2022. Still, the recent trend is clear enough to make McBride a major problem for a Seattle defense that will have to put significant pressure on its linebackers and a reshuffled safety group to consistently account for him. So this isn’t a theoretical matchup. Seattle has already seen McBride put up big numbers against this defense. And that puts pressure on the linebackers and safeties. The Seahawks’ safety room has undergone significant changes heading into this season, and those depth concerns became even more important when Ty Okada missed the opener with a hamstring injury and Nick Emmanwori was also inactive. With Bud Clark already lost for the season , Seattle entered Week 1 without three players who could have been important pieces in the back end. That matters against a player like McBride because the defense can’t simply assign one player to follow him around the field. Arizona can move McBride around the formation, create matchups against linebackers and use motion to force the defense to communicate after the snap. If…

summary: The San Francisco 49ers play both their first game in Levi’s Stadium and their first game in North America for 2026 in Week 2. The 49ers have returned from Australia, where they beat the Los Angeles Rams, and jet lag is always a question, but it seems like the team has adjusted for Sunday’s game. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 22: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on before the play during the second quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on December 22, 2024 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers play both their first game in Levi’s Stadium and their first game in North America for 2026 in Week 2. The 49ers have returned from Australia, where they beat the Los Angeles Rams, and jet lag is always a question, but it seems like the team has adjusted for Sunday’s game. This will be an afternoon game with Kevin Kugler on play-by-play and Daryl Johnston providing color. Week 1 could not have gone any better for the 49ers. They went to the aforementioned Australia game and beat the Rams 27-7. It was a dominant 49ers performance and another great game for quarterback Brock Purdy. It wasn’t without some setbacks; wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling left the game and will be out for an extended period to have surgery, and tight end Jacob Tonges is out for the season. Besides those two, the 49ers are relatively healthy going into Week 2. Hopefully they can get through this game without any carts coming to the field. The Dolphins aren’t positioned for anything grand in 2026. They’ve had a lot of churn in the offseason, some of the more notable moves being firing head coach Mike McDaniel and releasing quarterback Tua Tagovailoa. In the head coach’s seat is Jeff Hafley, former defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers. 49ers fans may remember Hafley as the team’s defensive backs coach from 2016 to 2018. For quarterback, the Dolphins signed Malik Willis in the offseason. Week 1 was rough, with a 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Willis, in his first start as the Dolphins’ quarterback, went 15-of-27 for 220 yards passing, one rushing touchdown, an interception, a fumble, and took five sacks. The Dolphins’ rushing attack was equally disappointing, putting up just 74 yards total across 18 carries. The Dolphins’ defense had a bit better day than the offense. While they recorded zero sacks, the secondary was decent, getting two interceptions and limiting Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins to 160 total yards passing. The 49ers had a slight scare with kicker Eddie Pineiro not kicking due to an illness, but it’s been confirmed he will be playing . Running back Kaelon Black was also questionable , but it looks like he will be playing. The Dolphins will be without EDGE Chop Robinson and inside linebacker Ronnie Harrison—both listed as out. The 49ers are favored by nearly two touchdowns in this game. After what they showed us last week against the Rams, how they beat the Dolphins will be a discussion point rather than “if”. If the Dolphins can pull the upset or keep it within three points at the end of the game, that will not be a fun talking point on Monday. title: 49ers News: Game day
summary: I can’t wait to see how Connor Colby and Jake Brendel handle the Miami Dolphins defensive line, how the 49ers secondary takes care of the Dolphins offense, and whether the 49ers throttle up or down. It’s natural to let your guard down, being in their position, so we will learn a lot about this team today. […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers running back Roger Craig (33) hurdles over defenders during Super Bowl XIX, a 38-16 victory over the Miami Dolphins on January 20, 1985, at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, California. (Photo by Paul Fine/Getty Images) I can’t wait to see how Connor Colby and Jake Brendel handle the Miami Dolphins defensive line, how the 49ers secondary takes care of the Dolphins offense, and whether the 49ers throttle up or down. It’s natural to let your guard down, being in their position, so we will learn a lot about this team today. I have high expectations. They earned it with their performance ten days ago. Let’s get this win and let’s get out with minimal injuries. Go Niners! How the 49ers are readjusting after weeklong Australia trip “Perry, the team’s vice president of player health and performance, and his staff provided players with instructions on how much water to drink on the plane, how long to stay up before falling asleep and when to wake up. Right tackle Colton McKivitz said the objective was to stay up for a couple of hours (an easy enough task with so much adrenaline still pumping from the game), go to sleep in their lie-flat seats, and then wake up for the final few hours of the flight. McKivitz estimated he slept for about seven hours. Running back Christian McCaffrey said he was out for about 13 hours, which was about the same as rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton. Defensive end Nick Bosa was in the same range. “I actually felt it worse on the way back,” Bosa said. “Going out, you just kind of power through a few hours and then go to bed early and then just stay on a little earlier wake-up is what I did. And then when I came back, it’s been kind of hard to get to bed, but [Tuesday] night I got to bed nice and early.” Kawakami: Why do the 49ers suffer so many injuries? Here’s my grand unifying theory (paywall) “Shanahan and John Lynch seek out players who never want to come off the field, which is good for team spirit and fighting through tougher times but sometimes bad for the health of those players. I don’t think Shanahan and Lynch have ever told an injured player to keep going no matter what. I just believe that they seek out hardy souls who run to contact and don’t want to let down their teammates. Which happen to be character traits of players who will try to ignore more reasonable medical advice. Should Stribling have been kept off the field on Thursday after he initially hurt his ankle? Yes. But he wanted to keep going. The 49ers’ doctors allowed it; there’s always risk of worsening an injury and it’s always a judgment call. But if Stribling didn’t want to go back in, he wouldn’t have gone back in. And the 49ers have built this roster — and won a lot of games — with players who want to go back in… ….they gather hard-nosed players, they charge through practice, they play games full-tilt, and they believe that tough players sometimes can make it back into the lineup faster than anyone else expected. This stuff resonates in an NFL locker room. When you trust the players, the players trust you. Plus, sometimes it really pays off. Why else would the 49ers have brought George Kittle and Nick Bosa with them to Australia and to play in Week 1 after both had only recently returned to practice? Or how could Shanahan and Lynch know that this group of players would respond well to flying out to Australia a week early, blow out the Rams, and understand what it takes to be ready for the Dolphins on Sunday? The 49ers put a lot of trust in their players. Sometimes they put too much trust in their recovery powers; there are benefits and there are consequences for this. But the 49ers would rather keep that level of faith than players who deserve no faith at all.” Eddy Pineiro will kick for 49ers against the Dolphins “According to Matt Maiocco, the team did not sign either one, which means they’re confident Eddy Pineiro is no longer sick and will be available for Sunday’s home opener against the Miami Dolphins. Pineiro didn’t practice all week due to an illness. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Friday the team would work out kickers ahead of the game. It was unclear whether that move was preventive. Turns out, that’s exactly what happened.”

The move allowed the 49ers to promote defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster ahead of the team’s Week 2 game against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Okoronkwo was called up from the practice squad last week against the Los Angeles Rams and played in 30 percent of the defensive snaps with the team’s injury situation. He’ll likely have a similar role in Week 2, as the 49ers go with a deep rotation that included nine defensive linemen in Week 1. The 49ers also elevated wide receiver Khadarel Hodge for Week 1 with Jordan Watkins out, and he was signed to the active roster earlier this week. The 49ers are looking pretty clean on the injury report going into Week 2. They had two questionable players, kicker Eddy Piniero and running back Kaelon Black, but it’s looking like both will play. The 49ers hosted kickers Greg Joseph and Younghoe Koo for tryouts on Saturday, but didn’t sign either. Meanwhile, they didn’t elevate a running back, which heavily indicates that Black will be ready to go after being limited on Thursday and Friday with a groin injury. With Stribling out, the 49ers are probably going with five receivers in Week 2, and it could look very similar to how their Week 1 rotation played out. They had Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, Khadarel Hodge, and Jacob Cowing up last week, and Kyle Shanahan indicated that’ll be the group again on Sunday. That means former fifth-round rookie Jordan Watkins is expected to be inactive for the second straight week. That could be the way San Francisco goes until Stribling is able to return in a few months.

title: How has the jet lag impacted the 49ers this week ahead of Dolphins game?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have had a different week of preparation than usual ahead of their Week 2 game against the Miami Dolphins, as they’ve had to deal with the aftermath of their Australia travel. After their Thursday night game last week, the 49ers are back to playing on Sunday this week, and head coach […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 08: San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan and his coaching staff look on during a San Fransisco 49ers NFL media availability at AAMI Park on September 08, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have had a different week of preparation than usual ahead of their Week 2 game against the Miami Dolphins, as they’ve had to deal with the aftermath of their Australia travel. After their Thursday night game last week, the 49ers are back to playing on Sunday this week, and head coach Kyle Shanahan acknowledged it did take a few days after returning to get back to normal with the jet lag, which was the biggest challenge of the week. “The biggest challenge when we first got here was getting over the jet lag, just like it was when we went out there,” Shanahan said to NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco. “But we got the extra days to do that. We got back Friday. Saturday, Sunday was pretty rough. Monday wasn’t great. But by Tuesday we felt normal. Saw the players on Wednesday, none of them were complaining. So once the week started, I felt that was over. “And I always feel whether it’s Australia, whether it’s the Greenbrier, we go places for a week, usually once a year, but it’s always a challenge when you get back to get the focus. I think one of the benefits to being in a hotel all week, you never want to be away from your family too long and stuff like that, but when you are in a hotel, you have nowhere else to go. You get back from practice, you’re done with your meetings, and your bedroom’s upstairs. There’s no family waiting for you at home, for the players, for the coaches, so you’re all kind of just around there. So you just hunker, hover around, you talk football a little bit longer, players are around longer. There’s nothing to do but just focus exactly on that game. “And I always think when you come back, then you got your family you haven’t seen in a week, you just got other things, you go home at night, and it’s just about regaining that focus that everything is about those 3.5 hours on Sunday. And it’s something you got to work to and get ready for, but that’s what I’ve experienced the most when we’ve done it the weeks away.” With people overcoming jet lag, Shanahan did notice that things were slower earlier in the week before the team was back to normal by the start of practices on Wednesday. “I think [the team’s response] has been great,” Shanahan said. “When I saw them Monday, it was just to review some of the game and stuff meeting-wise. I thought we were dragging a little bit. But by the time that we got to Wednesday, which is the first real day, guys were great in the meetings, attentive. We’ve had 3 good days of practice and guys are ready to go.” The NFL has had international games in the past, but this has definitely been the biggest adjustment for a team, which is why we’ve seen both Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan speak up about their frustrations. The Rams, who had a much different travel schedule, looked flat in Week 1. We’ll see now how the 49ers respond as a major favorite against the Dolphins in Week 2.

title: 49ers vs. Dolphins prediction: A vintage Christian McCaffrey performance
summary: The San Francisco 49ers got the upset over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, surprising many in dominating fashion as they won 27-7 to start the season on a strong note. Now, in Week 2, they’re seen as easily the biggest favorite on the slate as they take on the Miami Dolphins. San Francisco […]
full_text: Football: San Francisco 49ers Christian McCaffrey (23) stands on the field vs Los Angeles Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground.Melbourne, Australia 9/10/2026CREDIT: Erick W. Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images/Getty Images) (Set Number: X164949) The San Francisco 49ers got the upset over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, surprising many in dominating fashion as they won 27-7 to start the season on a strong note. Now, in Week 2, they’re seen as easily the biggest favorite on the slate as they take on the Miami Dolphins. San Francisco enters the weekend as 13.5-point favorites after starting the week as a 10.5-point favorite. In the debut of new head coach Jeff Hafley and quarterback Malik Willis, the Dolphins lost 27-13 to the Las Vegas Raiders last weekend as they couldn’t get much going offensively, with De’Von Achane rushing for just 36 yards. The 49ers will be returning from Australia and won’t get the coveted extra day of rest that the Rams are getting by playing Monday night. But there’s a significant level of confidence in San Francisco heading into Sunday. Is this a letdown opportunity? Will the 49ers dominate again in Week 2? Here are three predictions for the 49ers against the Dolphins. Kyle Shanahan has a vintage rushing game In the early years of the Shanahan era, the 49ers loved to establish their run game, looking to hit that coveted 40-rush total as they dominated on the ground and at the line of scrimmage. However, with Brock Purdy at the helm, San Francisco has had more confidence in its passing game at all levels of the field. That, paired with the 49ers’ issues rushing the ball last season, led to San Francisco relying more on Purdy and the passing game, which was both its strength (during the regular season) and its downfall (against the Seahawks defense). We saw a much different look in Week 1, as the 49ers ran all over the Rams defensive line, going for 174 yards on 30 carries. Kaelon Black and Christian McCaffrey both had over 60 yards with great efficiency, while the 49ers were still humming in the pass game. Now, they might be facing the worst defense in the NFL against a rebuilding Dolphins team. This seems like a perfect opportunity for a vintage Shanahan rushing game, especially with Black now being able to shoulder some of the load as well. The 49ers could go for 200 yards on the ground. The Raiders went for 130 yards on the ground last weekend, as Ashton Jeanty went for over 100 yards, and I think San Francisco can do better with their quality offensive line. Niners continue the turnovers Early on, the 49ers have looked aggressive on defense with Raheem Morris. Their defensive front and linebackers were up to the task against Los Angeles’s front, but their cornerbacks were also playing aggressively against Los Angeles’s elite receivers. That led to a forced fumble (by Fred Warner) and an interception (by Renardo Green), while the 49ers broke up four other passes. Miami’s group of skill position players is young and unproven. That’ll be a tall task against this San Francisco defense, and I think Morris will continue to be aggressive, which should create more opportunities for turnovers. San Francisco was in the bottom six in takeaways per game last year. I think that their hot start to 2026 continues here in Week 2. 49ers cover the spread For my game prediction of the week, after missing on the Rams last weekend, I’m taking the 49ers to cover the spread. San Francisco should be able to get explosives and sustain well on the ground, and I expect them to score 30 points in this one. Miami’s offense with the quarterback run could give San Francisco problems, but the 49ers linebackers played so well last week that I think they can force the Dolphins into a ton of tougher third-down situations where Miami has to rely on its passing game. Game script bodes well for San Francisco here, and the fact that it’s the home opener at Levi’s only adds to the intrigue for the 49ers. Give me the 49ers to win by at least two touchdowns (would’ve certainly taken the spread at 10.5), and start the season 2-0.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: How Brock Purdy’s story as the 49ers’ starting quarterback began with the Dolphins
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, and the last time they hosted the Dolphins was a turning point in 49ers history. That was when injuries thrust Brock Purdy into the starting quarterback role. Fans had seen Purdy take the field before, either in mop-up duty (Arizona Cardinals) or when the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 04: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers drops back to pass against the Miami Dolphins during the second quarter of an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on December 04, 2022 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, and the last time they hosted the Dolphins was a turning point in 49ers history. That was when injuries thrust Brock Purdy into the starting quarterback role. Fans had seen Purdy take the field before, either in mop-up duty (Arizona Cardinals) or when the game was out of reach (Kansas City Chiefs), but they hadn’t seen him when a game was in contention. Many remember the following week’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where Purdy outplayed Buccaneers quarterback Tom Brady. While it wasn’t as flashy as that game, Purdy’s entrance to the field showed one important thing: he belonged. The 49ers already lost their starting quarterback, Trey Lance, two games into the season. Jimmy Garoppolo, who the 49ers replaced Lance with to start that offseason, stepped in without a hitch and things continued. The Dolphins game began with the visitors getting a touchdown from a pass to Trent Sherfield. Garoppolo took the 49ers down the field for their first drive, leading to a field goal after a third-down sack. The sack was Garoppolo’s last play in a 49ers uniform. The next drive, Brock Purdy, a player who began as the No. 3 quarterback at the beginning of the year, was next man up under center. No one knew then, but he wasn’t giving that job back. Not to Lance, not to Garoppolo, not to anybody. On his first drive, Purdy had a few errant passes. Some analysts during the game suggested Kyle Shanahan lacked trust in calling anything sophisticated for the rookie. Regardless, he drove the 49ers down the field and hit Kyle Juszczyk for a touchdown to give the 49ers the lead. It’s a touchdown; there’s nothing bad about that, but there wasn’t anything defining either. Just the same things we’ve seen with Jimmy G. The next 49ers offensive drive ended in an interception. Purdy stared down Brandon Aiyuk, and the Dolphins defense knew where the ball was going. Rookie mistake, the last pick in the draft. It’s hard not to anticipate these mistakes. What is notable is the drive after. That’s the statement. During the two-minute drill, Purdy took the 49ers down the field (with a nice QB sneak on a fourth down) and hit George Kittle just before getting drilled. Brock Purdy uncorked this throw on 3rd and 10 in a two minute drill to keep the drive going at the end of the first half. They capped off the drive with a TD to take the lead, and never gave it back. Easy to see why Kyle likes him so much. Remarkable poise here. pic.twitter.com/RlDJuHrdZu — Brett Kollmann (@BrettKollmann) December 5, 2022 It’s not the play that says Purdy is the starting quarterback, but it is a play to show that this rookie, Mr. Irrelevant, can hang in the NFL. There wouldn’t be any more offensive touchdowns in this game. Purdy would drive the 49ers down to score three field goals to pull the 49ers further away from the Dolphins—a Dre Greenlaw fumble recovery for a touchdown sealed the game. For a season where the 49ers had playoff aspirations and Garoppolo’s fate uncertain, Purdy at least showed he could be a capable backup. His numbers following the game weren’t awful, but not necessarily special either: 25 for 37 (67 percent completion rate with a 5.7-yard average), 210 passing yards, two touchdowns, and one interception for a rating of 88.8. For a rookie playing his first game, it’s not in any way bad, but it’s not something that would put Purdy on the map. After the game, it was evident Garoppolo would be missing time (the rest of the season) with a foot injury. The 49ers were going to be Purdy’s team. It took the following week against the Buccaneers to show that Purdy wasn’t just a capable backup, but the starter of the future. While the Buccaneers game showed the 49ers had something special in Purdy, the Dolphins game showed he belonged. Rather than jitters, errant passes all game, and an opposing defense sending the cavalry to sack him, Purdy hung in the pocket every play and delivered—even when something was being delivered to him. Sunday’s game against the Dolphins marks the first time the teams have met in Levi’s Stadium since that day. They had met in 2024, but at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami. The Dolphins coming to Levi’s always serves as a reminder of the day Mr. Irrelevant became Mr. Relevant.

title: Titans vs. Eagles preview: 5 questions with Bleeding Green Nation
summary: Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation was nice enough to answer 5 questions about his Philadelphia Eagles ahead of tomorrow’s matchup. I did the same for him, and you can read his questions with my answers here. I long for the day when I can answer the opposing team’s questions with some confidence in the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 11: A.J. Brown #11 of the Philadelphia Eagles pumps up the crowd before the NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation was nice enough to answer 5 questions about his Philadelphia Eagles ahead of tomorrow’s matchup. I did the same for him, and you can read his questions with my answers here . I long for the day when I can answer the opposing team’s questions with some confidence in the Tennessee Titans. That day is not today. Here are my questions with his answers: 1 – The Titans franchise went into the tank the night they traded A.J. Brown to the Eagles. Summarize his time with the Eagles from your perspective. Why was it necessary to trade him this offseason? Including the playoffs, the Eagles were 56-20 during A.J. Brown’s Philly tenure. They went to two Super Bowls and won one. He was a big part of the most successful era in modern franchise history. For that, I’ll always think of him fondly. He was pretty fun to watch! Of course, the 2025 season left Eagles fans with a sour taste in their mouths. Brown clearly didn’t put his best foot forward last year. He looked really disillusioned and disinterested while being frustrated with the Eagles’ offensive struggles. We can’t act like he was totally crazy to feel that; plenty of Eagles fans were similarly annoyed with the team’s offensive incompetence. But Brown didn’t express those feelings in the most constructive manner. It reached the point where it was hard to envision him being fully motivated as a member of the Eagles. His once close relationship with Jalen Hurts deteriorated. Trading Brown away wasn’t ideal. The Eagles got worse at receiver by moving on from him. But keeping him didn’t seem like a tenable situation. And that’s a shame because Brown looked pretty good to me when I saw him practice against the Eagles in Foxboro this summer. I don’t buy the idea that he’s in rapid decline. Unfortunately for him, he’s now dealing with an injury that will cause him to miss time and perhaps negatively impact him over the course of the entire 2026 season. We’ll see on that front. The Eagles, meanwhile, will look forward to the 2027 fifth-round pick and 2028 first-round pick they received from the New England Patriots in exchange for Brown. 2 – Who fills in for Landon Dickerson? How big of a loss is his injury for the Eagles’ offensive line? Should I be like the Eagles and try to obfuscate here? Competitive advantage in the SB Nation blog Q&A exchange?! Nah. That would be silly. As silly as the team trying to hide their seemingly obvious intentions? Who can say for sure. Sure seems to me like Drew Kendall will be the guy. He was the first-team left guard whenever Dickerson missed reps or sat out of practice in training camp. Dating back to the NFL Combine, there was word that the Eagles were internally high on Kendall, a 2025 fifth-round pick. He then looked good in their preseason games this summer. Alternatively, there’s been some buzz about the Eagles moving starting center Cam Jurgens to left guard and putting Kendall in at center. That could make sense for the perspective that Kendall only played the pivot in college and thus lacks extensive guard experience. But then there’s the matter of Jurgens lacking experience at left guard; he previously played right guard in 2023. The Eagles showed a look with veteran swing tackle Fred Johnson, who played some guard earlier in his career, during practice this week. I’d be surprised if he’s the Dickerson replacement since he didn’t play well this summer and he hasn’t played guard in a long time. Wee Willie Lampkin is also potentially a factor in this equation. Ultimately, though, I’m leaning Kendall until I see otherwise. Losing Dickerson isn’t a big deal in terms of the player that he was in Week 1. It looked like he couldn’t move out there. He admitted that he was a “complete liability” against the Washington Commanders. By virtue of him struggling so much, his replacement should be an automatic upgrade, even if they’re not actually all that great. 3 – As you know, the Eagles and Titans don’t play very often. Who are some of the under-the-radar players that we should keep an eye out for? Offense: Dontayvion Wicks. He’s only played one career game against the Titans, which came early in 2024 as a member of the Green Bay Packers. Wicks saw two targets for zero catches in that one. I’d expect him to be more noticeable this time around. Wicks logged the longest reception of his career last week in a win over Washington. With the Titans likely to try to key in on stopping DeVonta Smith, Wicks should get some opportunities to win his matchups. His route-running savvy allows him to get open for Jalen Hurts, who has already developed solid chemistry with his new target. Defense: Jalyx Hunt. The 2024 third-round pick had a stellar summer for the Eagles. He wasn’t very active in the traditional box score in Week 1 but Pro Football Focus charted him with four pressures. Whereas the Eagles had to respect Jayden Daniels’ mobility in Week 1, I think their pass rush will be able to attack Cam Ward more aggressively this weekend. I could see Hunt having a big game while going up against Dan Moore at left tackle. Real deep cut: my guy Darius Cooper, who deserves more offensive playing time than he saw in Week 1. Cooper logged four special teams tackles against the Commanders. 4 – If the Eagles could steal one player from the Titans’ roster, who would it be and why? The Eagles are already strong at defensive tackle but Jalen Carter is now dealing with a wrist injury that’s causing him to wear a cast. And the Eagles are relying on him to play a lot of snaps. I’d steal Jeffery Simmons and strengthen the DT rotation. The combination of Simmons, Carter, Jordan Davis, and Moro Ojomo would be really nice. Opposing offensive lines would hate facing that group. Honorable mentions: Peter Skoronski could step in to fill the hole at left guard. I thought about Calvin Ridley or Carnell Tate since I’m not sure what to make of Makai Lemon as WR3 just yet. 5- What’s the biggest matchup in the Eagles’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? Biggest matchup in the Eagles’ favor: Philly’s defensive front going up against the Titans’ offensive line and Cam Ward. The Eagles generated pressure on 19 of Jayden Daniels’ 38 dropbacks in Week 1. Was their pass rush perfect? Hardly. They logged just one sack and two quarterback hits. But I’m willing to believe that the rush was accounting for Daniels’ mobility; the Eagles did keep his rushing production in check. Vic Fangio’s defense should be able to have more success attacking Ward. Biggest matchup in the Titans’ favor: Jeffery Simmons against the Eagles’ interior offensive line. The Birds will be starting a backup at left guard and it’s not like Cam Jurgens, who struggled last year, was lighting the world on fire. Tyler Steen is a solid starter at right guard but not a Pro Bowler. Simmons having a big game should work towards preventing the Eagles’ offense finding a rhythm. Which is something they certainly didn’t have in Week 1 when they gained just 10 first downs, second-fewest in the league. 6 – Who wins this game and why? With the Titans currently listed as 7-point home underdogs, what’s your score prediction? The Eagles will win this game and cover. I feel good about Fangio’s defense being able to cause problems for Ward and a Titans offense that struggled against the New York Jets last weekend. I don’t feel amazing about the Eagles’ offense as a collective right now … but I do feel encouraged by what I saw from Jalen Hurts against the Commanders. He might be able to make some big plays that end up being the difference in this game, just like he did against Washington. The Eagles come out on top in this…

He explained on “ The John Keim Report ” why Williams has a better understanding of how to get open. Keim referenced an example from Williams’ regular-season debut, the 24-22 defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 1. Williams “sold the go route and then he crosses them out to the outside. Now, he would have been open except the ball was out, but I liked the route. You do that time and time again. You get you’re gonna get more chances.” This subtle agility running a route was contrasted with what Keim used to see from Dotson. Keim explained, “I used to say that about Jahan Dotson when he was a rookie and then he just plateaued. He could never really get off the line. That was a big problem. I think Antonio Williams is better at getting off the line for sure.” Williams certainly proved adept at quickly escaping coverage out of his breaks, during a performance that earned him high grades , as well as a league-wide award . The 22-year-old is already trending upwards, in the opposite direction to Dotson. That wasn’t to be, but Payne was a bright spot. He’ll need to bring that consistency into Dallas this weekend. Payne could have a considerable impact on the proceedings at AT&T Stadium. The Cowboys are missing interior offensive lineman Tyler Smith , which weakens the left guard position. This won’t have gone unnoticed by defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, and the former Alabama standout has the physical tools to attack this area to make Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott uncomfortable. Operating in a 3-4 base defensive system seems to suit Payne. It gives him a little extra space to do damage as an end rather than trying to clog up lanes at tackle. He might be a seasoned veteran by this point, but he remains explosive off the snap. Once he gains early leverage, few guards in the league can deal with him. It will take much more than Payne, of course. But if he can set the tone inside, it will spread throughout the defense. title: Five Washington Commanders key to beating Dallas Cowboys in Week 2
summary: The Commanders and Cowboys face off on Sunday afternoon. For the (checks notes) 133rd time. Rarely do these matchups come so early in the season.   Honestly, it’s kind of a bummer that the first contest falls in Week 2, but the Commanders were dealt this hand and simply must play it well. They can’t […]
full_text: The Commanders and Cowboys face off on Sunday afternoon. For the (checks notes) 133rd time . Rarely do these matchups come so early in the season. Honestly, it’s kind of a bummer that the first contest falls in Week 2, but the Commanders were dealt this hand and simply must play it well. They can’t lose their second straight NFC East game in as many weeks. That would create a huge hole with lots of digging required to get out. That’s why the Commanders must play well and come away with a victory in Week 2. An 0-2 record is no fun. An 0-2 division record is even worse . They’ll need excellence from several key players to leave Dallas with a win. Here are five (not named Jayden Daniels) that must show up big for Washington: WR Terry McLaurin The veteran No. 1 receiver wasn’t a big part of Washington’s offense against Philadelphia. He wasn’t targeted until the fourth quarter, as the Eagles did a bunch to take him away. Washington still went to him in key moments late in that game, but he rolled with the punches like a veteran should. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin on not getting frustrated when he doesn't get the ball — as was the case Sunday against the Eagles pic.twitter.com/9LxKzMivR9 — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) September 17, 2026 Still, designing plays to get him involved early on Sunday could assist with McLaurin finding a required early flow. There should be room for him to work within the suspect Dallas secondary, and that connection he and quarterback Jayden Daniels refined all spring and summer must show up in important, explosive moments. It’s hard to keep McLaurin down. Seems borderline impossible in consecutive weeks. RB Bill Croskey-Merritt The team’s top running back led the Commanders with 63 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. While there were some hard runs in there, it’s still just 3.9 yards per clip . He’s got to be more efficient running the football in a zone scheme that suits him, but that’s not the most important thing. Hold onto the freaking ball. Croskey-Merritt got the ball punched out with roughly four minutes left in the fourth quarterback. That simply can’t happen. The Commanders acknowledged that point with actions, putting Kaytron Allen in the mix on that key comeback attempt. That was a shot across the bow if there ever was one. “Yeah, I think the ball security,” Quinn said, “that’s definitely the premium for us.” Croskey-Merritt must act like a feature back on Sunday, holding onto the ball while being a steadily productive force. If not, snaps may start going to others. LB Leo Chenal The Commanders will play Sunday without captain and green-dot wearer Frankie Luvu. That means Leo Chenal will step in and take most every snap next to Sonny Styles. Washington paid him handsomely to be a key defensive component. Chenal was more of a key reserve and roving chess piece in Kansas City, but he must be an every-down, stabilizing force in this one. There’s no second option with Jordan Magee on injured reserve, so Chenal has to be good in coverage, a stout run defender while shutting down plays before they turn explosive. That doesn’t sound super glamorous, but it’s a required job with Luvu unavailable. EDGE Dorance Armstrong The Commanders pass rush got off to a relatively strong start in Week 1, with impactful play when blitzing or applying a four-man rush. Now Washington adds Dorance Armstrong to the mix upon his reinstatement from a one-game suspension. Armstrong’s return from suspension and an ACL tear that cut an excellent start to the 2025 campaign short comes in Dallas, where the Texas native got hurt . It’s a full-circle moment to be sure, and he joins Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson as edge rushers. Quinn not-so-subtly hinted at the fact Armstrong could join those two in a personnel package that has all of them rushing the passer at once. Armstrong can bring it from the interior, too, and should make the Commanders four-man rush super dangerous. CB Mike Sainristil Have you reached Mikey fatigue at this point? The cornerback’s Week 1 gaffes have been rehashed and written about a ton in recent days, to the point its put-up-or-shut-up time. There isn’t much more to say other than that he’s got to play better, and has a tough task ahead against the Cowboys receivers. Commanders fans should keep an eye on his play and his usage in this one, to see if Washington’s staff sticks with Sainristil or decreases his snaps some. He’ll still be involved in that game in some capacity, and simply can’t give up the explosives that proved so costly in Week 1.

title: Antonio Williams and Tyler Owens spark fan excitement – survey results
summary: Despite starting the 2026 NFL season with a tough 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, the mood around the Washington Commanders fan base is remarkably positive. While standard logic would suggest a divisional loss would cause panic, this week’s Hogs Haven Reacts survey reveals a fan base that is more optimistic than it was before […]
full_text: Despite starting the 2026 NFL season with a tough 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, the mood around the Washington Commanders fan base is remarkably positive. While standard logic would suggest a divisional loss would cause panic, this week’s Hogs Haven Reacts survey reveals a fan base that is more optimistic than it was before the Week 1 kickoff. The 13% confidence surge As is true in every week of the season (until early December, at least), in each of the first two weeks, Hogs Haven readers were asked if they are confident that the Commanders are headed in the right direction. Remarkably, 83% of respondents voted “yes” this week; a significant 13% increase from the 70% confidence rating recorded just prior to the start of the season. Why the increased confidence after a loss? The answer lies in how competitive and disciplined the team looked against an elite division rival. A resilient, upgraded defense: Under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, the defense showed immediate teeth. They brought intense pressure up front, forcing Philadelphia to punt seven times. While there were defensive breakdowns that yielded explosive plays in both the run and pass game, the overall performance offered evidence that Washington’s front-7 will challenge opponents and that, despite some continuing secondary concerns, the defense will no longer be the patsy it so often was under former DC Joe Whitt. 3rd & 10: Jalen Hurts gets sacked Three straight three-and-outs for the Eagles offense pic.twitter.com/aQtc2xL7cW — 𝐃𝐈𝐄-𝐇𝐀𝐑𝐃 🦅 𝐑𝐄𝐀𝐋 𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐓𝐄 (@Eaglesfans9) September 13, 2026 Jayden Daniels’ poise & protection: The health of quarterback Jayden Daniels is paramount to the team’s success. Against Philly’s highly touted defensive line, Daniels played an incredibly smart game. He protected himself from unnecessary hits while consistently manufacturing big plays as both a passer and a dangerous runner. JAYDEN DANIELS. pic.twitter.com/g6hFnxsaJj — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) September 13, 2026 Pass protection: Despite offseason anxieties regarding unit depth, Washington’s front surrendered only one sack all afternoon. Jayden’s mobility and smarts combine to help mask most deficiencies in the OL play, and Sam Cosmi, in particular, had an outstanding game against the Eagles highly-touted DL. There won’t be many tougher tests in the trenches against opponents in the ’26 regular season. BiB: I agree – Cosmi should have been on the list. Here’a a partial make up for leaving him off: Sam Cosmi had the best tape of any OL I've seen from Week 1. He put Jalen Carter in Alcatraz whenever they faced off 1v1. Stack this on top of his awesome performances vs. him in 2024 as well. ELITE. pic.twitter.com/C2pspIo52Z — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 14, 2026 The second-half adaptation: Another massive confidence builder was the coaching staff’s ability to adjust. David Blough’s offense had a noticeably slow start, but the team didn’t fold. Daniels and the unit completely lit up the fourth quarter, orchestrating a furious comeback by scoring touchdowns on both possessions in the final stanza, but ultimately falling a two-point conversion short of tying the game with a minute on the clock. Seeing an offense adapt and thrive late in the game signals potential improvement in the coming weeks and into the remainder of the 2026 campaign. Jayden Daniels in the 4th Quarter yesterday: – 9/11 – 99 pass yds – 2 TDS Delivered in the clutch just came up short pic.twitter.com/BLAkdX1CO6 — Commanders on Real (@WSHOnReal) September 14, 2026 The rookie standout The second survey question asked fans to name the player, from among six choices, who put together the best overall game against the Eagles. Rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams dominated the voting, capturing 52% of the total. Veteran safety Nick Cross followed with 25%, and rookie linebacker Sonny Styles pulled in 20%. Visit our partners at FanDuel Williams put on an absolute clinic in his first-ever NFL game that was surprising to some fans, but not to all. He was incredibly efficient, turning 4 targets into 4 receptions for 64 yards and a crucial touchdown. His separation speed and reliable hands gave Daniels a trusted go-to option when the pressure mounted. Antonio Williams darkhorse OROY candidate. As a true freshman he played 93% from slot. With McLaurin and Diggs aging and on outside, the future is AW. pic.twitter.com/YtEnxQtq3s — Elite Drafters (@Elite_Drafters) September 14, 2026 This stellar debut did not go unnoticed nationally, earning him the fan-voted Pepsi Rookie of the Week award . He becomes the 5 th Commanders rookie to win the award since the start of the 2024 season. The viral sceptre: Tyler Owens explodes onto the scene While the survey focused on six nominated players, special teams ace Tyler Owens was left off the ballot—though his performance strongly dictates he should have been there. Owens put on an absolute masterclass in third-phase football, executing two beautiful special teams plays that turned heads across the league. Tyler Owens had two incredible special-teams plays last night. The one that went viral was the second. Here's the first: pic.twitter.com/k4AHvfXO2j — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) September 14, 2026 One of his thunderous hits went completely viral on social media immediately following the game. On NFL Network’s Good Morning Football , host Kyle Brandt went as far as breaking his own segment rules, choosing a special teams gunner to win the award of the Week 1 “Angry Runs” sceptre. The media attention Owens garnered this week highlighted the kind of special teams prowess t hat has been a hallmark of Commanders football ever since ST coordinator Larry Izzo was hired by Dan Quinn in 2024. Looking ahead to Sunday in Dallas The division’s collective fan confidence metrics as measured by SB Nation’s Reacts surveys reflect wildly different reactions to the opening week across the NFC East, driven largely by the preseason expectations of each fan base. Confidence New York Giants: 99% Washington Commanders: 83% Philadelphia Eagles: 70% Dallas Cowboys: 19% The Cowboys’ fan base plummeted to a dismal 19% after they were thoroughly handled by the Giants in Week 1. This sets up a highly urgent, high-stakes Week 2 battle between two old rivals, each desperate to avoid a dangerous 0-2 start to the season. Details of today’s game The Commanders travel to Texas to face the Dallas Cowboys today, Sunday, September 20, 2026 The Cowboys are favored by 4.5 points , and the over/under per FanDuel is set at 50.5 points Kickoff is officially scheduled for 4:25 PM EDT If Washington can replicate its Week 1 grit while cleaning up a few defensive breakdowns, the Commanders have a prime opportunity to push Dallas deeper into panic mode. full_text: Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs was fined for a post-touchdown celebration where he score and then jumped onto the goalpost padding. Per The Athletic’s Nick Jhabvala , Diggs was fined $14,926 for the infraction, which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Commanders WR Stefon Diggs was fined $14,926 for jumping on the goalpost after his TD vs. the Eagles. — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) September 19, 2026 In stead of explaining, it looked like this. The NFL fined Commanders WR Stefon Diggs $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct (illegal celebrations and vulgar acts) — jumping onto the goalpost after his TD last week against the Eagles. Diggs was penalized and now a fine on top of it. pic.twitter.com/JyWafraEiT — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 19, 2026 It was a major mistake. The Commanders were down by two points at that relatively early point in the fourth quarter, and the penalty erased the prospect of going for a 2-point conversion. Afterward head coach Dan Quinn said the Commanders would’ve gone for two had Diggs not drawn a flag. The Commanders kicked an extra point there, gave up a touchdown and ended up trailing by eight points again. They scored a late touchdown, but failed at their pressure-packed 2-point conversion at the end of the game and ultimately lost 24-22 to Philadelphia . Diggs was accountable for the mistake in the aftermath, realizing the gravity of his mistake, which cost him some money, too. Stefon Diggs addressed his teammates about his penalty following the Commanders loss to the Eagles. Diggs said he just wants to win. pic.twitter.com/a8jjDZEVqR — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) September 16, 2026

title: Four Commanders players Washington should use more vs. Dallas Cowboys
summary: The Commanders lost their regular season opener, but there were bright spots within the final 24-22 result. This initial salvo also showed how many of the new faces brought in via free agency and the draft fit in with Washington’s grand plan.   There were also some major issues that led to the loss, with […]
full_text: The Commanders lost their regular season opener, but there were bright spots within the final 24-22 result . This initial salvo also showed how many of the new faces brought in via free agency and the draft fit in with Washington’s grand plan. There were also some major issues that led to the loss, with some obvious weak spots in the lineup. Making mistakes in one game shouldn’t cause a player to lose a starting spot or cause a coaching staff to overreact, but it’s valid to wonder if some personnel swaps might lead to better results. Now, be wary of such swaps. Let’s call it the backup quarterback theory. The No. 2 signal caller is everyone’s favorite when the starter struggles despite never playing a significant role. A starter becomes a starter over time. A backup earns his role, too. In sum, different isn’t always better. That said, the Commanders could make some alterations with the depth available that could prove beneficial. Here are a few Commanders players who should play a bigger role on Sunday afternoon versus the Cowboys: CB Rasul Douglas Rasul Douglas played 17 defensive snaps at cornerback against the Eagles, while Mike Saintisril and Amik Robertson played all but one combined. Douglas was the third cornerback in that instance, but there are reasons why it might be smart to move him to No. 2 against the Cowboys. First, there’s Douglas’ 6-foot-2, 192-pound frame. Then there’s his adept play in zone and his penchant for taking the ball away. That may be beneficial against Dallas, a team featuring larger receivers in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Then we’ve got the Sainristil problem , after the far shorter cornerback inexplicably allowed an explosive play down the sideline and an easy touchdown for Philadelphia. Both plays have drawn heavy criticism and simply can’t happen again. Starting Douglas while using Sainristil almost exclusively in the slot might help the secondary overall. The Commanders could use a third safety in those instances if Sainristil makes another big mistake. WR Antonio Williams This falls under the “well, duh” category. Third-round rookie receiver Antonio Williams had four receptions for 64 yards and a touchdowns on 10 routes run. Yeah, you read that right. Williams earned rookie of the week honors for his exploits and will certainly get more opportunities and targets against the Cowboys, as a third receiver, both aligned wide and in the slot. He has earned more snaps and targets. Expect them to be built into the game plan. TE Ben Sinnott This one will happen naturally with Chig Okonkwo out with a groin injury . John Bates will be the top tight end on Sunday, and is always the best blocking tight end on the field. Sinnott’s a player who has talent and upside in there somewhere. While the instinct may be to play fewer multiple tight end sets or use more receivers, giving Sinnott some targets could prove beneficial to him and the offensive unpredictability when do-it-all tight ends are involved. NOTE: So I wrote everything above about Sinnott before I read a whole comment thread about how much you don’t think he’s very good. I’m not talking 40 snaps here. I’m talking 30 productive snaps and 10 as an in-line route runner. Let’s see what he can do. S Quan Martin This one scares me, even though Jeremy Reaves wasn’t superlative against the Eagles. Also, listening to Dan Quinn talk about Reaves and his communication and leadership, it sure seems like his defensive role is secure right now. Martin was simply not good last year but had a good camp. Maybe he finds time in the slot or can be an option playing deep next to Nick Cross. Still, though, it’s an option in a pinch.

Commanders links Articles Blogging the Boys 5 Questions with Hogs Haven: Cowboys want a better defense, but the Commanders might have got one Blogging The Boys: What were some of the best things that you saw from the Commanders in the first game versus Philadelphia that bode well for the season? Hogs Haven: I think the first thing almost any Commanders fan would say is the performance of the defense. Last year, the Commanders had one of the worst defenses in the NFL, so they completely overhauled it in the offseason, with a new DC in Daronte Jones (who brings an attacking Flores-like scheme) and replacing over half of the starters on defense. Early returns indicate the overhaul has paid off. The defense was living in the Eagles backfield last Sunday, generating a 48.48% pressure rate on Jalen Hurts and a 24% TFL rate, both notably higher than NFL average. BTB: Give us a rundown on a few of the new players in Washington who could make a big impact this season. On defense, as mentioned before, over half the defensive starters this year are new to the team. I won’t go through all of them, but the standouts are LB Sonny Styles, S Nick Cross, and EDGE Odafe Oweh.Styles was drafted 7th overall and has lived up to his billing. He was all over the field on Sunday making plays and even steamrolled Saquon Barkley to get a big hit on Jalen Hurts on a blitz. Nick Cross was a physical presence flying all over the field, showing well in coverage while also getting tackles and limiting yardage to the line of scrimmage. Odafe Oweh was the team’s biggest FA signing with a 4-year, $96 million contract. He didn’t have a huge impact in week 1 against the Eagles elite OTs, ending the game with 1 sack, 3 total tackles and a tackle for loss. I would also be remiss if I didn’t mention standout gunner Tyler Owens, who was a maven on special teams and had an angry run that went viral after the game. Recording one sack and two tackles for loss, Styles’ elite physicality and dominance were on full display. Will Campbell’s rookie pressure rate Styles still has some work to do when dropping back into coverage. During Dallas Goedert’s 43-yard touchdown reception , Styles had some difficulty communicating during pre-snap movements, allowing for Goedert to slip by unmarked. Sports Illustrated Washington May Need Treylon Burks One Week After Making Him Inactive Treylon Burks was among the five players on the 53-man active roster who did not dress against the Philadelphia Eagles, as the team dressed four tight ends and five wide receivers instead . What made the inactive status odd was that Burks was featured among the starters in the Week 1 depth chart. Now with TE Chig Okonkwo out this week , the roster math has shifted completely. While he is not a tight end, Burks brings his 6-foot-2, 225-pound frame with him every snap, works well over the middle, and has a bigger catch radius than most of Washington’s receiving room. Quinn talked about those traits during camp: “But at the Z position, we really feel his impact, you know? Deep routes, in-breaking routes, he’s got a long catch radius, and so that’s the thing that you feel on a regular basis.” Ben Sinnott is another player the team would like to see step into a larger role with Okonkwo out. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Commanders secondary faces a test against Cowboys wide receivers The Cowboys are coming off a rough offensive showing after amassing just 244 yards of total offense against the New York Giants in the start of the John Harbaugh era. The Sunday night showing marked the fewest yards gained since week nine during the Cowboys’ 2024 season, giving Dallas fuel to turn the tide in their home opener. Both Ceedee Lamb and George Pickens combined to register 43 catches of at least 20 yards in 2025 as the duo ranked among the top 14 across the NFL in the category last season. Yet they will also look to turn the page after combining for six drops and 72 yards while Lamb found the endzone for Dallas’ first touchdown of the season. Add in the fact that the Cowboys had just two possessions through the second half, how defensive coordinator Daronte Jones and the Commanders’ defense can extend the Cowboys’ slowly developing passing attack again may be the biggest question mark . Both Pickens and Lamb recorded at least four receptions and 45 yards each in both of the meetings in 2025, and it’s a debate whether the unit is upgraded one season later. With Amos sidelined for at least another three weeks and uncertainty whether he’ll be available in week five, Rasul Douglas, who Daronte Jones called a “savvy vet,” has been able to step into an impact role with Amik Robertson and Mike Sainristil rounding out the top of the room. Though Douglas allowed a 31 yard completion on third down, the veteran showed why he can at least be a stopgap at the position. Yet the test goes beyond Douglas with Sainristil looking to bounceback as Jones pointed to “urgency” from his third year cornerback. Dallas failed to get much pressure on Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and, unlike the Philadelphia Eagles, only generated two pressures on four-man rushes during the evening. Blough should have plenty of opportunities to get his offense on the right track, as the Cowboys’ defense also lost safety Malik Hooker and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown to injuries this week. Conversely, Washington’s defense looked vastly improved under Daronte Jones’ direction, but failed to limit the Philadelphia’s explosive playmaking ability, giving up 171 of the Eagles’ 318 total yards on just four plays. The secondary in particular struggled. Dallas’ two big wide receivers George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb will be going against last week’s starters, Amik Robertson and Mike Sainristil, making this a matchup to watch. title: NFL Week 2 uniforms: Rams debut 'Classic Sol,' Ravens go all-white
summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 2, led by a new alternate look from the Los Angeles Rams.
full_text:
Uniforms revealed in the offseason will make their respective debuts in Week 2. Fresh from their trip Down Under, the Los Angeles Rams look to win their first game of the season with a design rooted in its history.

 

 Los Angeles will wear its "Classic Sol" alternate threads against the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football." The uniform honors the Rams' championship in 1951, with this season marking the 75th anniversary. A sol-colored jersey includes royal blue stitched and colored numbers. The three-stripe royal blue sleeve design is a direct nod to the uniforms worn in the 1951 season. The Giants will counter by going all-white.

 The Baltimore Ravens underwent  a closet redesign in the offseason , and with it came a new helmet and combination. Nicknamed "White Noise," Baltimore will pair all-white threads with the "Purple Rising" helmet against the New Orleans Saints . Baltimore originally revealed the purple lids in 2024, but tweaked them in April with a logo change, maintaining the metallic purple. It tops off a sleek new all-white look. 

 It's an all-white look for the New York Jets as well, but from head-to-toe. New York unveiled new white helmets in July that differ from the throwback ones it typically wears with its classic uniforms. The Jets will pair it together with all-white jerseys and pants against the Green Bay Packers , who will wear their traditional home green on the road.

 In the NFL "Rivalries" space, the Arizona Cardinals are the first to wear their design this season. Revealed last year, Arizona will rock it versus the Seattle Seahawks -- the same team they debuted it against in the previous campaign.

full_text:
Week 2 of the  2026 NFL season is off to an exciting start, as the Bills defeated the Lions 41-31 in the first game at Highmark Stadium . But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projected out stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen suggests three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Could the Bengals upset the Texans? Will we see big receiving days for the Dolphins' Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas ? Can Eagles running back Saquon Barkley find the end zone? And is it finally time for the Jets to snag an interception? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Jacksonville Jaguars +2.5 at Denver Broncos (+124) 

 Denver's offense hasn't shown enough to justify laying points. The Broncos produced only 176 yards and 3.7 yards per play in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, with quarterback  Bo Nix turning it over twice. Jacksonville is bringing a pass rush that generated five sacks against Cleveland, while QB  Trevor Lawrence  threw four touchdown passes. Defense makes the Broncos the favorite, but the Jaguars have the more trustworthy offense to win outright.

 
 

 

 Cincinnati Bengals +2.5   at Houston Texans  (+120) 

 The Bengals' biggest weakness looked better against the Bucs , as quarterback  Joe Burrow was sacked only once. If that holds, he gets a Houston defense that just allowed 10.4 yards per pass to Buffalo in Week 1 . Houston can obviously pressure Burrow, but if Cincinnati's offensive line continues to improve, it should have enough through the air with  Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins .

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Rhamondre Stevenson , RB, New England Patriots : 16 carries, 63 rushing yards; 5 receptions, 42 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown

 Since 2023, running backs catch passes on 8% of dropbacks against man coverage but 15%  against zone coverage. Why does that matter here? Because in Week 1  against the Falcons, the Steelers ran zone coverage 89% of the time under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. So I expect Stevenson to have a big day in the receiving game.

 And while I don't expect the Patriots will be as run-heavy as they were in Week 1  -- which certainly didn't work out for them! -- New England should be ahead by enough early to run the ball late in the game. All in all, it should be a healthy workload for Stevenson.

 
 

 Riq Woolen , CB, Philadelphia Eagles : 34 coverage snaps, 1 reception allowed for 7 yards on four targets, 1 interception

 Woolen had a strong Week 1 against the Commanders, allowing just one reception for 1 yard. Granted, that one reception was a touchdown to WR  Stefon Diggs , but I'm not sure that play was entirely on him. Either way, it was a strong game for Woolen, who also scored highly in my cornerback metric . Now, he gets to face second-year Titans QB  Cam Ward , who struggled against the Jets in Week 1 . Woolen should have the advantage against  Carnell Tate , Calvin Ridley or Elic Ayomanor .

 
 

 Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins : 7 receptions, 77 receiving yards, 1 touchdown

 Washington ran a route on 84% of Miami's dropbacks in Week 1 , the highest rate on the Dolphins. He was also targeted eight times but had just three receptions. His 99 incomplete air yards was tied for second among all players, a number that indicates some positive regression could be coming in Week 2.

 The Dolphins threw a little more than expected versus the Raiders, and they'll have to pass plenty against the 49ers since this looks likely to be a blowout loss. Washington, who frequently plays out of the slot, historically runs shorter routes and could be an option underneath in garbage time.

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Jordan Love , QB, Green Bay Packers (rostered in 43.9% of ESPN leagues) 

 Love threw for 387 yards in Week 1 against the Vikings, the second-highest total of his career, and scored 19.4 fantasy points on 42 pass attempts. Green Bay struggled to run the ball without Josh Jacobs , and its offensive line will still be banged up in Week 2 against the Jets. But with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 48.2 fantasy points last week, Love should be an appealing streaming option.

 

 
 

 Caleb Douglas , WR, Miami Dolphins (34.9%) 

 Douglas caught five of seven targets for 94 yards, scoring 14.4 fantasy points in his NFL debut against the Raiders. He played more than 90% of Miami's offensive snaps and led all rookies in targets, receptions and receiving yards. The Dolphins enter Week 2 as double-digit underdogs against the 49ers , so Douglas could benefit from a pass-heavy game script.

 
 

 Mack Hollins , WR, New England Patriots (5.2%) 

 Hollins outsnapped Romeo Doubs in the first half against the Seahawks in Week 1 , and he led the Patriots receivers in snaps after A.J. Brown exited with an ankle injury. Hollins should continue to see significant playing time against Pittsburgh now that Brown is on injured reserve .

 Holins received at least six targets in four games last season, averaging 12.8 fantasy points in those contests. He finished with five targets and 9.1 fantasy points in Week 1.

 

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Derrick Henry , RB, Baltimore Ravens 

 Henry rushed for three touchdowns in the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts -- including two on carries inside the 5-yard line. Under new coordinator Declan Doyle, the Ravens used schemed zone concepts and creative tight end movement to put Henry on a north/south track. That should work versus a Saints defense that allowed two rushing scores in New Orleans'  Week 1 loss to the Lions.

 
 

 George Pickens , WR, Dallas Cowboys 

 Pickens caught just three of six targets for 28 yards in the Cowboys' Week 1 loss to the Giants, including two drops. But that doesn't mean quarterback Dak Prescott will stop going to Pickens for big plays. The vertical pass game is a key element of Dallas' offense, and it could lead Pickens into the end zone.

 

 
 

 Saquon Barkley , RB, Philadelphia Eagles 

 Barkley did have 15 carries in the Week 1 win over the Commanders, with two goal-to-go attempts, so we can bet on him seeing the ball in scoring position. Plus, he has home run ability to score from outside the red zone. Yes, the Eagles need more up front to create consistent daylight for Barkley, but he gets a matchup against a Titans defense that gave up just 152 rushing yards to the Jets.

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will lead the league in scrimmage yards 

 Jeanty led the Raiders in both rushing yards (102) and receiving yards (45) last week in the Raiders' win over the Dolphins. Without Brock Bowers  ( meniscus trim ) for another week and facing another light box defense from the Chargers , I expect Jeanty to once again thrive on the ground and in the air. Jeanty was seventh last week with 147 scrimmage yards, but his longest play was only 15 yards. With a couple home run plays on Sunday, he could knock on the door for 200.

 
 

 The Jets will get their first interception 

 The last Jets pick was on Jan. 5, 2025 -- 623 days from their matchup with the Packers on Sunday . Green Bay's pass protection is a glaring issue, and while quarterback  Jordan Love is around league-average in his interception rate, the 16 hits he took in Week 1 could have him looking to get rid of the ball faster in Week 2. I'm banking on safety Minkah Fitzpatrick to track down a deep heave and end the drought.
